kitaqgb/lib/audio.c:589

c
void __stackcall Audio_SetPanPacked(u8 packed) {
    u8 mix = 0;
    u8 pan = (u8)(packed & 3);
    if (pan == AUDIO_PAN_CENTER) mix = (u8)(mix | 0x11);
    else if (pan == AUDIO_PAN_LEFT) mix = (u8)(mix | 0x10);
    else if (pan == AUDIO_PAN_RIGHT) mix = (u8)(mix | 0x01);
    pan = (u8)((packed >> 2) & 3);
    if (pan == AUDIO_PAN_CENTER) mix = (u8)(mix | 0x22);
    else if (pan == AUDIO_PAN_LEFT) mix = (u8)(mix | 0x20);
    else if (pan == AUDIO_PAN_RIGHT) mix = (u8)(mix | 0x02);
    pan = (u8)((packed >> 4) & 3);
    if (pan == AUDIO_PAN_CENTER) mix = (u8)(mix | 0x44);
    else if (pan == AUDIO_PAN_LEFT) mix = (u8)(mix | 0x40);
    else if (pan == AUDIO_PAN_RIGHT) mix = (u8)(mix | 0x04);
    pan = (u8)((packed >> 6) & 3);
    if (pan == AUDIO_PAN_CENTER) mix = (u8)(mix | 0x88);
    else if (pan == AUDIO_PAN_LEFT) mix = (u8)(mix | 0x80);
    else if (pan == AUDIO_PAN_RIGHT) mix = (u8)(mix | 0x08);
    Audio_Pan = mix;
    Audio_UpdateNR51();
}
Audio_SetPaused

Silence on pause while preserving music/effect positions. Resume retriggers eligible CH1, CH2 and CH4 notes.

Syntax

c
void __stackcall Audio_SetPaused(u8 on);

Parameters

on

Zero disables; nonzero enables. Read this function’s description to distinguish muting from gating updates.

Return value

No return value. Changes sound registers or driver state.

Conditions and limits

Include audio_hwregs_gb.c before audio.c and call Audio_Init at startup. Call Audio_Update exactly once per frame, about 59.7 Hz. Stream reads temporarily change the ROM mapping; do not re-enter this driver from an interrupt.

This routine does not retrigger CH3. Effects continue on a later update. Direct note-on calls can still sound while paused.

    AUDIO_CMD_LOOP
};

    Audio_SetPaused(1);
    sound_wait(30);

    sound_result[1]=Audio_Paused;
    Audio_SetPaused(0);
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_result[2]=Audio_Paused;
    // Disabling suppresses note writes; the next 30 updates still consume data.
    Audio_SetMusicEnabled(0);
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_result[3]=Audio_Delay;
    sound_result[4]=Audio_MusicEnabled;
    // Explicitly stop the sounding channel while leaving the stream running.
    Audio_StopChannel(AUDIO_CHANNEL_CH1);

    Audio_SetMusicEnabled(1);
    sound_wait(30);
    Audio_StopMusic();
    sound_result[5]=Audio_PlayingMusic;
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_end();

kitaqgb/lib/audio.h:90

Declaration notes (original source)
On pause entry, silence hardware while retaining cursors. On resume, retrigger
eligible legacy CH1, CH2 and CH4 notes; CH3 is not retriggered here. Updates still
advance master fades while paused, and effect playback resumes on a later update.

kitaqgb/lib/audio.c:1010

c
void __stackcall Audio_SetPaused(u8 on) {
    if (on != 0) {
        if (Audio_Paused == 0) {
            Audio_Paused = 1;
            Audio_SilenceAll();
        }
    } else {
        if (Audio_Paused != 0) {
            Audio_Paused = 0;
            if (Audio_PlayingMusic != 0 && Audio_MusicEnabled != 0) {
                if ((Audio_LastChMask & AUDIO_RESUME_CH1) != 0 && Audio_EffectPointer == 0) {
                    Audio_Ch1NoteOn(Audio_LastCh1Note, Audio_Ch1Env, Audio_Ch1Duty);
                }
                if ((Audio_LastChMask & AUDIO_RESUME_CH2) != 0) {
                    Audio_Ch2NoteOn(Audio_LastCh2Note, Audio_Ch2Env, Audio_Ch2Duty);
                }
                if ((Audio_LastChMask & AUDIO_RESUME_CH4) != 0) {
                    Audio_Ch4NoteOn(Audio_LastCh4Param, Audio_Ch4Env);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
Audio_SetSfxEnabled

Gate effect note writes; disabling also releases the effect slots.

Syntax

c
void __stackcall Audio_SetSfxEnabled(u8 on);

Parameters

on

Zero disables; nonzero enables. Read this function’s description to distinguish muting from gating updates.

Return value

No return value. Changes sound registers or driver state.

Conditions and limits

In the ordinary configuration, effect release turns CH3 off. It silences CH1 when music is stopped, but does not automatically replay an earlier music note while music is playing. With AUDIO_VBLANK_SFX_RESTORE, release requests recovery from the ISR.

Starting while disabled can register a stream, but updates suppress its note writes. Enable effects before requesting audible playback.

Usage example

c
// Each pair lasts one update. Priority controls replacement within each slot.
#include "gb_sound_example.h"
#pragma bank 2
__prg_rom u8 effect[]={33,0xC0,33,0xC0,33,0xC0,33,0xC0,33,0xC0,33,0xC0,
    40,0xC0,40,0xC0,40,0xC0,40,0xC0,40,0xC0,40,0xC0,0};
__prg_rom u8 wave_effect[]={AUDIO_SFX_CH3_MARKER,
    33,0x20,33,0x20,33,0x20,33,0x20,33,0x20,33,0x20,
    40,0x20,40,0x20,40,0x20,40,0x20,40,0x20,40,0x20,0};
#pragma bank 0
void main() {
    sound_begin("BANKED SOUND EFFECT");
    Audio_SetMasterVolume(3,3);
    // Read the marker in bank 2 while restoring the caller's original mapping.
    Audio_PlaySFXPannedBanked(2,effect,5,AUDIO_PAN_LEFT);
    sound_result[0]=Audio_EffectPriority;
    Audio_PlaySFXBanked(2,effect,4);
    sound_result[1]=Audio_EffectPriority;
    sound_wait(30);
    Audio_PlaySFXPannedBanked(2,wave_effect,5,AUDIO_PAN_RIGHT);
    sound_result[2]=Audio_EffectPriority3;
    sound_wait(30);
    // Implicit-bank entry points capture bank 2; the service restores bank 1.
    __bankswitch(2);
    Audio_PlaySFX(effect,5);
    __bankswitch(1);
    sound_result[3]=Audio_EffectBank;
    sound_wait(30);
    __bankswitch(2);
    Audio_PlaySFXPanned(effect,5,AUDIO_PAN_RIGHT);
    __bankswitch(1);
    sound_wait(6);
    Audio_StopSfx();
    sound_result[4]=(u8)(Audio_EffectPointer==0);
    sound_wait(24);
    // Disabling effects releases current owners; re-enable before the next request.
    Audio_PlaySFXBanked(2,effect,5);
    sound_wait(6);
    Audio_SetSfxEnabled(0);
    sound_result[5]=Audio_SfxEnabled;
    sound_result[6]=(u8)(Audio_EffectPointer==0);
    sound_wait(24);
    Audio_SetSfxEnabled(1);
    Audio_PlaySFXBanked(2,effect,5);
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_result[7]=Audio_SfxEnabled;
    sound_end();
}

Expected result

Bank-2 data plays a short rising pulse on the left, a wave effect on the right and a centered pulse. Later examples stop a right pulse early, disable an effect and re-enable playback. A priority-4 request cannot replace priority 5.

Audio_StopChannel

Stop one physical voice and remove its music note from the resume mask.

Syntax

c
void __stackcall Audio_StopChannel(u8 ch);

Parameters

ch

Channel ID: 0=CH1, 1=CH2, 2=CH3, 3=CH4. Direct APIs and music streams use the same IDs.

Return value

No return value. Changes sound registers or driver state.

Conditions and limits

CH1/CH3 also clear their effect slot. Values outside 0..3 do nothing. VBlank latched notes are managed separately.

Usage example

c
// Four isolated voices, each lasting 30 frames, separated by 15 silent frames.
#include "gb_sound_example.h"
void main() {
    sound_begin("FOUR SOUND CHANNELS");
    Audio_SetMasterVolume(3,3);
    // CH1: A4, 50% duty, fixed envelope volume 12.
    Audio_SetCh1Duty(2);
    sound_result[0]=Audio_Ch1Duty;
    Audio_Ch1NoteOn(33,0xC0,Audio_Ch1Duty);
    sound_result[1]=NR12;
    sound_wait(30); Audio_StopChannel(AUDIO_CHANNEL_CH1); sound_wait(15);
    // CH2: A4, 25% duty. Changing the cached duty takes effect on this trigger.
    Audio_SetCh2Duty(1);
    sound_result[2]=Audio_Ch2Duty;
    Audio_Ch2NoteOn(33,0xC0,Audio_Ch2Duty);
    sound_result[3]=NR22;
    sound_wait(30); Audio_StopChannel(AUDIO_CHANNEL_CH2); sound_wait(15);
    // CH3: the initialized triangle wave, at 50% digital output level.
    Audio_SetCh3Level(AUDIO_CH3_LEVEL_50);
    sound_result[4]=Audio_Ch3Level;
    Audio_Ch3NoteOn(33,Audio_Ch3Level);
    sound_result[5]=NR32;
    sound_wait(30); Audio_StopChannel(AUDIO_CHANNEL_CH3); sound_wait(15);
    // CH4: a sustained noise burst; param is NR43, not a pitched note number.
    Audio_SetCh4Param(0x35);
    sound_result[6]=Audio_Ch4Param;
    Audio_Ch4NoteOn(Audio_Ch4Param,0xC0);
    sound_result[7]=NR43;
    sound_wait(30); Audio_StopChannel(AUDIO_CHANNEL_CH4); sound_wait(15);
    sound_end();
}

Expected result

After about half a second of silence, hear CH1 A4, CH2 A4, CH3 A3 and noise. Each voice lasts 30 frames, with 15-frame gaps. SEQUENCE COMPLETE marks program completion; use the recording to assess the sound.

Declaration notes (original source)
Stop a physical channel and clear its legacy resume bit. CH1 also clears the
pulse effect stream; CH3 clears the wave effect stream. This is the legacy
channel API and does not clear a VBlank driver's independently latched notes.

kitaqgb/lib/audio.c:981

c
void __stackcall Audio_StopChannel(u8 ch) {
    if (ch == AUDIO_CHANNEL_CH1) {
        Audio_EffectPointer = 0;
        Audio_EffectPriority = 0;
        Audio_EffectBank = 0;
        Audio_EffectPan = AUDIO_PAN_INHERIT;
        Audio_LastChMask = (u8)(Audio_LastChMask & (u8)~AUDIO_RESUME_CH1);
        Audio_UpdateNR51();
        Audio_SilenceCh1();
    } else if (ch == AUDIO_CHANNEL_CH2) {
        Audio_LastChMask = (u8)(Audio_LastChMask & (u8)~AUDIO_RESUME_CH2);
        Audio_SilenceCh2();
    } else if (ch == AUDIO_CHANNEL_CH3) {
        Audio_EffectPointer3 = 0;
        Audio_EffectPriority3 = 0;
        Audio_EffectBank3 = 0;
        Audio_EffectPan3 = AUDIO_PAN_INHERIT;
        Audio_LastChMask = (u8)(Audio_LastChMask & (u8)~AUDIO_RESUME_CH3);
        Audio_UpdateNR51();
        Audio_Ch3Off();
    } else if (ch == AUDIO_CHANNEL_CH4) {
        Audio_LastChMask = (u8)(Audio_LastChMask & (u8)~AUDIO_RESUME_CH4);
        Audio_SilenceCh4();
    }
}

Audio_StopSfx

Clear both effect streams and their pan overrides, then release the borrowed channels.

Syntax

c
void Audio_StopSfx();

Return value

No return value. Changes sound registers or driver state.

Conditions and limits

An effect consumes one (note,value) pair per update and ends at note=0. The value is NR12 for pulse effects or NR32 for CH3. Prefix CH3 data with 0xFF. Keep storage alive until completion. Priorities compete within a slot; equal priority can replace its owner.

In the ordinary configuration, effect release turns CH3 off. It silences CH1 when music is stopped, but does not automatically replay an earlier music note while music is playing. With AUDIO_VBLANK_SFX_RESTORE, release requests recovery from the ISR.

Usage example

c
// Each pair lasts one update. Priority controls replacement within each slot.
#include "gb_sound_example.h"
#pragma bank 2
__prg_rom u8 effect[]={33,0xC0,33,0xC0,33,0xC0,33,0xC0,33,0xC0,33,0xC0,
    40,0xC0,40,0xC0,40,0xC0,40,0xC0,40,0xC0,40,0xC0,0};
__prg_rom u8 wave_effect[]={AUDIO_SFX_CH3_MARKER,
    33,0x20,33,0x20,33,0x20,33,0x20,33,0x20,33,0x20,
    40,0x20,40,0x20,40,0x20,40,0x20,40,0x20,40,0x20,0};
#pragma bank 0
void main() {
    sound_begin("BANKED SOUND EFFECT");
    Audio_SetMasterVolume(3,3);
    // Read the marker in bank 2 while restoring the caller's original mapping.
    Audio_PlaySFXPannedBanked(2,effect,5,AUDIO_PAN_LEFT);
    sound_result[0]=Audio_EffectPriority;
    Audio_PlaySFXBanked(2,effect,4);
    sound_result[1]=Audio_EffectPriority;
    sound_wait(30);
    Audio_PlaySFXPannedBanked(2,wave_effect,5,AUDIO_PAN_RIGHT);
    sound_result[2]=Audio_EffectPriority3;
    sound_wait(30);
    // Implicit-bank entry points capture bank 2; the service restores bank 1.
    __bankswitch(2);
    Audio_PlaySFX(effect,5);
    __bankswitch(1);
    sound_result[3]=Audio_EffectBank;
    sound_wait(30);
    __bankswitch(2);
    Audio_PlaySFXPanned(effect,5,AUDIO_PAN_RIGHT);
    __bankswitch(1);
    sound_wait(6);
    Audio_StopSfx();
    sound_result[4]=(u8)(Audio_EffectPointer==0);
    sound_wait(24);
    // Disabling effects releases current owners; re-enable before the next request.
    Audio_PlaySFXBanked(2,effect,5);
    sound_wait(6);
    Audio_SetSfxEnabled(0);
    sound_result[5]=Audio_SfxEnabled;
    sound_result[6]=(u8)(Audio_EffectPointer==0);
    sound_wait(24);
    Audio_SetSfxEnabled(1);
    Audio_PlaySFXBanked(2,effect,5);
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_result[7]=Audio_SfxEnabled;
    sound_end();
}

Expected result

Bank-2 data plays a short rising pulse on the left, a wave effect on the right and a centered pulse. Later examples stop a right pulse early, disable an effect and re-enable playback. A priority-4 request cannot replace priority 5.

    Audio_EffectPointer = 0;

    Audio_EffectBank3 = 0;

Audio_Update

Advance the volume fade once; unless paused, service effects then music.

Syntax

c
void Audio_Update();

Return value

No return value. Changes sound registers or driver state.

Conditions and limits

Include audio_hwregs_gb.c before audio.c and call Audio_Init at startup. Call Audio_Update exactly once per frame, about 59.7 Hz. Stream reads temporarily change the ROM mapping; do not re-enter this driver from an interrupt.

Fades continue while paused. Reading WAIT n is followed by n waiting calls, so the next command occurs after n+1 updates.

Usage example

c
// Original two-note phrase: pause preserves the cursor; the enable gate does not.
#include "gb_sound_example.h"
__prg_rom u8 song[]={
    AUDIO_CMD_SET_INST,AUDIO_STREAM_CHANNEL_CH1,2,0xC0,
    AUDIO_CMD_NOTE,AUDIO_STREAM_CHANNEL_CH1,33,AUDIO_CMD_WAIT,59,
    AUDIO_CMD_NOTE,AUDIO_STREAM_CHANNEL_CH1,40,AUDIO_CMD_WAIT,59,
    AUDIO_CMD_LOOP
};
void main() {
    u8 delay;
    sound_begin("MUSIC PAUSE GATE");
    Audio_SetMasterVolume(3,3);
    Audio_PlayMusic(0,song);
    sound_wait(30);
    delay=Audio_Delay;
    Audio_SetPaused(1);
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_result[0]=(u8)(Audio_Delay==delay);
    sound_result[1]=Audio_Paused;
    Audio_SetPaused(0);
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_result[2]=Audio_Paused;
    // Disabling suppresses note writes; the next 30 updates still consume data.
    Audio_SetMusicEnabled(0);
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_result[3]=Audio_Delay;
    sound_result[4]=Audio_MusicEnabled;
    // Explicitly stop the sounding channel while leaving the stream running.
    Audio_StopChannel(AUDIO_CHANNEL_CH1);
    sound_wait(30);
    Audio_SetMusicEnabled(1);
    sound_wait(30);
    Audio_StopMusic();
    sound_result[5]=Audio_PlayingMusic;
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_end();
}

Expected result

Hear a note, paused silence, resume, a note retained while music is disabled, explicit channel silence, the next note after re-enabling, then stop. RAM also verifies that 30 paused updates preserve the delay, while the disabled gate still advances it to 30.

audio_vblank.h — Music playback through the VBlank IRQ

Services music in VBlank, coordinates effect ownership and provides a frame hook. Do not also advance the same song through the ordinary music decoder.

audio_vblank.c implements __kq_vblank_vector; do not also install a competing VBlank vector. The sample defines Audio_NoiseEffectActive, excludes the ordinary music decoder, and uses Audio_Update only for effects and fades. Mask interrupts while changing song pointers or shared state.

Keep direct song data in fixed ROM or another area always visible to the ISR. A record is five bytes: delay, CH1, CH2, CH3, CH4. In note fields, 0xFF holds the current voice and 0xFD stops it. In the delay field, 0xFF ends playback and 0xFE loops. This is the record layout, not the channel-ID numbering. WRAM queue playback is a separate mode; submit complete five-byte records with AudioVBlank_QueueRefill.

AudioVBlank_DisableIrq

Clear only IE’s VBlank bit, leaving other interrupt sources and sound unchanged.

Syntax

c
void AudioVBlank_DisableIrq();

Return value

No return value. Changes sound registers or driver state.

Conditions and limits

audio_vblank.c implements __kq_vblank_vector; do not also install a competing VBlank vector. The sample defines Audio_NoiseEffectActive, excludes the ordinary music decoder, and uses Audio_Update only for effects and fades. Mask interrupts while changing song pointers or shared state.

Keep direct song data in fixed ROM or another area always visible to the ISR. A record is five bytes: delay, CH1, CH2, CH3, CH4. In note fields, 0xFF holds the current voice and 0xFD stops it. In the delay field, 0xFF ends playback and 0xFE loops. This is the record layout, not the channel-ID numbering. WRAM queue playback is a separate mode; submit complete five-byte records with AudioVBlank_QueueRefill.

Usage example

c
// Direct fixed-bank music with an actual VBlank ISR and a counting frame hook.
#define SOUND_VBLANK
#include "gb_sound_example.h"
__wram u8 hook_count;
__prg_rom u8 irq_song[]={30,33,0xFF,0xFF,0xFF,30,40,0xFF,0xFF,0xFF,0xFE};
void frame_hook() { hook_count++; }
void main() {
    u8 before;
    sound_begin("VBLANK MUSIC GATES");
    Audio_NoiseEffectActive=0;
    AudioVBlank_Init();
    sound_result[0]=AudioVBlank_MusicPlaying;
    AudioVBlank_Ch1Envelope=0xC0;
    Audio_SetMasterVolume(3,3);
    hook_count=0; AudioVBlank_FrameHook=frame_hook;
    AudioVBlank_SetMusic(irq_song);
    AudioVBlank_Play();
    AudioVBlank_EnableIrq();
    sound_wait(45);
    // Disable music processing while the hook and current note remain active.
    __asm { DI }
    AudioVBlank_SetEnabled(0); before=hook_count;
    __asm { EI }
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_result[1]=(u8)(hook_count!=before);
    __asm { DI }
    AudioVBlank_Stop();
    __asm { EI }
    sound_wait(30);
    __asm { DI }
    AudioVBlank_SetEnabled(1); AudioVBlank_PlayMusic(irq_song);
    __asm { EI }
    sound_wait(45);
    AudioVBlank_DisableIrq();
    before=hook_count;
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_result[2]=(u8)(hook_count==before);
    sound_result[3]=(u8)(AudioVBlank_IE&1);
    AudioVBlank_Stop(); sound_wait(30);
    sound_end();
}

Expected result

The ISR plays a two-note song. Compare gating music updates, which retains the current sound; Stop, which silences it; and gating IRQ after restart, which also retains sound. RAM verifies that the hook runs while music is disabled and stops when IRQ is disabled.

void AudioVBlank_Play()

    Audio_SetMasterVolume(3,3);
    hook_count=0; AudioVBlank_FrameHook=frame_hook;
    AudioVBlank_SetMusic(irq_song);
    AudioVBlank_Play();
    AudioVBlank_EnableIrq();
    sound_wait(45);
    // Disable music processing while the hook and current note remain active.
    __asm { DI }
    AudioVBlank_SetEnabled(0); before=hook_count;
    __asm { EI }
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_result[1]=(u8)(hook_count!=before);
    __asm { DI }
    AudioVBlank_Stop();
    __asm { EI }
    sound_wait(30);
    __asm { DI }
    AudioVBlank_SetEnabled(1); AudioVBlank_PlayMusic(irq_song);
    __asm { EI }
    sound_wait(45);
    AudioVBlank_DisableIrq();
    before=hook_count;
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_result[2]=(u8)(hook_count==before);
    sound_result[3]=(u8)(AudioVBlank_IE&1);
    AudioVBlank_Stop(); sound_wait(30);
    sound_end();
}

Expected result

The ISR plays a two-note song. Compare gating music updates, which retains the current sound; Stop, which silences it; and gating IRQ after restart, which also retains sound. RAM verifies that the hook runs while music is disabled and stops when IRQ is disabled.

AudioVBlank_QueuePlay

Enable playback when queue mode is active and at least one record is available. Preserve cursors, delay, music-enable and pause state. Reset and prefill the queue before starting a new stream.

Syntax

c
u8 AudioVBlank_QueuePlay();

Return value

Return one when accepted, or zero for an empty queue or non-queue mode. Consumption requires a running ISR, enabled music and an unpaused driver.

Conditions and limits

After AudioVBlank_Init, call QueueReset, QueueRefill and QueuePlay in that order. Compile the ordinary audio_vblank.c; AUDIO_VBLANK_CORE_ONLY excludes the C producer functions. Foreground code fills a queue of sixteen five-byte records and the VBlank ISR consumes it.

Use a single foreground producer; do not call it recursively or from an ISR or FrameHook. Each short publication step saves IE and masks interrupt sources, then restores IE and SVBK. IME is unchanged. Select and retain the source ROM/RAM bank in caller code.

Timed records contain delay, ch1_note, ch2_note, ch3_note and ch4_noise_param. Supply END as a complete five-byte record too. Expand LOOP in producer code by submitting the required records again. Do not pass a variable-length direct-play command stream unchanged.

Usage example

c
if(AudioVBlank_QueuePlay()==0) sound_result[0]++;
    AudioVBlank_EnableIrq();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Play an original eight-note phrase six times, then stop. Feed 49 records—48 notes plus END—through the sixteen-slot queue. Checks cover all 49 accepted records, zero underruns, stopped playback, empty/full/null/zero-count cases, CGB WRAM-bank restoration, preserved IME, active audio and silence after completion.

{

AudioVBlank_QueueRefill

Copy complete five-byte records into available queue slots and publish each only after its copy finishes. One call accepts at most sixteen records.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall AudioVBlank_QueueRefill(const u8 *records, u8 count);

Parameters

records

Record array in the currently readable bank. Provide five readable bytes per accepted record. A null pointer returns zero.

count

Number of records to attempt, not bytes. Values above sixteen are capped at sixteen; zero does nothing.

Return value

Return the actual accepted record count, 0..16. Return zero for a full queue, null input, zero count or non-queue mode. Advance the source by five times the return value. The ISR may free slots during the call, so this is not necessarily the free count at entry.

Conditions and limits

After AudioVBlank_Init, call QueueReset, QueueRefill and QueuePlay in that order. Compile the ordinary audio_vblank.c; AUDIO_VBLANK_CORE_ONLY excludes the C producer functions. Foreground code fills a queue of sixteen five-byte records and the VBlank ISR consumes it.

Use a single foreground producer; do not call it recursively or from an ISR or FrameHook. Each short publication step saves IE and masks interrupt sources, then restores IE and SVBK. IME is unchanged. Select and retain the source ROM/RAM bank in caller code.

Timed records contain delay, ch1_note, ch2_note, ch3_note and ch4_noise_param. Supply END as a complete five-byte record too. Expand LOOP in producer code by submitting the required records again. Do not pass a variable-length direct-play command stream unchanged.

Usage example

c
next=AudioVBlank_QueueRefill(queue_song,16);
    // next counts records; each record occupies five source bytes.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Play an original eight-note phrase six times, then stop. Feed 49 records—48 notes plus END—through the sixteen-slot queue. Checks cover all 49 accepted records, zero underruns, stopped playback, empty/full/null/zero-count cases, CGB WRAM-bank restoration, preserved IME, active audio and silence after completion.

Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/audio_vblank.h:93

Declaration notes (original source)
Copy complete records from the currently mapped source; return records accepted.
Each call attempts at most 16 records and stops when full. Null/zero returns 0.
Supports ROM and RAM sources, restores SVBK and IE, and never changes IME.
Single foreground producer only: do not call from an ISR or frame hook.
LOOP must be expanded by the producer. END occupies a full five-byte record.

kitaqgb/lib/audio_vblank_queue.inc:93

c
u8 __stackcall AudioVBlank_QueueRefill(const u8 *records, u8 count)
{
    u8 accepted;
    u8 i;
    if (records == 0 || count == 0 || AudioVBlank_QueueMode == 0) return 0;
    if (count > AUDIO_VBLANK_QUEUE_RECORDS) count = AUDIO_VBLANK_QUEUE_RECORDS;
    accepted = 0;
    while (accepted < count) {
        if (AudioVBlank_QueueCount >= AUDIO_VBLANK_QUEUE_RECORDS) break;
        for (i = 0; i < 5; i++) AudioVBlank_QueueStaging[i] = records[i];
        if (AudioVBlank_QueuePublish() == 0) break;
        records += 5;
        accepted++;
    }
    return accepted;
}

AudioVBlank_RequestRestoreCh1

Set pulse release-only request 2 if nothing is pending, preserving an existing recovery request 1.

Syntax

c
void AudioVBlank_RequestRestoreCh1();

Return value

No return value. Changes sound registers or driver state.

Conditions and limits

audio_vblank.c implements __kq_vblank_vector; do not also install a competing VBlank vector. The sample defines Audio_NoiseEffectActive, excludes the ordinary music decoder, and uses Audio_Update only for effects and fades. Mask interrupts while changing song pointers or shared state.

When calling recovery directly, the caller ensures the effect has released the voice and clears the pending flag afterward. Request functions alone do not write sound registers.

Usage example

c
// Exercise the recovery API with IRQ disabled and explicit effect ownership.
#define SOUND_VBLANK
#include "gb_sound_example.h"
void main() {
    sound_begin("EFFECT RECOVERY");
    Audio_NoiseEffectActive=0; AudioVBlank_Init();
    Audio_SetMasterVolume(3,3);
    AudioVBlank_MusicPlaying=1;
    AudioVBlank_Ch1Envelope=0xC0; AudioVBlank_Ch1LatchedNote=33;
    AudioVBlank_Ch3LatchedNote=33;
    // Value 1 represents a suppressed BGM event and survives a release request.
    AudioVBlank_RestoreCh1Pending=1;
    AudioVBlank_RequestRestoreCh1();
    sound_result[0]=AudioVBlank_RestoreCh1Pending;
    AudioVBlank_RestoreCh1(); AudioVBlank_RestoreCh1Pending=0;
    sound_wait(30);
    // Without a pending event, RequestRestore creates release-only value 2.
    AudioVBlank_RequestRestoreCh1();
    sound_result[1]=AudioVBlank_RestoreCh1Pending;
    AudioVBlank_RestoreCh1(); AudioVBlank_RestoreCh1Pending=0;
    sound_wait(30);
    AudioVBlank_RestoreCh3Pending=1;
    AudioVBlank_RequestRestoreCh3();
    sound_result[2]=AudioVBlank_RestoreCh3Pending;
    AudioVBlank_RestoreCh3(); AudioVBlank_RestoreCh3Pending=0;
    sound_wait(30);
    AudioVBlank_RequestRestoreCh3();
    sound_result[3]=AudioVBlank_RestoreCh3Pending;
    AudioVBlank_RestoreCh3(); AudioVBlank_RestoreCh3Pending=0;
    sound_wait(30);
    AudioVBlank_Stop();
    sound_end();
}

Expected result

Hear pulse recovery, silence, wave recovery and silence, each for 30 frames. A release request preserves pending value 1; requesting with no pending event produces release-only value 2. Here IRQ is disabled and the caller explicitly manages ownership.

kitaqgb/lib/audio_vblank.c:769

c
void AudioVBlank_RestoreCh1()
{
    __asm {
        LD_A_MEM Audio_EffectUsesCh2
        OR_A
        JR_NZ audiovb_restore_ch2
        LD_A_MEM AudioVBlank_RestoreCh1Pending
        CP_IMM 2
        JR_Z audiovb_restore_ch1_off
        LD_A_MEM AudioVBlank_MusicPlaying
        OR_A
        JR_Z audiovb_restore_ch1_off
        LD_A_MEM AudioVBlank_MusicEnabled
        OR_A
        JR_Z audiovb_restore_ch1_off
        LD_A_MEM Audio_MusicEnabled
        OR_A
        JR_Z audiovb_restore_ch1_off
        LD_A_MEM AudioVBlank_Ch1LatchedNote
        CP_IMM 0x44
        JR_NC audiovb_restore_ch1_off
        LD_C_A
        LD_A_MEM AudioVBlank_Ch1Sweep
        LDH_MEM_A 0x10
        LD_A_MEM AudioVBlank_Ch1Duty
        LDH_MEM_A 0x11
        LD_A_MEM AudioVBlank_Ch1Envelope
        LDH_MEM_A 0x12
        LD_A_C
        LD_E_A
        LD_D_IMM 0
        LD_HL_IMM AudioVBlank_FreqLo
        ADD_HL_DE
        LD_A_HL
        LDH_MEM_A 0x13
        LD_HL_IMM AudioVBlank_FreqHi
        ADD_HL_DE
        LD_A_HL
        OR_IMM 0x80
        LDH_MEM_A 0x14
        JR audiovb_restore_ch1_done
audiovb_restore_ch1_off:
        XOR_A
        LDH_MEM_A 0x12
audiovb_restore_ch1_done:
        JR audiovb_restore_square_done

audiovb_restore_ch2:
        LD_A_MEM AudioVBlank_RestoreCh1Pending
        CP_IMM 2
        JR_Z audiovb_restore_ch2_off
        LD_A_MEM AudioVBlank_MusicPlaying
        OR_A
        JR_Z audiovb_restore_ch2_off
        LD_A_MEM AudioVBlank_MusicEnabled
        OR_A
        JR_Z audiovb_restore_ch2_off
        LD_A_MEM Audio_MusicEnabled
        OR_A
        JR_Z audiovb_restore_ch2_off
        LD_A_MEM AudioVBlank_Ch2LatchedNote
        CP_IMM 0x44
        JR_NC audiovb_restore_ch2_off
        LD_C_A
        LD_A_MEM AudioVBlank_Ch2Duty
        LDH_MEM_A 0x16
        LD_A_MEM AudioVBlank_Ch2Envelope
        LDH_MEM_A 0x17
        LD_A_C
        LD_E_A
        LD_D_IMM 0
        LD_HL_IMM AudioVBlank_FreqLo
        ADD_HL_DE
        LD_A_HL
        LDH_MEM_A 0x18
        LD_HL_IMM AudioVBlank_FreqHi
        ADD_HL_DE
        LD_A_HL
        OR_IMM 0x80
        LDH_MEM_A 0x19
        JR audiovb_restore_square_done
audiovb_restore_ch2_off:
        XOR_A
        LDH_MEM_A 0x17
audiovb_restore_square_done:
    }
}

    AudioVBlank_RestoreCh3(); AudioVBlank_RestoreCh3Pending=0;
    sound_wait(30);
    AudioVBlank_Stop();
    sound_end();
}

Expected result

Hear pulse recovery, silence, wave recovery and silence, each for 30 frames. A release request preserves pending value 1; requesting with no pending event produces release-only value 2. Here IRQ is disabled and the caller explicitly manages ownership.

AudioVBlank_SetEnabled

Gate VBlank music and clear recovery requests on disable. Current sound and IRQ remain unchanged.

Syntax

c
void __stackcall AudioVBlank_SetEnabled(u8 on);

Parameters

on

Zero disables; nonzero enables. Read this function’s description to distinguish muting from gating updates.

Return value

No return value. Changes sound registers or driver state.

Conditions and limits

audio_vblank.c implements __kq_vblank_vector; do not also install a competing VBlank vector. The sample defines Audio_NoiseEffectActive, excludes the ordinary music decoder, and uses Audio_Update only for effects and fades. Mask interrupts while changing song pointers or shared state.

Keep direct song data in fixed ROM or another area always visible to the ISR. A record is five bytes: delay, CH1, CH2, CH3, CH4. In note fields, 0xFF holds the current voice and 0xFD stops it. In the delay field, 0xFF ends playback and 0xFE loops. This is the record layout, not the channel-ID numbering. WRAM queue playback is a separate mode; submit complete five-byte records with AudioVBlank_QueueRefill.

Usage example

c
// Direct fixed-bank music with an actual VBlank ISR and a counting frame hook.
#define SOUND_VBLANK
#include "gb_sound_example.h"
__wram u8 hook_count;
__prg_rom u8 irq_song[]={30,33,0xFF,0xFF,0xFF,30,40,0xFF,0xFF,0xFF,0xFE};
void frame_hook() { hook_count++; }
void main() {
    u8 before;
    sound_begin("VBLANK MUSIC GATES");
    Audio_NoiseEffectActive=0;
    AudioVBlank_Init();
    sound_result[0]=AudioVBlank_MusicPlaying;
    AudioVBlank_Ch1Envelope=0xC0;
    Audio_SetMasterVolume(3,3);
    hook_count=0; AudioVBlank_FrameHook=frame_hook;
    AudioVBlank_SetMusic(irq_song);
    AudioVBlank_Play();
    AudioVBlank_EnableIrq();
    sound_wait(45);
    // Disable music processing while the hook and current note remain active.
    __asm { DI }
    AudioVBlank_SetEnabled(0); before=hook_count;
    __asm { EI }
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_result[1]=(u8)(hook_count!=before);
    __asm { DI }
    AudioVBlank_Stop();
    __asm { EI }
    sound_wait(30);
    __asm { DI }
    AudioVBlank_SetEnabled(1); AudioVBlank_PlayMusic(irq_song);
    __asm { EI }
    sound_wait(45);
    AudioVBlank_DisableIrq();
    before=hook_count;
    sound_wait(30);
    sound_result[2]=(u8)(hook_count==before);
    sound_result[3]=(u8)(AudioVBlank_IE&1);
    AudioVBlank_Stop(); sound_wait(30);
    sound_end();
}

Expected result

The ISR plays a two-note song. Compare gating music updates, which retains the current sound; Stop, which silences it; and gating IRQ after restart, which also retains sound. RAM verifies that the hook runs while music is disabled and stops when IRQ is disabled.

{

bank.h — Bank-aware code and data access

A ROM bank is a block of cartridge storage mapped into the CPU's address space. Different banks can appear at the same CPU address, so a 16-bit pointer alone does not identify banked data. BankPtr is a packed three-byte descriptor containing a one-byte bank number and a two-byte pointer. Use farptr_make to construct it and farptr_read8, farptr_read16 or farptr_read to access its contents.

The GB example uses an MBC5 cartridge: code in fixed bank 0 stays accessible at $0000–$3FFF while banks 1, 2 and 3 are selected at $4000–$7FFF. Keep bank_switch and the code that resumes after it in fixed ROM. Initialize the library's bank record with bank_switch before querying it. GB far_call accepts a callback pointer; __farcall requires a function name.

bank_get_current

Return the last bank number stored by bank_switch. This reads software bookkeeping, not cartridge registers.

Syntax

c
u8 bank_get_current();

Return value

The u8 value most recently stored by bank_switch; zero before initialization.

Conditions and limits

The library record starts at zero and does not discover the cartridge's startup mapping. Initialize it with bank_switch. Direct intrinsics and raw mapper writes do not update this separate record; bank_get_current therefore cannot verify the actual hardware mapping.

Usage example

c
starting_bank=bank_get_current(); // Last value recorded by bank_switch.
bank_expect(starting_bank==2,1);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The initial bank_switch(2) records and selects bank 2. Later, direct switching selects bank 1 and reads A1 from home1 while bank_get_current still reports 2; switching back makes home2 read B2 again.

The complete program teaches how a bank number and near address identify data, how callbacks cross banks, and how to distinguish the library's record from the actual mapping. All displayed numbers are hexadecimal. BANK IN and BANK OUT must show 02, BYTE HEX D3, WORD HEX 5C7A, and both FAILED CHECKS and FIRST FAILURE 00. CGB and FC display blue text; DMG displays black text.

CALL COUNT is 03: far_call, __farcall and __farcall_ptr each invoke the callback once.

bank_switch

Select the ROM bank and record it in both the bank library and the compiler's bank state. Far reads and calls use the compiler state to restore the previous mapping.

Syntax

c
void bank_switch(u8 bank);

Parameters

bank

An unsigned 8-bit ROM-bank number. For a call, it must agree with the function's placement; for a read, it selects the source mapping. Use the target cartridge's valid range.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

A permanent bank change must not unmap the executing code or its return address. Put this call, bank_switch itself when used, and the code that continues afterwards in common/fixed bank 0, as the sample does.

The library record starts at zero and does not discover the cartridge's startup mapping. Initialize it with bank_switch. Direct intrinsics and raw mapper writes do not update this separate record; bank_get_current therefore cannot verify the actual hardware mapping.

These GB bank interfaces carry eight bank bits and do not set the ninth MBC5 bank bit. Cartridge rules still apply, including mapper-specific treatment of bank zero. The example explicitly uses MBC5 banks 1–3; do not mix this state with untracked raw mapper writes.

Usage example

c
bank_switch(2); // Select the payload window and update library bookkeeping.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The initial bank_switch(2) records and selects bank 2. Later, direct switching selects bank 1 and reads A1 from home1 while bank_get_current still reports 2; switching back makes home2 read B2 again.

The complete program teaches how a bank number and near address identify data, how callbacks cross banks, and how to distinguish the library's record from the actual mapping. All displayed numbers are hexadecimal. BANK IN and BANK OUT must show 02, BYTE HEX D3, WORD HEX 5C7A, and both FAILED CHECKS and FIRST FAILURE 00. CGB and FC display blue text; DMG displays black text.

CALL COUNT is 03: far_call, __farcall and __farcall_ptr each invoke the callback once.

far_call

Forward a bank number and callback pointer to __farcall_ptr. This library function invokes a zero-argument callback and returns only after the caller's bank has been restored.

Syntax

c
void far_call(u8 bank, const void* func);

Parameters

bank

An unsigned 8-bit ROM-bank number. For a call, it must agree with the function's placement; for a read, it selects the source mapping. Use the target cartridge's valid range.

func

A valid executable address for a callback with no parameters. A function name or runtime pointer may supply it. Null pointers and a wrong bank/address combination are not checked at runtime.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

These calls do not forward user arguments or make the callback interrupt-reentrant. Keep the callback's own data, stack and interrupt use valid. The bank-restoring call paths are tested with nested calls and repeated calls; physical hardware and arbitrary interrupt interleavings are not covered by this example.

These GB bank interfaces carry eight bank bits and do not set the ninth MBC5 bank bit. Cartridge rules still apply, including mapper-specific treatment of bank zero. The example explicitly uses MBC5 banks 1–3; do not mix this state with untracked raw mapper writes.

Usage example

c
far_call(3,callback); // No arguments; callback reads payload[0] in bank 3.
bank_expect(callback_count==1 && callback_byte==0xD3,15);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

At this point in the complete program, far_call raises callback_count to 1. The callback reads D3 from bank 3. A later near read of B2 from home2 verifies that execution returned with bank 2 mapped.

The complete program teaches how a bank number and near address identify data, how callbacks cross banks, and how to distinguish the library's record from the actual mapping. All displayed numbers are hexadecimal. BANK IN and BANK OUT must show 02, BYTE HEX D3, WORD HEX 5C7A, and both FAILED CHECKS and FIRST FAILURE 00. CGB and FC display blue text; DMG displays black text.

CALL COUNT is 03: far_call, __farcall and __farcall_ptr each invoke the callback once.

far_data_read

Copy len bytes from the specified ROM bank into caller-owned RAM through the far-memory intrinsic. Restore the previous bank before returning.

Syntax

c
void far_data_read(u8 bank, const void* addr, void* dst, u16 len);

Parameters

bank

An unsigned 8-bit ROM-bank number. For a call, it must agree with the function's placement; for a read, it selects the source mapping. Use the target cartridge's valid range.

addr

Near pointer to readable source bytes in the selected ROM bank. It does not contain a bank number.

dst

Destination in writable memory. Reserve enough space for every byte copied. Except for a zero-byte transfer, a null or invalid destination is not checked.

len

Byte count, 0–65535. Zero performs no memory copy, but the bank-selection and restoration steps still run.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

Keep the full source range in the intended ROM mapping and the full destination range in writable memory. Copying does not select the next bank at a window boundary, handle overlapping ranges like memmove, or provide VRAM-safe writes. Use the graphics transfer APIs for VRAM.

Far reads and copies are synchronous and use shared compiler scratch. Do not let an interrupt run another banked transfer over the same scratch while one is active. On GB, the copy helper also uses one shared HRAM slot for the saved bank. The sample performs these operations from fixed code with no competing banked-transfer handler.

These GB bank interfaces carry eight bank bits and do not set the ninth MBC5 bank bit. Cartridge rules still apply, including mapper-specific treatment of bank zero. The example explicitly uses MBC5 banks 1–3; do not mix this state with untracked raw mapper writes.

Usage example

c
far_data_read(3,payload,buffer,4); // Copy into four writable RAM bytes.
bank_expect(buffer[0]==0xD3 && buffer[1]==0x7A && buffer[2]==0x5C && buffer[3]==0x96,7);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This excerpt copies 4 bytes through far_data_read and checks the buffer against D3 7A 5C 96. The source descriptor or pointer is retained by the caller; the full program separately checks a zero-length copy and bank restoration.

The complete program teaches how a bank number and near address identify data, how callbacks cross banks, and how to distinguish the library's record from the actual mapping. All displayed numbers are hexadecimal. BANK IN and BANK OUT must show 02, BYTE HEX D3, WORD HEX 5C7A, and both FAILED CHECKS and FIRST FAILURE 00. CGB and FC display blue text; DMG displays black text.

CALL COUNT is 03: far_call, __farcall and __farcall_ptr each invoke the callback once.

far_data_read16

Read two consecutive bytes through __farpeek16 and combine them as a little-endian word. The first byte becomes the low eight bits.

Syntax

c
u16 far_data_read16(u8 bank, const void* addr);

Parameters

bank

An unsigned 8-bit ROM-bank number. For a call, it must agree with the function's placement; for a read, it selects the source mapping. Use the target cartridge's valid range.

addr

Near pointer to readable source bytes in the selected ROM bank. It does not contain a bank number.

Return value

The little-endian word read, as u16 (0–65535).

Conditions and limits

The complete byte or word must be readable in the selected CPU mapping. These reads do not validate pointers, clip addresses or advance automatically to another ROM bank at a window boundary. A word read needs two valid consecutive bytes.

Far reads and copies are synchronous and use shared compiler scratch. Do not let an interrupt run another banked transfer over the same scratch while one is active. On GB, the copy helper also uses one shared HRAM slot for the saved bank. The sample performs these operations from fixed code with no competing banked-transfer handler.

These GB bank interfaces carry eight bank bits and do not set the ninth MBC5 bank bit. Cartridge rules still apply, including mapper-specific treatment of bank zero. The example explicitly uses MBC5 banks 1–3; do not mix this state with untracked raw mapper writes.

Usage example

c
word_value=far_data_read16(3,payload+1); // Little-endian 7A 5C -> 0x5C7A.
bank_expect(word_value==0x5C7A,6);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This excerpt uses far_data_read16 to read payload+1 in bank 3 and checks 5C7A. In the full program, the near read from home2 also confirms that the bank-2 mapping is restored.

The complete program teaches how a bank number and near address identify data, how callbacks cross banks, and how to distinguish the library's record from the actual mapping. All displayed numbers are hexadecimal. BANK IN and BANK OUT must show 02, BYTE HEX D3, WORD HEX 5C7A, and both FAILED CHECKS and FIRST FAILURE 00. CGB and FC display blue text; DMG displays black text.

CALL COUNT is 03: far_call, __farcall and __farcall_ptr each invoke the callback once.

farptr_make

Store a bank byte and a CPU-visible pointer in the caller's BankPtr. This constructs a descriptor; it does not switch banks or read the pointed-to bytes.

Syntax

c
void farptr_make(BankPtr* out, u8 bank, const u8* ptr);

Parameters

out

Pointer to writable storage for one three-byte BankPtr. A null out pointer is ignored and causes no write.

bank

An unsigned 8-bit ROM-bank number. For a call, it must agree with the function's placement; for a read, it selects the source mapping. Use the target cartridge's valid range.

ptr

The 16-bit CPU-visible address to store in the descriptor. It is copied unchanged; this function does not check whether that address exists in the chosen bank.

Return value

None (void).

Usage example

farptr_make(&pointer,3,payload+1); // Store a bank and address; do not read ROM.
bank_expect(pointer.bank==3 && pointer.ptr==payload+1,8);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The descriptor is set to bank 3 and payload+1. Its readers then obtain 7A, 5C7A and the three bytes 7A 5C 96. The null-output call must leave all state unchanged.

The complete program teaches how a bank number and near address identify data, how callbacks cross banks, and how to distinguish the library's record from the actual mapping. All displayed numbers are hexadecimal. BANK IN and BANK OUT must show 02, BYTE HEX D3, WORD HEX 5C7A, and both FAILED CHECKS and FIRST FAILURE 00. farptr_read

Copy len bytes from a BankPtr into writable RAM. The descriptor is passed by value, so the caller's pointer still identifies the start of the source.

Syntax

c
void farptr_read(BankPtr ptr, void* dst, u16 len);

Parameters

ptr

A BankPtr value containing both bank and ptr. Pass the descriptor itself, not its address. The caller's descriptor is not modified.

dst

Destination in writable memory. Reserve enough space for every byte copied. Except for a zero-byte transfer, a null or invalid destination is not checked.

len

Byte count, 0–65535. Zero performs no memory copy, but the bank-selection and restoration steps still run.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

Keep the full source range in the intended ROM mapping and the full destination range in writable memory. Copying does not select the next bank at a window boundary, handle overlapping ranges like memmove, or provide VRAM-safe writes. Use the graphics transfer APIs for VRAM.

Far reads and copies are synchronous and use shared compiler scratch. Do not let an interrupt run another banked transfer over the same scratch while one is active. On GB, the copy helper also uses one shared HRAM slot for the saved bank. The sample performs these operations from fixed code with no competing banked-transfer handler.

These GB bank interfaces carry eight bank bits and do not set the ninth MBC5 bank bit. Cartridge rules still apply, including mapper-specific treatment of bank zero. The example explicitly uses MBC5 banks 1–3; do not mix this state with untracked raw mapper writes.

Usage example

c
farptr_read(pointer,buffer,3);
bank_expect(buffer[0]==0x7A && buffer[1]==0x5C && buffer[2]==0x96,11);
bank_expect(pointer.bank==3 && pointer.ptr==payload+1,23);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This excerpt copies 3 bytes through farptr_read and checks the buffer against 7A 5C 96. The source descriptor or pointer is retained by the caller; the full program separately checks a zero-length copy and bank restoration.

The complete program teaches how a bank number and near address identify data, how callbacks cross banks, and how to distinguish the library's record from the actual mapping. All displayed numbers are hexadecimal. BANK IN and BANK OUT must show 02, BYTE HEX D3, WORD HEX 5C7A, and both FAILED CHECKS and FIRST FAILURE 00. CGB and FC display blue text; DMG displays black text.

CALL COUNT is 03: far_call, __farcall and __farcall_ptr each invoke the callback once.

camera.h — World coordinates and visible areas

Manage Q8.8 camera positions, targets and bounds, and convert world/screen coordinates. Choose caller-owned Camera8_8 objects or the lowercase API for one shared camera.

Camera_Add

Add Q8.8 deltas to the current position, then apply any enabled bounds.

Syntax

c
void Camera_Add(Camera8_8* cam, s16 dfx, s16 dfy);

Parameters

cam

Valid pointer to an initialized, caller-owned Camera8_8.

dfx

Signed Q8.8 displacement; 256 moves one pixel.

dfy

Signed Q8.8 displacement; 256 moves one pixel.

Return value

No return value. The affected state and when it takes effect are described in this entry.

Conditions and limits

Coordinates have eight fractional bits. Keep positions, targets and intermediate sums/differences within s16. Update the display separately with Camera_ApplyBg or a buffered flush.

Usage example

c
Camera_Add(&cam,256,512);result[13]=cam.fx;result[14]=cam.fy;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Learn Q8.8 following, clamping and coordinate conversion. Following yields X/Y=3584/4096; bounds give 3072/3584. BG X remains 13 while pending and becomes 8 after flush. The additional image shows a camera at (8,16) moving a 32×24 world rectangle from (32,32) to screen (24,16).

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\batch2_camera.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\batch2_camera.gb --no-cache --no-disasm --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k

Usage example

c
Camera_Init(&view);
Camera_Set(&view,2048,4096);
Camera_ApplyBg(&view);
Scroll_SetWindow(103,80);
Scroll_WindowShow();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

With camera (8,16), the red 32×24 rectangle appears at screen (24,16). The window shows a blue 64×64 frame at (96,80) and a green 16×16 square at (112,96). All shapes are black on DMG.

camera_clamp

Apply world-minus-screen bounds to the shared camera.

Syntax

c
void camera_clamp(u16 world_w_px, u16 world_h_px, u8 screen_w_px, u8 screen_h_px);

Parameters

world_w_px

World dimension in integer pixels; keep its positive excess over the screen within 0–127.

world_h_px

World dimension in integer pixels; keep its positive excess over the screen within 0–127.

screen_w_px

Viewport size in integer pixels; a viewport at least as large as the world gives zero travel on that axis.

screen_h_px

Viewport size in integer pixels; a viewport at least as large as the world gives zero travel on that axis.

Return value

No return value. The affected state and when it takes effect are described in this entry.

Conditions and limits

A world smaller than the viewport gives zero travel. A positive difference of 128 or more exceeds signed Q8.8 when converted. The u16 parameters do not imply support for camera travel across arbitrarily large worlds. These calls share one camera; use the uppercase API for independent camera objects. Positions converted from integer pixels to Q8.8 must be within −128 through 127.

Usage example

c
camera_clamp(176,160,160,144);result[29]=camera_world_to_screen_x(100);result[30]=camera_world_to_screen_y(90);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Learn Q8.8 following, clamping and coordinate conversion. Following yields X/Y=3584/4096; bounds give 3072/3584. BG X remains 13 while pending and becomes 8 after flush. The additional image shows a camera at (8,16) moving a 32×24 world rectangle from (32,32) to screen (24,16).

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\batch2_camera.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\batch2_camera.gb --no-cache --no-disasm --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k

Usage example

c
Camera_Init(&view);
Camera_Set(&view,2048,4096);
Camera_ApplyBg(&view);
Scroll_SetWindow(103,80);
Scroll_WindowShow();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

With camera (8,16), the red 32×24 rectangle appears at screen (24,16). The window shows a blue 64×64 frame at (96,80) and a green 16×16 square at (112,96). All shapes are black on DMG.

kitaqgb/lib/camera.h:46

Declaration notes (original source)
Derive nonnegative camera extents from world minus screen size, then convert
them to Q8.8 bounds. Extents must fit signed Q8.8; the u16 input type does

kitaqgb/lib/camera.c:123

c
void Camera_ClampToSize(Camera8_8* cam, u16 world_w_px, u16 world_h_px, u8 screen_w_px, u8 screen_h_px)
{
    s16 max_x = 0;
    s16 max_y = 0;

    if (world_w_px > screen_w_px) max_x = (s16)((u16)(world_w_px - screen_w_px) << 8);
    if (world_h_px > screen_h_px) max_y = (s16)((u16)(world_h_px - screen_h_px) << 8);
    Camera_SetBounds(cam, (s16)0, (s16)0, max_x, max_y);
}

camera_set

Move the shared camera using integer pixel coordinates, applying its enabled bounds.

Syntax

c
void camera_set(s16 x, s16 y);

Parameters

x

World X coordinate in integer pixels; the result and intermediate difference must fit s16.

y

World Y coordinate in integer pixels; the result and intermediate difference must fit s16.

Return value

No return value. The affected state and when it takes effect are described in this entry.

Conditions and limits

Coordinates have eight fractional bits. Keep positions, targets and intermediate sums/differences within s16. Update the display separately with Camera_ApplyBg or a buffered flush. These calls share one camera; use the uppercase API for independent camera objects. Positions converted from integer pixels to Q8.8 must be within −128 through 127.

Camera_StepTowardTarget

Approach the target by a right-shifted fraction of the remaining distance; do nothing when following is disabled.

Syntax

c
void Camera_StepTowardTarget(Camera8_8* cam, u8 shift);

Parameters

cam

Valid pointer to an initialized, caller-owned Camera8_8.

shift

Power of two used to divide the delta: 0 uses the whole delta, 1 uses half. Values above 7 are clamped to 7.

Return value

No return value. The affected state and when it takes effect are described in this entry.

Conditions and limits

A small positive delta can truncate to zero; an arithmetic right shift can turn a small negative delta into −1. Target equality is tested before clamping. An out-of-bounds target may therefore keep following active, or clear it even though the final clamped position differs from the target.

Usage example

Camera_StepTowardTarget(&cam,1);result[6]=cam.fx;result[7]=cam.fy;

Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/camera.h:38

Declaration notes (original source)
Move by the signed target delta shifted by 0..7 bits, then apply bounds.
Quantization can make a small delta produce no movement; only exact equality
clears targeting, and a target outside the bounds may remain active indefinitely.

kitaqgb/lib/camera.c:89

c
void Camera_StepTowardTarget(Camera8_8* cam, u8 shift)
{
    s16 dx;
    s16 dy;

    if (cam->use_target == 0) return;
    if (shift > 7) shift = 7;

    // Keep target-minus-position differences within s16 as well as the individual positions.
    dx = cam->target_fx - cam->fx;
    dy = cam->target_fy - cam->fy;

    if (dx != 0) cam->fx += (dx >> shift);
    if (dy != 0) cam->fy += (dy >> shift);

    if (cam->fx == cam->target_fx && cam->fy == cam->target_fy) cam->use_target = 0;
    Camera_ApplyBounds(cam);
}

cgb_palette.h — CGB BG and OBJ palettes

cgb_palette.h and cgb_palette.c provide RGB15 packing and immediate CGB palette updates. Choose BG helpers for background/window colors and OBJ helpers for sprite colors. Single-color and RGB-component functions change one color; range functions update consecutive words; full-palette functions write four words. The raw range functions use absolute color slots, whereas register intrinsics use byte positions. Set the palette assignment separately through map attributes or OAM. Include the implementation once in the program, as the complete sample does.

Palette and guarded register writes do nothing in DMG mode. Here, safe means a CGB-mode guard, not a PPU access wait or a critical section. Use LCD-off setup or a sufficiently short update in an accessible PPU phase. These functions do not wait for VBlank or protect a multi-byte update from interrupts.

BG/window and OBJ palettes are separate stores. These library writes enable index auto-increment and leave the index register changed. OBJ color index zero is transparent when rendering sprites, even though its palette bytes can be stored and read.

cgb_bg_color

Write one packed RGB15 color to the background/window palette store immediately. The palette and color indices select one of 32 color slots; this does not change tile data or select a tile's palette.

Syntax

c
void cgb_bg_color(u8 palette_index, u8 color_index, u16 rgb15);

Parameters

palette_index

Palette number, 0–7; only the low three bits are used (& 7).

color_index

Color number within the selected palette, 0–3; only the low two bits are used (& 3).

rgb15

Packed 15-bit RGB color, normally 0–32767. Both bytes of the supplied u16 are written, low byte first; the library does not explicitly clear bit 15. Use CGB_RGB15 or cgb_rgb15 to construct a valid value.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

Palette and guarded register writes do nothing in DMG mode. Here, safe means a CGB-mode guard, not a PPU access wait or a critical section. Use LCD-off setup or a sufficiently short update in an accessible PPU phase. These functions do not wait for VBlank or protect a multi-byte update from interrupts.

BG/window and OBJ palettes are separate stores. These library writes enable index auto-increment and leave the index register changed. OBJ color index zero is transparent when rendering sprites, even though its palette bytes can be stored and read.

Usage example

c
cgb_bg_color(1,3,31); // Red background color 3 of palette 1.
expect_color(0,7,31);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This program teaches how palette contents affect the same tile pattern differently in BG and OBJ. Each triangle is 8 × 8 pixels; its top row has one pixel on the left, expanding to a full bottom row. At x = 16, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96, 112, the BG row at y = 24 is red, blue, green, red, blue, green, red. The OBJ row at y = 64 is blue, green, red, blue, green, red, blue. The columns use single-color, component, indexed-range, full-palette, absolute-range, canonical-register and alias-register writes, respectively.

At y = 88, the seven 8 × 8 cells show: red triangle (x = 16), blue one-pixel square outline from bank 1 (32), horizontally reflected green triangle (48), vertically reflected red triangle (64), blue triangle reflected both ways (80), green triangle over a red sprite with red visible through color-zero pixels (96), and a full red sprite in front of the BG triangle as a priority control (112). Coordinates are screen pixels measured from the upper-left corner. Blank space and black text remain on white.

FAILED CHECKS 000 confirms RGB masking, truth-valued flags (including input 2), palette index wrapping, writes crossing a palette boundary, clamping at slot 31, null/zero-length no-ops and palette readback while LCD is off. Four target/hardware combinations are tested: dual-mode ROM on DMG and CGB, DMG-only on DMG, and CGB-only on CGB. On DMG, CGB MODE is 0, all triangles are black, the bank/flip attributes have no display effect, and the last two bottom cells are black squares. CGB MODE is 1 in CGB tests. Real hardware and LCD-on palette contention are not covered.

cgb_bg_colors

Write consecutive RGB15 words to the background/window palettes, starting at the specified palette/color pair. The range can cross a four-color palette boundary; it stops at the end of the complete 32-color store.

Syntax

c
void cgb_bg_colors(u8 palette_index, u8 start_color_index, const u16* colors, u8 color_count);

Parameters

palette_index

Palette number, 0–7; only the low three bits are used (& 7).

start_color_index

Color number within the selected palette, 0–3; only the low two bits are used (& 3).

colors

Readable const u16* containing the requested color words. Data is consumed during the call, not queued. Keep the source and its ROM bank accessible; no bank switch is performed for you. A null pointer causes no writes.

color_count

Number of color words, not bytes, supplied as u8 (0–255). Zero does nothing. The effective count is limited to 32 - normalized_start_slot; only that many source words are read.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

Palette and guarded register writes do nothing in DMG mode. Here, safe means a CGB-mode guard, not a PPU access wait or a critical section. Use LCD-off setup or a sufficiently short update in an accessible PPU phase. These functions do not wait for VBlank or protect a multi-byte update from interrupts.

BG/window and OBJ palettes are separate stores. These library writes enable index auto-increment and leave the index register changed. OBJ color index zero is transparent when rendering sprites, even though its palette bytes can be stored and read.

Usage example

c
cgb_bg_colors(3,2,tail_green,2); // Two color words; color 3 becomes green.
expect_color(0,14,0); expect_color(0,15,992);

color_count

On DMG, CGB MODE is 0, all triangles are black, the bank/flip attributes have no display effect, and the last two bottom cells are black squares. CGB MODE is 1 in CGB tests. Real hardware and LCD-on palette contention are not covered.

cgb_obj_palette

Replace all four colors of one sprite (OBJ) palette from four RGB15 words. This is the indexed range writer with start color zero and count four; it does not select that palette for any tile or sprite.

Syntax

c
void cgb_obj_palette(u8 palette_index, const u16* colors);

Parameters

palette_index

Palette number, 0–7; only the low three bits are used (& 7).

colors

Readable const u16* containing the requested color words. Data is consumed during the call, not queued. Keep the source and its ROM bank accessible; no bank switch is performed for you. A null pointer causes no writes.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

Palette and guarded register writes do nothing in DMG mode. Here, safe means a CGB-mode guard, not a PPU access wait or a critical section. Use LCD-off setup or a sufficiently short update in an accessible PPU phase. These functions do not wait for VBlank or protect a multi-byte update from interrupts.

BG/window and OBJ palettes are separate stores. These library writes enable index auto-increment and leave the index register changed. OBJ color index zero is transparent when rendering sprites, even though its palette bytes can be stored and read.

Usage example

c
cgb_obj_palette(4,blue_palette); // Exactly four words; OBJ color zero is transparent on screen.
expect_color(1,16,32767); expect_color(1,19,31744);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

CGB_RGB15

Pack RGB components into a u16: red occupies bits 0–4, green 5–9 and blue 10–14; bit 15 is zero. Each component is masked with 31, so oversized values wrap instead of being clamped. This computes a value without writing hardware, on DMG as well as CGB.

Syntax

c
#define CGB_RGB15(r5, g5, b5) ((u16)((u16)((r5) & 31) | ((u16)((g5) & 31) << 5) | ((u16)((b5) & 31) << 10)))

Parameters

r5, g5, b5

Red, green and blue components respectively, normally 0–31 each. Values are masked, not saturated; each argument appears once in the macro expansion.

Return value

The packed RGB15 value as u16, from 0 to 32767.

Usage example

c
if (CGB_RGB15(component,64,95)!=31775) failures++; // (31,0,31), not saturation.

cgb_tile.h — CGB tile numbers and attributes

KQ_CGB_ATTR

Build a complete CGB map attribute byte from palette, tile-data bank, horizontal reflection, vertical reflection and BG priority. Palette uses bits 0–2; the four Boolean fields set bits 3, 5, 6 and 7. Bit 4 stays zero.

Syntax

c
#define KQ_CGB_ATTR(palette, bank, xflip, yflip, priority) ((u8)(((palette) & KQ_CGB_ATTR_PAL_MASK) | ((bank) ? KQ_CGB_ATTR_BANK1 : 0) | ((xflip) ? KQ_CGB_ATTR_XFLIP : 0) | ((yflip) ? KQ_CGB_ATTR_YFLIP : 0) | ((priority) ? KQ_CGB_ATTR_PRIORITY : 0)))

Parameters

palette

Palette number, 0–7; only the low three bits are used (& 7).

bank, xflip, yflip, priority

Zero disables the field; any nonzero value enables it. In particular, 2 enables the field too: these macros test truth, not the low bit.

Return value

The attribute field or combined attribute byte as u8, with the bit layout described above.

Conditions and limits

These macros only compute u8 values; they perform no VRAM or register writes. Each argument occurs once. Apply the result with a CGB attribute-writing API or an explicit bank-1 map write. DMG does not display CGB map attributes.

Build bit 3 of a CGB map attribute: return 0x08 for any nonzero bank argument, otherwise 0. This chooses which VRAM bank supplies the displayed tile pattern. It does not write VBK or select the CPU's VRAM bank.

Build the horizontal-reflection flag: 0x20 when enabled is nonzero, otherwise 0. When used in a CGB map attribute, the eight pixels in each tile row are displayed in reverse order; the stored pattern is unchanged.

Build the vertical-reflection flag: 0x40 when enabled is nonzero, otherwise 0. In a CGB map attribute, it displays the tile's eight rows in reverse order without changing the stored pattern.

Build the BG-over-OBJ priority flag: 0x80 when enabled is nonzero, otherwise 0. With CGB master priority enabled (LCDC bit 0), nonzero BG color indices cover sprites. BG color index zero still lets sprites through; the flag does not make a tile opaque.

Usage example

c
attr=KQ_CGB_ATTR(10,0,2,2,0); // Palette 2, bank 0, both reflections: 0x62.
if (attr!=98 || KQ_CGB_ATTR(10,2,3,4,5)!=234) failures++;
cell(10,11,1,attr);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

KQ_CGB_ATTR_XFLIP_IF

Build the horizontal-reflection flag: 0x20 when enabled is nonzero, otherwise 0. When used in a CGB map attribute, the eight pixels in each tile row are displayed in reverse order; the stored pattern is unchanged.

Syntax

Parameters

enabled

Zero disables the field; any nonzero value enables it. In particular, 2 enables the field too: these macros test truth, not the low bit.

Return value

The attribute field or combined attribute byte as u8, with the bit layout described above.

Conditions and limits

These macros only compute u8 values; they perform no VRAM or register writes. Each argument occurs once. Apply the result with a CGB attribute-writing API or an explicit bank-1 map write. DMG does not display CGB map attributes.

This program teaches how palette contents affect the same tile pattern differently in BG and OBJ. Each triangle is 8 × 8 pixels; its top row has one pixel on the left, expanding to a full bottom row. At x = 16, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96, 112, the BG row at y = 24 is red, blue, green, red, blue, green, red. The OBJ row at y = 64 is blue, green, red, blue, green, red, blue. The columns use single-color, component, indexed-range, full-palette, absolute-range, canonical-register and alias-register writes, respectively.

Coordinates are screen pixels measured from the upper-left corner. Blank space and black text remain on white.

chain.h — Ring buffers for position history

Use ChainBody for articulated snakes or ropes, and Chain for recorded position history. Each body joint stores its current position and one of 16 headings; bends travel backward one joint per update. Body operations support wrapped fields, growth by tail duplication and corrections of up to two pixels per axis.

chain_wrap_delta

Calculate the shortest signed displacement from the current position to a target on an axis whose ends join. Use it for following or distance comparisons across a field edge.

Syntax

c
s16 chain_wrap_delta(u8 target, u8 current, u16 size);

Parameters

target

Target coordinate, in 0..size−1.

current

Current coordinate, in 0..size−1.

size

Wrapped axis length, 1..256: width for X, height for Y. This is a 16-bit argument so that 256 is representable.

Return value

Return the shortest displacement as s16: positive toward increasing coordinates, negative toward decreasing coordinates, or zero at the same position. Valid inputs produce −128..+128. With screen coordinates, rightward and downward displacements are positive.

Conditions and limits

Include chain.h and compile chain.c exactly once. No Chain or ChainBody initialization is required. The function only calculates a displacement; it does not alter coordinate arrays, joint counts or the screen.

The function does not validate or normalize inputs. Do not pass size=0, size>256, or coordinates at least as large as size. Wrap coordinates from a larger coordinate system into 0..size−1 before calling.

If both routes have the same length, retain the sign of the direct target−current displacement. With size=160, 0→80 returns +80 and 80→0 returns −80. With size=1, zero is the only valid coordinate and the result is zero.

Usage example

c
distances[0]=chain_wrap_delta(1,159,160);   // +2: cross the right edge.
    distances[1]=chain_wrap_delta(159,1,160);   // -2: cross the left edge.
    distances[2]=chain_wrap_delta(80,0,160);    // +80: keep the direct sign.
    distances[3]=chain_wrap_delta(0,80,160);    // -80: same-length routes.
    distances[4]=chain_wrap_delta(0,0,1);       // 0: the only valid position.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This lesson demonstrates wrapped coordinates. Each arrow goes from the current position to the target. It displays computed results +02/−02 for crossing a width-160 edge, +80/−80 for half a field, and +00 for width 1. The leading zero is decimal padding. The lesson does not draw or move an object.

kitaqgb/lib/chain.h:35

Declaration notes (original source)
Return target minus current along the shortest wrapped route.
Supply size 1..256 and coordinates in 0..size-1; inputs are not normalized.
Exactly half a field retains the direct displacement sign.

kitaqgb/lib/chain.c:98

c
s16 chain_wrap_delta(u8 target, u8 current, u16 size)
{
    s16 delta;
    s16 half;
    delta = (s16)((s16)target - (s16)current);
    half = (s16)(size >> 1);
    // At exactly half a field, retain the sign of the direct displacement.
    if (delta > half) delta = (s16)(delta - (s16)size);
    else if (delta < (s16)(0 - half)) delta = (s16)(delta + (s16)size);
    return delta;
}

kitaqgb/lib/chain.c:119

c
u8 chain_body_init(ChainBody* body, u8* x, u8* y, u8* heading, u8 capacity, u16 width, u16 height)
{
    if (body == 0) return 0;
    body->x = x;
    body->y = y;
    body->heading = heading;
    body->count = 0;
    body->capacity = 0;
    body->width = width;
    body->height = height;
    if (x == 0 || y == 0 || heading == 0 || capacity == 0) return 0;
    if (width == 0 || width > 256 || height == 0 || height > 256) return 0;
    body->capacity = capacity;
    return 1;
}

Build a straight initial pose by placing joints behind the specified head.

Head X coordinate, wrapped to the field width.

Head Y coordinate, wrapped to the field height.

Return 1 on success. A zero or excessive count, or a null body, returns 0 without changing the pose.

Conditions and limits

Include chain.h and compile chain.c exactly once. ChainBody holds each joint’s current position and heading. It is a separate state type from the Chain position-history ring.

Supply three separate writable arrays, x, y and heading, each containing capacity bytes. Keep them alive while the body is used. Index zero is the head, included in count. Do not alter storage pointers, capacity or field dimensions after initialization.

Headings use 16 clockwise sectors: 0=right, 4=down, 8=left, 12=up. Only the low four input bits are used. Screen coordinates increase rightward and downward; each dimension is 1..256 pixels.

Cardinal spacing is four pixels. Intermediate headings use integer vectors such as (4,1), (3,3) and (1,4), so Euclidean distance is not exactly four pixels. The initial pose may cross a field edge.

Declaration notes (original source)
Seed count joints in a straight pose behind the head; count includes the head.
Return 0 without changing the pose if count is zero or exceeds capacity.
Coordinates wrap to the playfield and headings are masked to 0..15.

kitaqgb/lib/chain.c:135

c
u8 chain_body_reset(ChainBody* body, u8 count, u8 head_x, u8 head_y, u8 heading)
{
    u8 i;
    u8 x;
    u8 y;
    s16 ox;
    s16 oy;
    if (body == 0) return 0;
    if (count == 0 || count > body->capacity) return 0;
    heading = (u8)(heading & 15);
    x = chain_body_wrap((s16)head_x, body->width);
    y = chain_body_wrap((s16)head_y, body->height);
    ox = chain_body_offset_x(heading);
    oy = chain_body_offset_y(heading);
    i = 0;
    while (i < count) {
        body->x[(__safe_index u8)i] = x;
        body->y[(__safe_index u8)i] = y;
        body->heading[(__safe_index u8)i] = heading;
        x = chain_body_wrap((s16)((s16)x - ox), body->width);
        y = chain_body_wrap((s16)((s16)y - oy), body->height);
        i = (u8)(i + 1);
    }
    body->count = count;
    return 1;
}
chain_body_step

Set the head pose and pull each joint gradually toward a socket behind its predecessor. Heading changes propagate by one joint per update.

Syntax

c
void chain_body_step(ChainBody* body, u8 head_x, u8 head_y, u8 heading);

Parameters

body

Target ChainBody; null is ignored. Except for initialization, pass an initialized state.

head_x

Head X coordinate, wrapped to the field width.

head_y

Head Y coordinate, wrapped to the field height.

heading

Head heading in the 16-sector system.

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

Include chain.h and compile chain.c exactly once. ChainBody holds each joint’s current position and heading. It is a separate state type from the Chain position-history ring.

Supply three separate writable arrays, x, y and heading, each containing capacity bytes. Keep them alive while the body is used. Index zero is the head, included in count. Do not alter storage pointers, capacity or field dimensions after initialization.

Headings use 16 clockwise sectors: 0=right, 4=down, 8=left, 12=up. Only the low four input bits are used. Screen coordinates increase rightward and downward; each dimension is 1..256 pixels.

Use the predecessor’s updated position to find the target socket, then compute the shortest wrapped displacement on each axis. A zero displacement does not move; magnitude 1..4 moves one pixel, and magnitude 5 or more moves two. At exactly half a field, retain the original displacement sign.

Pass each joint’s saved, pre-update heading to the next joint, allowing a bend to travel through the body. An empty body is unchanged.

The caller handles head velocity, acceleration, collisions, rendering and waiting. Normally update the head first, then call chain_body_step once per simulation tick. This is joint following, not a rigid-body or exact length-constraint solver.

Usage example

c
chain_body_step(&body,48,20,4); // The head turns down; only joint 1 receives 4.
    show_pose(8,34);
    for(step=1;step<4;step++) {
        chain_body_step(&body,48,(u8)(20+step),4);
    }
    // After four ticks, the new heading has reached joints 1 through 4.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

The image shows a straight body at the top, one update after a downward turn in the middle, and four updates after the turn below. Coordinates are drawn at twice their logical size. The bend travels backward from the head at the right. CGB and FC use red for the head, blue for the body and green for the tail; DMG uses black. Four settling updates separate the duplicated tail after growth. These are three views of the same eight joints, not one 24-joint body.

kitaqgb/lib/chain.h:62

Declaration notes (original source)
Install the caller's head pose, then pull joints from front to rear.
Each joint aims four pixels behind its updated predecessor and receives that
predecessor's OLD heading. Each axis moves 1 pixel, or 2 when error exceeds 4.
Call once per simulation tick; this does not advance head physics or render.

kitaqgb/lib/chain.c:162

c
void chain_body_step(ChainBody* body, u8 head_x, u8 head_y, u8 heading)
{
    u8 i;
    u8 previous;
    u8 pull;
    u8 old;
    u8 x;
    u8 y;
    u8 tx;
    u8 ty;
    s16 sx;
    s16 sy;
    if (body == 0) return;
    if (body->count == 0) return;
    heading = (u8)(heading & 15);
    body->x[0] = chain_body_wrap((s16)head_x, body->width);
    body->y[0] = chain_body_wrap((s16)head_y, body->height);
    body->heading[0] = heading;
    pull = heading;
    i = 1;
    while (i < body->count) {
        previous = (u8)(i - 1);
        old = body->heading[(__safe_index u8)i];
        x = body->x[(__safe_index u8)i];
        y = body->y[(__safe_index u8)i];
        tx = chain_body_wrap((s16)((s16)body->x[(__safe_index u8)previous] - chain_body_offset_x(pull)), body->width);
        ty = chain_body_wrap((s16)((s16)body->y[(__safe_index u8)previous] - chain_body_offset_y(pull)), body->height);
        sx = chain_body_correction(chain_wrap_delta(tx, x, body->width));
        sy = chain_body_correction(chain_wrap_delta(ty, y, body->height));
        body->heading[(__safe_index u8)i] = pull;
        body->x[(__safe_index u8)i] = chain_body_wrap((s16)((s16)x + sx), body->width);
        body->y[(__safe_index u8)i] = chain_body_wrap((s16)((s16)y + sy), body->height);
        // Save before overwriting: a bend advances by one joint per update.
        pull = old;
        i = (u8)(i + 1);
    }
}

kitaqgb/lib/chain.c:200

c
u8 chain_body_grow(ChainBody* body)
{
    u8 tail;
    u8 next;
    if (body == 0) return 0;
    next = body->count;
    if (next == 0 || next >= body->capacity) return 0;
    tail = (u8)(next - 1);
    body->x[(__safe_index u8)next] = body->x[(__safe_index u8)tail];
    body->y[(__safe_index u8)next] = body->y[(__safe_index u8)tail];
    body->heading[(__safe_index u8)next] = body->heading[(__safe_index u8)tail];
    body->count = (u8)(next + 1);
    return 1;
}

chain_get_segment

Read a stored position by its age in the history.

Syntax

c
u8 chain_get_segment(const Chain* chain, u8 index, ChainPoint* out);

Parameters

chain

Pointer to the initialized Chain.

index

Point age: 0 is newest and count - 1 is oldest retained.

out

Separate writable ChainPoint for the result; null causes failure.

Return value

Returns 1 on success or 0 for an invalid request. A non-null out is cleared to (0,0) before validation.

Conditions and limits

Do not alias out with the backing array or Chain: clearing the output would destroy source data. The caller owns both Chain and its point array and must keep them alive. Use a capacity no greater than 128 to avoid overflow in the reader’s eight-bit index addition.

Usage example

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.
