    if ((s16)(b.y + b.h) <= a.y) return 0;
    return 1;
}

input.h — Button state, press, release and repeat

Use this library to separate continuous movement (input_down), one-shot actions (input_pressed), stopping on release (input_released) and menu repetition (input_repeat). Initialize once, update once per input tick, then query as often as needed. btn_down, btn_pressed, btn_released and btn_repeat are aliases for those four queries.

Shared masks: BTN_RIGHT=0x01, BTN_LEFT=0x02, BTN_UP=0x04, BTN_DOWN=0x08, BTN_A=0x10, BTN_B=0x20, BTN_SELECT=0x40, BTN_START=0x80. A set bit means held. This layout applies to input_* on both GB and FC; raw FC pad functions use a different order.

Repeat timing counts updates, not milliseconds. A new press emits immediately. With defaults INPUT_REPEAT_DELAY=18 and INPUT_REPEAT_RATE=5, the next pulse is 19 updates later, followed by pulses every 6 updates. Each button has its own counter. Define these macros consistently when compiling input.c; changing only the caller's header does not reconfigure the library.

input_current

Return the complete held-button mask from the most recent input update.

Return value

An 8-bit mask in the shared BTN_* layout. Several buttons may be set simultaneously; 0 means none.

Conditions and limits

Getters observe the most recent input_update() without polling, consuming an edge or advancing a repeat timer. Repeated getter calls in the same tick give the same answer. Calling input_update() twice while a button stays down clears its press edge on the second call.

input_update

Save the current mask as the previous mask, read the Game Boy buttons through __readpadex, calculate release edges, and advance one independent repeat timer per button. Call once per game input tick before querying the cached state.

Syntax

c
void input_update();

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

Shared masks: BTN_RIGHT=0x01, BTN_LEFT=0x02, BTN_UP=0x04, BTN_DOWN=0x08, BTN_A=0x10, BTN_B=0x20, BTN_SELECT=0x40, BTN_START=0x80. A set bit means held. This layout applies to input_* on both GB and FC; raw FC pad functions use a different order.

Repeat timing counts updates, not milliseconds. A new press emits immediately. With defaults INPUT_REPEAT_DELAY=18 and INPUT_REPEAT_RATE=5, the next pulse is 19 updates later, followed by pulses every 6 updates. Each button has its own counter. Define these macros consistently when compiling input.c; changing only the caller's header does not reconfigure the library.

Usage example

c
input_update(); // One update per input tick, followed by any number of queries.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

FIRST DOWN, FIRST PRESS and FIRST REPEAT are 1; FIRST CURRENT is 16. HELD TICKS is 40, PRESS COUNT is 1 and REPEAT COUNT is 5. On release, RELEASE is 1, LAST CURRENT is 0 and LAST PREVIOUS is 16. .\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaqgb\lib\input.c .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\input_edges.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\input_edges.gb --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --no-disasm --no-cache
Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/input.h:34

Declaration notes (original source)
Sample input once per game tick and derive press, release and repeat masks.
Repeat delays are measured in calls to this function, not elapsed wall-clock time.

kitaqgb/lib/input.c:35

c
void input_update()
{
    u8 i;
    u16 kt;

    kq_input_prev_keys = kq_input_keys;
    // The intrinsic packs held buttons in the low byte and new presses in the high byte.
    kt = __readpadex(kq_input_prev_keys);
    kq_input_keys = (u8)kt;
    kq_input_press_keys = (u8)(kt >> 8);
    kq_input_release_keys = (u8)(kq_input_prev_keys & (u8)(kq_input_keys ^ 0xFF));
    kq_input_repeat_keys = kq_input_press_keys;

    i = 0;
    while (i < 8) {
        u8 mask = input_mask_for_index(i);
        if ((kq_input_keys & mask) != 0) {
            if ((kq_input_press_keys & mask) != 0) {
                input_repeat_timer[i] = INPUT_REPEAT_DELAY;
            } else if (input_repeat_timer[i] != 0) {
                input_repeat_timer[i]--;
            } else {
                kq_input_repeat_keys = (u8)(kq_input_repeat_keys | mask);
                input_repeat_timer[i] = INPUT_REPEAT_RATE;
            }
        } else {
            input_repeat_timer[i] = INPUT_REPEAT_DELAY;
        }
        i++;
    }
}

link.h — Serial communication and logical packets

The library provides three layers: byte exchanges, packets of up to 24 bytes, and peer-specific queues. Start with BYTE MASTER/SLAVE, then PACKET, then LINK4 to learn clock ownership and receive readiness. Include the hardware-register unit, link.c and link_packet.c exactly once in a program; gb_link_example.h supplies that order.

Link4 manages logical host slot 0 and peer slots 1–3. SelectPeer does not send a command that switches physical wiring. KOKURA’s link4 topology follows the selected peer through compiler metadata. Use LinkDmg07 for the physical DMG-07 protocol.

Keep polling on both endpoints. A timeout counts 90 calls without progress, not hardware frames. Sending 0xFF solely to clock an ACK does not extend that deadline; transmission allows at most three attempts. Retries can deliver duplicates, so add application-level identifiers when a command must run exactly once.

Link4_BeginTransferTo

Select a destination, then start one byte exchange.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall Link4_BeginTransferTo(u8 peer_slot, u8 out);

Parameters

peer_slot

Configured remote slot: 1..slot_count−1 from the host, or 0 from a peer.

out

Outgoing eight-bit value.

Return value

Returns the first selection/start error, or 0 on success.

Conditions and limits

Link4 manages logical host slot 0 and peer slots 1–3. SelectPeer does not send a command that switches physical wiring. KOKURA’s link4 topology follows the selected peer through compiler metadata. Use LinkDmg07 for the physical DMG-07 protocol.

Error codes are 0=none, 1=busy, 2=timeout, 3=receive overflow, 4=invalid configuration/protocol and 5=an ACK timeout with a disconnect-like response. Start/configuration calls succeed with 0; receive/pop calls succeed with 1. Successful calls do not clear a latched error.

Link4 copies each received byte to both the ordinary ring and a per-peer ring. Reading one does not drain the other. Packet polling consumes the ordinary ring; regularly discard unused per-peer raw bytes as well to prevent overflow.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

Run these PowerShell commands from the parent containing kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs. Build every participating ROM before launching the linked session. For Link4, retain the generated symbol metadata beside the ROMs. For DMG runs, change --cgb=cgb to --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb to --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
result[6+slot]=Link4_BeginTransferTo(slot,16+slot);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Connect all four ROMs with KOKURA’s link4 topology. The host receives 161/162/163 from peers 1/2/3 and shows LAST PEER=3. It then sends commands 65/66/67 with payload 7/42/255; verify those values on each peer’s screen too.

u8 __stackcall Link4_BeginTransferTo(u8 peer_slot, u8 out) {

Link4_GetLastRxPeer

Read the peer attributed to the last completed byte.

Syntax

c
u8 Link4_GetLastRxPeer();

Return value

Host returns the selected peer and a peer returns 0; before reception returns 255.

Conditions and limits

Link4 manages logical host slot 0 and peer slots 1–3. SelectPeer does not send a command that switches physical wiring. KOKURA’s link4 topology follows the selected peer through compiler metadata. Use LinkDmg07 for the physical DMG-07 protocol.

These are configuration/history getters. They do not detect physical connections, query every peer or wait for transfer completion.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

Run these PowerShell commands from the parent containing kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs. Build every participating ROM before launching the linked session. For Link4, retain the generated symbol metadata beside the ROMs. For DMG runs, change --cgb=cgb to --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb to --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
result[19]=Link4_GetLastRxPeer();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Connect all four ROMs with KOKURA’s link4 topology. The host receives 161/162/163 from peers 1/2/3 and shows LAST PEER=3. It then sends commands 65/66/67 with payload 7/42/255; verify those values on each peer’s screen too.

Link4_HasByteFrom

Inspect unread data in one peer’s receive ring.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall Link4_HasByteFrom(u8 peer_slot);

Parameters

peer_slot

Configured remote slot: 1..slot_count−1 from the host, or 0 from a peer.

Return value

Returns 1 for queued data, 0 for empty/invalid peer.

Conditions and limits

An eight-entry receive ring holds seven bytes. A full ring drops the new byte and latches error 3. A received zero byte is valid data.

Link4 copies each received byte to both the ordinary ring and a per-peer ring. Reading one does not drain the other. Packet polling consumes the ordinary ring; regularly discard unused per-peer raw bytes as well to prevent overflow.

This query does not poll hardware; an invalid peer does not change the error latch.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

Run these PowerShell commands from the parent containing kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs. Build every participating ROM before launching the linked session. For Link4, retain the generated symbol metadata beside the ROMs. For DMG runs, change --cgb=cgb to --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb to --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
result[9+slot]=Link4_HasByteFrom(slot);value=0;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Connect all four ROMs with KOKURA’s link4 topology. The host receives 161/162/163 from peers 1/2/3 and shows LAST PEER=3. It then sends commands 65/66/67 with payload 7/42/255; verify those values on each peer’s screen too.

Link4_HasPacketFrom

Inspect the completed-packet mailbox for one remote slot.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall Link4_HasPacketFrom(u8 peer_slot);

Parameters

peer_slot

Configured remote slot: 1..slot_count−1 from the host, or 0 from a peer.

Return value

Returns 1 for an unread packet, 0 for empty/invalid peer.

Conditions and limits

Link4 manages logical host slot 0 and peer slots 1–3. SelectPeer does not send a command that switches physical wiring. KOKURA’s link4 topology follows the selected peer through compiler metadata. Use LinkDmg07 for the physical DMG-07 protocol.

A packet contains 0xA5, command, length, 0–24 payload bytes and an XOR checksum. The response is 0x79 (ACK, accepted) or 0x1F (NAK, rejected). The checksum XORs the command, length and payload. Each machine has one shared packet mailbox; Link4 additionally has one mailbox per peer.

This query does not poll hardware; an invalid peer does not change the error latch.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

Usage example

c

Expected result

Link4_InitHost

Initialize a logical host with two to four slots and select peer 1.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall Link4_InitHost(u8 slot_count);

Parameters

slot_count

Number of slots including the host, 2..4.

Return value

Returns 0 for valid configuration, 4 for an invalid slot count.

Conditions and limits

Initialization discards byte queues, packets, peer selection and errors, and disables the transfer and serial IRQ source. It does not preserve an in-flight exchange.

Link4 manages logical host slot 0 and peer slots 1–3. SelectPeer does not send a command that switches physical wiring. KOKURA’s link4 topology follows the selected peer through compiler metadata. Use LinkDmg07 for the physical DMG-07 protocol.

Internal critical sections track software nesting depth. Leaving the outer section enables CPU interrupts, so do not assume that a previously disabled IME state is preserved.

Initialization occurs before validation. A failed call still discards the previous topology and unread data.

Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/link.h:108

Declaration notes (original source)
Cooperative 4-player adapter helpers.

This layer models the common host-selected adapter pattern:
- Slot 0 is always the host.
- The host selects one active peer slot at a time.
- Packet mailboxes stay one-deep per peer.
- The original Link_* API remains available for normal 2-player projects.
Reset as master, validate slot count and select logical peer one. Invalid configuration still discards old link state.

kitaqgb/lib/link.c:489

c
u8 __stackcall Link4_InitHost(u8 slot_count) {
    u8 err;

    Link_InitMaster();
    err = Link4_ValidateConfig(LINK4_MODE_HOST, LINK4_HOST_SLOT, slot_count);
    if (err != LINK_ERR_NONE) {
        Link_SetErrorInternal(err);
        return err;
    }

    Link4_ApplyConfig(LINK4_MODE_HOST, LINK4_HOST_SLOT, slot_count);
    return LINK_ERR_NONE;
}

Link4_PollPacket

Advance the shared packet engine once for the currently selected peer.

Syntax

c
void Link4_PollPacket();

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

Link4 manages logical host slot 0 and peer slots 1–3. SelectPeer does not send a command that switches physical wiring. KOKURA’s link4 topology follows the selected peer through compiler metadata. Use LinkDmg07 for the physical DMG-07 protocol.

A packet contains 0xA5, command, length, 0–24 payload bytes and an XOR checksum. The response is 0x79 (ACK, accepted) or 0x1F (NAK, rejected). The checksum XORs the command, length and payload. Each machine has one shared packet mailbox; Link4 additionally has one mailbox per peer.

Keep polling on both endpoints. A timeout counts 90 calls without progress, not hardware frames. Sending 0xFF solely to clock an ACK does not extend that deadline; transmission allows at most three attempts. Retries can deliver duplicates, so add application-level identifiers when a command must run exactly once.

Link4 copies each received byte to both the ordinary ring and a per-peer ring. Reading one does not drain the other. Packet polling consumes the ordinary ring; regularly discard unused per-peer raw bytes as well to prevent overflow.

Does not rotate across all slots. Change peers only after the exchange has finished and selection is permitted.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

Run these PowerShell commands from the parent containing kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs. Build every participating ROM before launching the linked session. For Link4, retain the generated symbol metadata beside the ROMs. For DMG runs, change --cgb=cgb to --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb to --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
for(i=0;i<50;i++){Link4_PollPacket();while(Link4_TryReadByteFrom(slot,0)){}m_wait();}

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Connect all four ROMs with KOKURA’s link4 topology. The host receives 161/162/163 from peers 1/2/3 and shows LAST PEER=3. It then sends commands 65/66/67 with payload 7/42/255; verify those values on each peer’s screen too.

Link4_ReadPacketFrom

Copy a packet from a specific peer and consume its mailbox.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall Link4_ReadPacketFrom(u8 peer_slot, u8 *cmd, u8 *len, u8 *dst);

Parameters

peer_slot

Configured remote slot: 1..slot_count−1 from the host, or 0 from a peer.

cmd

Writable command byte; null omits it.

len

Writable length byte, 0..24; null omits it.

dst

Writable payload buffer with room for 24 bytes; null discards the payload.

Return value

Returns 1 when consumed, 0 for empty/invalid peer.

Conditions and limits

There is no destination-capacity parameter. Provide 24 writable bytes when using dst. cmd, len and dst may independently be null. Serialize mailbox inspection and consumption against other code and interrupts.

Clears the shared mailbox only when it refers to this same peer’s packet. Unread packets from other peers remain available.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

Run these PowerShell commands from the parent containing kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs. Build every participating ROM before launching the linked session. For Link4, retain the generated symbol metadata beside the ROMs. For DMG runs, change --cgb=cgb to --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb to --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
result[9]=Link4_HasPacketFrom(0);result[10]=Link4_ReadPacketFrom(0,&cmd,&len,data);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

As peer 1 of four slots, expect HOST BYTE=17, COMMAND=65, LENGTH=3 and PAYLOAD 2=42. CONSUMED=0 is the host mailbox flag after consumption.

c
u8 __stackcall Link4_ReadPacketFrom(u8 peer_slot, u8 *cmd, u8 *len, u8 *dst) {
    u8 i;
    u8 offset;

    if (Link4_PacketPeerReady(peer_slot) == 0) return 0;

    if (cmd != 0) *cmd = Link4_ReceivedPacketCmd[(__safe_index u8)peer_slot];
    if (len != 0) *len = Link4_ReceivedPacketLen[(__safe_index u8)peer_slot];

    if (dst != 0) {
        for (i = 0; i < Link4_ReceivedPacketLen[(__safe_index u8)peer_slot]; ++i) {
            offset = Link4_PacketOffset(peer_slot, i);
            dst[(__safe_index u8)i] = Link4_ReceivedPacketBuf[(__safe_index u8)offset];
        }
    }

    Link4_ReceivedPacketReady[(__safe_index u8)peer_slot] = 0;
    if (Link4_LastPacketPeer == peer_slot) {
        Link_ReceivedPacketReady = 0;
        Link4_LastPacketPeer = LINK4_INVALID_SLOT;
    }
    return 1;
}
Link4_SelectPeer

Poll completion and change the logical destination only while idle.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall Link4_SelectPeer(u8 peer_slot);

Parameters

peer_slot

Configured remote slot: 1..slot_count−1 from the host, or 0 from a peer.

Return value

Returns 0 on selection, 1 for busy byte/packet/ACK state, or 4 for an unconfigured/invalid peer.

Conditions and limits

Link4 manages logical host slot 0 and peer slots 1–3. SelectPeer does not send a command that switches physical wiring. KOKURA’s link4 topology follows the selected peer through compiler metadata. Use LinkDmg07 for the physical DMG-07 protocol.

Error codes are 0=none, 1=busy, 2=timeout, 3=receive overflow, 4=invalid configuration/protocol and 5=an ACK timeout with a disconnect-like response. Start/configuration calls succeed with 0; receive/pop calls succeed with 1. Successful calls do not clear a latched error.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

kitaqgb/lib/link.c:552

c
u8 __stackcall Link4_SelectPeer(u8 peer_slot) {
    Link_Poll();

    if (Link4_IsEnabledInternal() == 0) {
        Link_SetErrorInternal(LINK_ERR_PROTOCOL);
        return LINK_ERR_PROTOCOL;
    }

    if (Link_Busy != 0 || Link_PacketState != LINK_PKT_STATE_IDLE || Link_PendingAck != 0) {
        Link_SetErrorInternal(LINK_ERR_BUSY);
        return LINK_ERR_BUSY;
    }

    if (Link4_ModeState == LINK4_MODE_HOST) {
        if (Link4_IsValidRemoteSlotInternal(peer_slot) == 0) {
            Link_SetErrorInternal(LINK_ERR_PROTOCOL);
            return LINK_ERR_PROTOCOL;
        }
        Link4_SelectedPeer = peer_slot;
        return LINK_ERR_NONE;
    }

    if (Link4_ModeState == LINK4_MODE_PEER && peer_slot == LINK4_HOST_SLOT) {
        Link4_SelectedPeer = LINK4_HOST_SLOT;
        return LINK_ERR_NONE;
    }

    Link_SetErrorInternal(LINK_ERR_PROTOCOL);
    return LINK_ERR_PROTOCOL;
}
Link4_SendPacketTo

Select a logical peer, copy the packet and schedule its transmission.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall Link4_SendPacketTo(u8 peer_slot, const u8 *data, u8 len, u8 cmd);

Parameters

peer_slot

Configured remote slot: 1..slot_count−1 from the host, or 0 from a peer.

data

Readable source of len bytes; may be null only when len is zero.

len

Payload length in bytes, 0..24.

cmd

Application-defined eight-bit command.

Return value

Returns the first selection/queueing error; 0 means accepted.

Conditions and limits

Link4 manages logical host slot 0 and peer slots 1–3. SelectPeer does not send a command that switches physical wiring. KOKURA’s link4 topology follows the selected peer through compiler metadata. Use LinkDmg07 for the physical DMG-07 protocol.

Error codes are 0=none, 1=busy, 2=timeout, 3=receive overflow, 4=invalid configuration/protocol and 5=an ACK timeout with a disconnect-like response. Start/configuration calls succeed with 0; receive/pop calls succeed with 1. Successful calls do not clear a latched error.

A packet contains 0xA5, command, length, 0–24 payload bytes and an XOR checksum. The response is 0x79 (ACK, accepted) or 0x1F (NAK, rejected). The checksum XORs the command, length and payload. Each machine has one shared packet mailbox; Link4 additionally has one mailbox per peer.

Keep polling on both endpoints. A timeout counts 90 calls without progress, not hardware frames. Sending 0xFF solely to clock an ACK does not extend that deadline; transmission allows at most three attempts. Retries can deliver duplicates, so add application-level identifiers when a command must run exactly once.

Link4 copies each received byte to both the ordinary ring and a per-peer ring. Reading one does not drain the other. Packet polling consumes the ordinary ring; regularly discard unused per-peer raw bytes as well to prevent overflow.

Selection happens before payload validation; a rejected payload can still leave the new destination selected.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

Link4_TryReadByteAny

Scan remote slots in ascending order and pop the first available byte.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall Link4_TryReadByteAny(u8 *peer_slot, u8 *out);

Parameters

peer_slot

Writable origin-slot byte; null omits the origin output.

out

Writable byte destination; null discards the byte.

Return value

Returns 1 on receipt, otherwise 0.

Conditions and limits

An eight-entry receive ring holds seven bytes. A full ring drops the new byte and latches error 3. A received zero byte is valid data.

Link4 copies each received byte to both the ordinary ring and a per-peer ring. Reading one does not drain the other. Packet polling consumes the ordinary ring; regularly discard unused per-peer raw bytes as well to prevent overflow.

Internal critical sections track software nesting depth. Leaving the outer section enables CPU interrupts, so do not assume that a previously disabled IME state is preserved.

Skips the local slot. Continuously queued lower slots take priority; use per-peer reads when round-robin fairness is required.

kitaqgb/lib/link.h:136

Declaration notes (original source)
Scan remote rings in increasing slot order and return the first available
byte. Null output pointers are allowed; lower slots have polling priority.

kitaqgb/lib/link.c:604

c
u8 __stackcall Link4_TryReadByteAny(u8 *peer_slot, u8 *out) {
    u8 slot;

    if (Link4_IsEnabledInternal() == 0) return 0;

    for (slot = 0; slot < Link4_SlotCount; ++slot) {
        if (slot != Link4_LocalSlot) {
            if (Link4_PopRxByte(slot, out) != 0) {
                if (peer_slot != 0) *peer_slot = slot;
                return 1;
            }
        }
    }

    return 0;
}

peer_slot

Configured remote slot: 1..slot_count−1 from the host, or 0 from a peer.

out

Writable byte destination; null discards the byte.

Return value

Returns 1 on a pop; empty/invalid peer returns 0 and preserves out.

Conditions and limits

An eight-entry receive ring holds seven bytes. A full ring drops the new byte and latches error 3. A received zero byte is valid data.

Link4 copies each received byte to both the ordinary ring and a per-peer ring. Reading one does not drain the other. Packet polling consumes the ordinary ring; regularly discard unused per-peer raw bytes as well to prevent overflow.

Internal critical sections track software nesting depth. Leaving the outer section enables CPU interrupts, so do not assume that a previously disabled IME state is preserved.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

Run these PowerShell commands from the parent containing kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs. Build every participating ROM before launching the linked session. For Link4, retain the generated symbol metadata beside the ROMs. For DMG runs, change --cgb=cgb to --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb to --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
if(slot==1)result[13]=Link4_TryReadByteFrom(slot,&value);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Connect all four ROMs with KOKURA’s link4 topology. The host receives 161/162/163 from peers 1/2/3 and shows LAST PEER=3. It then sends commands 65/66/67 with payload 7/42/255; verify those values on each peer’s screen too.

Link_BeginTransfer

Load SB and start or arm one full-duplex byte exchange.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall Link_BeginTransfer(u8 out);

Parameters

out

Eight-bit outgoing value; every exchange sends a byte even if only reception matters.

Return value

Returns 0 when started/armed, or 1 if already busy.

Conditions and limits

Each machine has one shared link state. Byte exchanges are full duplex: one side supplies the internal clock and the other uses external clocks. Normal speed takes 512 clocks per bit; CGB fast speed takes 16.

Error codes are 0=none, 1=busy, 2=timeout, 3=receive overflow, 4=invalid configuration/protocol and 5=an ACK timeout with a disconnect-like response. Start/configuration calls succeed with 0; receive/pop calls succeed with 1. Successful calls do not clear a latched error.

An external-clock endpoint waits for the other side to supply clocks. A busy rejection does not replace the byte already in flight.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

Run these PowerShell commands from the parent containing kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs. Build every participating ROM before launching the linked session. For Link4, retain the generated symbol metadata beside the ROMs. For DMG runs, change --cgb=cgb to --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb to --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
lesson_delay(12);result[0]=Link_BeginTransfer(42);value=0;result[1]=Link_WaitByte(8,&value);result[2]=value;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Connect to BYTE SLAVE. Send 42 and receive 99, then exchange zero in both directions. RECEIVED=1, PEER BYTE=99, ZERO READY=1 and ZERO BYTE=0 distinguish valid zero data from no data. Two CGB instances use fast clocks for the second exchange.

kitaqgb/lib/link.h:66

Declaration notes (original source)
Start one full-duplex byte exchange, or return BUSY without replacing an
active transfer. Slave mode arms reception and waits for external clocks.

kitaqgb/lib/link.c:362

c
u8 __stackcall Link_BeginTransfer(u8 out) {
    u8 sc = LINK_SC_START;

    if (Link_Busy != 0) {
        Link_SetErrorInternal(LINK_ERR_BUSY);
        return LINK_ERR_BUSY;
    }

    LinkHw_WriteSB(out);
    Link_LastTx = out;
    Link4_LastTxPeer = Link4_CurrentTransferPeerInternal();
    Link_Busy = 1;
    LinkHw_WriteIF((u8)(LinkHw_ReadIF() & (u8)~LINK_IF_SERIAL));

    if (Link_Mode == LINK_MODE_MASTER) {
        sc = (u8)(sc | LINK_SC_INTERNAL);
        if (Link_FastClock != 0) sc = (u8)(sc | LINK_SC_FAST);
    }

    LinkHw_WriteSC(sc);
    return LINK_ERR_NONE;
}
Link_Cancel

Stop the active or externally clocked byte transfer.

Syntax

c
void Link_Cancel();

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

Internal critical sections track software nesting depth. Leaving the outer section enables CPU interrupts, so do not assume that a previously disabled IME state is preserved.

kitaqgb/lib/link.h:71

Declaration notes (original source)
Stop the hardware transfer under interrupt protection. Queued receive bytes
and packet-layer state remain available; this is not a full protocol reset.

kitaqgb/lib/link.c:396

c
void Link_Cancel() {
    u8 tok = __critical_enter();

    Link_Busy = 0;
    LinkHw_WriteSC(0x00);
    LinkHw_WriteIF((u8)(LinkHw_ReadIF() & (u8)~LINK_IF_SERIAL));

    __critical_leave(tok);
}

Link_HasPacket

Inspect the shared completed-packet mailbox.

Syntax

c
u8 Link_HasPacket();

Return value

Returns 1 for an unread packet, otherwise 0.

Conditions and limits

A packet contains 0xA5, command, length, 0–24 payload bytes and an XOR checksum. The response is 0x79 (ACK, accepted) or 0x1F (NAK, rejected). The checksum XORs the command, length and payload. Each machine has one shared packet mailbox; Link4 additionally has one mailbox per peer.

Reads a flag without progressing the protocol. It does not indicate whether the sender has received its ACK.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

Run these PowerShell commands from the parent containing kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs. Build every participating ROM before launching the linked session. For Link4, retain the generated symbol metadata beside the ROMs. For DMG runs, change --cgb=cgb to --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb to --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Connect to PACKET MASTER and check COMMAND=49, LENGTH=3 and payload 7/42/255. CONSUMED=0 after ReadPacket means that the mailbox is now empty.

Link_InitCommon

Reset the shared link state to its external-clock default.

Syntax

c
void Link_InitCommon();

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

Each machine has one shared link state. Byte exchanges are full duplex: one side supplies the internal clock and the other uses external clocks. Normal speed takes 512 clocks per bit; CGB fast speed takes 16.

Initialization discards byte queues, packets, peer selection and errors, and disables the transfer and serial IRQ source. It does not preserve an in-flight exchange.

Internal critical sections track software nesting depth. Leaving the outer section enables CPU interrupts, so do not assume that a previously disabled IME state is preserved.

Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/link.h:43

Declaration notes (original source)
Reset byte queues, packet mailboxes, cooperative-peer state and errors, then
disable serial transfers and serial IRQ delivery. Existing data is discarded.

kitaqgb/lib/link.c:243

c
void Link_InitCommon() {
    u8 i;

    Link_Mode = LINK_MODE_SLAVE;
    Link_UseInterrupt = 0;
    Link_FastClock = LINK_CLOCK_NORMAL;
    Link_Busy = 0;
    Link_LastRx = 0xFF;
    Link_LastTx = 0xFF;
    Link_RxReady = 0;
    Link_LastErrorCode = LINK_ERR_NONE;
    Link_PacketState = LINK_PKT_STATE_IDLE;
    Link_TxSeq = 0;
    Link_RxSeq = 0;
    Link4_ModeState = LINK4_MODE_NONE;
    Link4_LocalSlot = LINK4_HOST_SLOT;
    Link4_SlotCount = 0;
    Link4_SelectedPeer = LINK4_INVALID_SLOT;
    Link4_LastRxPeer = LINK4_INVALID_SLOT;
    Link4_LastTxPeer = LINK4_INVALID_SLOT;
    Link4_LastPacketPeer = LINK4_INVALID_SLOT;

    Link_RxHead = 0;
    Link_RxTail = 0;
    Link_TxHead = 0;
    Link_TxTail = 0;

    Link_CurrentPacketCmd = 0;
    Link_CurrentPacketLen = 0;
    Link_CurrentPacketChecksum = 0;
    Link_PendingAck = 0;

    Link_ReceivedPacketReady = 0;
    Link_ReceivedPacketCmd = 0;
    Link_ReceivedPacketLen = 0;
    Link_ReceivedPacketChecksum = 0;
    Link_PacketRetryCount = 0;
    Link_PacketTimer = 0;

    for (i = 0; i < LINK_RX_QUEUE_SIZE; ++i) Link_RxQueue[(__safe_index u8)i] = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < LINK_TX_QUEUE_SIZE; ++i) Link_TxQueue[(__safe_index u8)i] = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < LINK4_MAX_PLAYERS; ++i) {
        Link4_RxHead[(__safe_index u8)i] = 0;
        Link4_RxTail[(__safe_index u8)i] = 0;
        Link4_ReceivedPacketReady[(__safe_index u8)i] = 0;
        Link4_ReceivedPacketCmd[(__safe_index u8)i] = 0;
        Link4_ReceivedPacketLen[(__safe_index u8)i] = 0;
    }
    for (i = 0; i < (u8)(LINK4_MAX_PLAYERS * LINK_RX_QUEUE_SIZE); ++i) {
        Link4_RxQueue[(__safe_index u8)i] = 0;
    }
    for (i = 0; i < LINK_PKT_MAX_PAYLOAD; ++i) {
        Link_CurrentPacketBuf[(__safe_index u8)i] = 0;
        Link_ReceivedPacketBuf[(__safe_index u8)i] = 0;
    }
    for (i = 0; i < (u8)(LINK4_MAX_PLAYERS * LINK_PKT_MAX_PAYLOAD); ++i) {
        Link4_ReceivedPacketBuf[(__safe_index u8)i] = 0;
    }

    LinkHw_WriteSB(0xFF);
    LinkHw_WriteSC(0x00);
    LinkHw_WriteIF((u8)(LinkHw_ReadIF() & (u8)~LINK_IF_SERIAL));
    Link_SetSerialInterruptEnabled(0);
}

Link_InitSlave

Reset state and select externally clocked communication.

Syntax

c
void Link_InitSlave();

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

Each machine has one shared link state. Byte exchanges are full duplex: one side supplies the internal clock and the other uses external clocks. Normal speed takes 512 clocks per bit; CGB fast speed takes 16.

Initialization discards byte queues, packets, peer selection and errors, and disables the transfer and serial IRQ source. It does not preserve an in-flight exchange.

Internal critical sections track software nesting depth. Leaving the outer section enables CPU interrupts, so do not assume that a previously disabled IME state is preserved.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

Run these PowerShell commands from the parent containing kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs. Build every participating ROM before launching the linked session. For Link4, retain the generated symbol metadata beside the ROMs. For DMG runs, change --cgb=cgb to --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb to --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
Link_InitSlave();result[0]=Link_BeginTransfer(99);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

BYTE MASTER supplies the clocks. Expect PEER BYTE=42, ZERO READY=1 and ZERO BYTE=0. EMPTY READ is also zero afterwards, which is why readiness or TryRead’s return value is needed to distinguish an empty queue.

Link_IsBusy

Poll once for completion, then report whether an exchange remains active.

Syntax

c
u8 Link_IsBusy();

Return value

Returns 1 while busy, otherwise 0.

Conditions and limits

An eight-entry receive ring holds seven bytes. A full ring drops the new byte and latches error 3. A received zero byte is valid data.

This is not a passive query: a completed SB byte is enqueued, which can change readiness and error state.

Link_LastError

Read the most recently latched link error without clearing it.

Syntax

c
u8 Link_LastError();

Return value

Returns the current error code, 0..5.

Conditions and limits

Error codes are 0=none, 1=busy, 2=timeout, 3=receive overflow, 4=invalid configuration/protocol and 5=an ACK timeout with a disconnect-like response. Start/configuration calls succeed with 0; receive/pop calls succeed with 1. Successful calls do not clear a latched error.

Collect a completed byte from a handler that has identified a serial request.

Syntax

c

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

An eight-entry receive ring holds seven bytes. A full ring drops the new byte and latches error 3. A received zero byte is valid data.

Internal critical sections track software nesting depth. Leaving the outer section enables CPU interrupts, so do not assume that a previously disabled IME state is preserved.

Link_PollPacket

Parse received bytes, start the next outgoing byte or ACK, and advance timeout/retry state.

Syntax

c
void Link_PollPacket();

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

A packet contains 0xA5, command, length, 0–24 payload bytes and an XOR checksum. The response is 0x79 (ACK, accepted) or 0x1F (NAK, rejected). The checksum XORs the command, length and payload. Each machine has one shared packet mailbox; Link4 additionally has one mailbox per peer.

Keep polling on both endpoints. A timeout counts 90 calls without progress, not hardware frames. Sending 0xFF solely to clock an ACK does not extend that deadline; transmission allows at most three attempts. Retries can deliver duplicates, so add application-level identifiers when a command must run exactly once.

Raw ReadByte-style calls consume the same ordinary ring and can steal part of a packet. Do not mix raw reads with packet reception.

Link4 copies each received byte to both the ordinary ring and a per-peer ring. Reading one does not drain the other. Packet polling consumes the ordinary ring; regularly discard unused per-peer raw bytes as well to prevent overflow.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

kitaqgb/lib/link.h:92

Declaration notes (original source)
Drain received bytes, advance one outgoing exchange and update the retry
timer. Timeout ticks count calls without progress, not hardware frames; call
with a controlled cadence and avoid mixing raw reads with packet consumption.

kitaqgb/lib/link_packet.c:400

c
void Link_PollPacket() {
    u8 progress = 0;
    u8 previous_state;
    u8 value = 0;

    Link_Poll();

    if (Link_PacketState == LINK_PKT_STATE_ERROR) {
        Link_PacketGoIdle();
        return;
    }

    while (Link_TryReadByte(&value) != 0) {
        if (Link_PacketConsumeByte(value) != 0) progress = 1;
    }

    if (Link_PacketState == LINK_PKT_STATE_SEND_ACK) {
        if (Link_PacketStartAckTransfer() != 0) progress = 1;
    } else if (Link_PacketIsSendState() != 0) {
        // Clocking an ACK is not protocol progress: a missing peer must time out.
        previous_state = Link_PacketState;
        if (Link_PacketStartNextTransfer() != 0 && previous_state != LINK_PKT_STATE_WAIT_ACK) progress = 1;
    } else {
        if (Link_PacketStartReceiveTransfer() != 0) progress = 1;
    }

    if (Link_PacketState == LINK_PKT_STATE_IDLE) {
        Link_PacketTimer = 0;
        return;
    }

    if (progress != 0) {
        Link_PacketTimer = LINK_PKT_TIMEOUT_TICKS;
        return;
    }

    if (Link_PacketTimer != 0) Link_PacketTimer--;
    if (Link_PacketTimer == 0) Link_PacketHandleTimeout();
}

Link_ReadPacket

Copy a completed packet and consume the shared mailbox.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall Link_ReadPacket(u8 *cmd, u8 *len, u8 *dst);

Parameters

cmd

Writable command byte; null omits it.

len

Writable length byte, 0..24; null omits it.

dst

Writable payload buffer with room for 24 bytes; null discards the payload.

Return value

Returns 1 when consumed, 0 when empty; empty reads leave outputs unchanged.

Conditions and limits

There is no destination-capacity parameter. Provide 24 writable bytes when using dst. cmd, len and dst may independently be null. Serialize mailbox inspection and consumption against other code and interrupts.

In Link4 mode, also clears the peer mailbox corresponding to this shared packet. Other peer mailboxes remain available.

c
u8 __stackcall Link_ReadPacket(u8 *cmd, u8 *len, u8 *dst) {
    u8 i;
    u8 peer_slot = Link4_LastPacketPeer;

    if (Link_ReceivedPacketReady == 0) return 0;

    if (cmd != 0) *cmd = Link_ReceivedPacketCmd;
    if (len != 0) *len = Link_ReceivedPacketLen;

    if (dst != 0) {
        for (i = 0; i < Link_ReceivedPacketLen; ++i) {
            dst[(__safe_index u8)i] = Link_ReceivedPacketBuf[(__safe_index u8)i];
        }
    }

    Link_ReceivedPacketReady = 0;
    if (Link4_IsValidRemoteSlotInternal(peer_slot) != 0) {
        Link4_ReceivedPacketReady[(__safe_index u8)peer_slot] = 0;
    }
    Link4_LastPacketPeer = LINK4_INVALID_SLOT;
    return 1;
}
Link_SendPacket

Copy the payload into owned storage and schedule packet transmission.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall Link_SendPacket(const u8 *data, u8 len, u8 cmd);

Parameters

data

Readable source of len bytes; may be null only when len is zero.

len

Payload length in bytes, 0..24.

cmd

Application-defined eight-bit command.

Return value

Returns 0 when accepted, 1 for busy packet state, or 4 for invalid length/pointer.

Conditions and limits

Error codes are 0=none, 1=busy, 2=timeout, 3=receive overflow, 4=invalid configuration/protocol and 5=an ACK timeout with a disconnect-like response. Start/configuration calls succeed with 0; receive/pop calls succeed with 1. Successful calls do not clear a latched error.

A packet contains 0xA5, command, length, 0–24 payload bytes and an XOR checksum. The response is 0x79 (ACK, accepted) or 0x1F (NAK, rejected). The checksum XORs the command, length and payload. Each machine has one shared packet mailbox; Link4 additionally has one mailbox per peer.

Keep polling on both endpoints. A timeout counts 90 calls without progress, not hardware frames. Sending 0xFF solely to clock an ACK does not extend that deadline; transmission allows at most three attempts. Retries can deliver duplicates, so add application-level identifiers when a command must run exactly once.

Zero means queued, not received or acknowledged by the peer. The source array may be reused after acceptance.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

Send command 49 with payload 7/42/255, then change the source array. QUEUED=0 accepts the send; SECOND SEND=1 rejects a second start. That busy error remains latched until ClearError. PAYLOAD 2=42 on the receiving endpoint proves that the queued payload is an owned copy.

kitaqgb/lib/link_packet.c:361

c
u8 __stackcall Link_SendPacket(const u8 *data, u8 len, u8 cmd) {
    u8 i;
    u8 checksum = (u8)(cmd ^ len);

    if (len > LINK_PKT_MAX_PAYLOAD) {
        Link_SetErrorInternal(LINK_ERR_PROTOCOL);
        return LINK_ERR_PROTOCOL;
    }

    if (len != 0 && data == 0) {
        Link_SetErrorInternal(LINK_ERR_PROTOCOL);
        return LINK_ERR_PROTOCOL;
    }

    if (Link_PacketState != LINK_PKT_STATE_IDLE || Link_PendingAck != 0) {
        Link_SetErrorInternal(LINK_ERR_BUSY);
        return LINK_ERR_BUSY;
    }

    Link_CurrentPacketCmd = cmd;
    Link_CurrentPacketLen = len;

    for (i = 0; i < len; ++i) {
        Link_CurrentPacketBuf[(__safe_index u8)i] = data[(__safe_index u8)i];
        checksum = (u8)(checksum ^ data[(__safe_index u8)i]);
    }

    Link_CurrentPacketChecksum = checksum;
    Link_TxSeq = 0;
    Link_RxSeq = 0;
    Link_PacketRetryCount = 0;
    Link_PacketTimer = LINK_PKT_TIMEOUT_TICKS;
    Link_PacketState = LINK_PKT_STATE_SEND_SYNC;
    return LINK_ERR_NONE;
}
Link_SetFastClock

Choose whether future internally clocked transfers use the CGB fast-clock bit.

Syntax

c
void __stackcall Link_SetFastClock(u8 on);

Parameters

on

Zero requests normal speed; nonzero requests fast speed.

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

Each machine has one shared link state. Byte exchanges are full duplex: one side supplies the internal clock and the other uses external clocks. Normal speed takes 512 clocks per bit; CGB fast speed takes 16.

Does not change an in-flight transfer. External-clock transfers ignore this setting. Hardware support is not checked; run both sample endpoints on matching hardware modes.

Link_TryReadByte

Pop one byte from the ordinary receive ring without waiting.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall Link_TryReadByte(u8 *out);

Parameters

out

Writable byte destination; null discards the byte.

Return value

Returns 1 when popped, 0 when empty; an empty read leaves out unchanged.

Conditions and limits

An eight-entry receive ring holds seven bytes. A full ring drops the new byte and latches error 3. A received zero byte is valid data.

Internal critical sections track software nesting depth. Leaving the outer section enables CPU interrupts, so do not assume that a previously disabled IME state is preserved.

Link4 copies each received byte to both the ordinary ring and a per-peer ring. Reading one does not drain the other. Packet polling consumes the ordinary ring; regularly discard unused per-peer raw bytes as well to prevent overflow.

The screens come from KOKURA. Multi-endpoint examples check values on linked emulator instances, and screens are captured from their final saved states. These checks do not establish physical cable or four-player adapter behavior.

kitaqgb/lib/link.h:83

Declaration notes (original source)
Require an output pointer, poll immediately, then wait at most timeout_frames
VBlanks for a byte. Zero timeout still performs the initial poll and read.

kitaqgb/lib/link.c:435

c
u8 __stackcall Link_WaitByte(u16 timeout_frames, u8 *out) {
    u16 waited = 0;

    if (out == 0) return 0;

    Link_Poll();
    if (Link_TryReadByte(out) != 0) return 1;

    while (waited < timeout_frames) {
        __wait_vblank();
        waited++;
        Link_Poll();
        if (Link_TryReadByte(out) != 0) return 1;
    }

    Link_SetErrorInternal(LINK_ERR_TIMEOUT);
    return 0;
}

link_dmg07.h — DMG-07 external-clock communication

The DMG-07 broadcasts one submitted byte from each console to all four players. This library handles discovery, player-1 startup, delayed packet broadcasts and aligned restart control. Learn four-console exchange with EXCHANGE, timeout behavior with NO ADAPTER, unread data with OVERFLOW and recovery with RESTART.

Library player numbers are 1..4; zero means undiscovered. Connection-mask bits 0..3 correspond to players 1..4. KOKURA --link-session slot values are 0..3, a separate numbering convention from the ROM API.

This driver owns the serial port. Do not run ordinary Link or Link4 concurrently; include link_hwregs_gb.c and link_dmg07.c once each. The adapter supplies external clocks; the driver does not select CGB fast serial mode.

Call Poll repeatedly throughout the frame and TickFrame exactly once per frame. One Poll per VBlank cannot re-arm the port between adapter bytes. The shared header’s d_poll detects entry into LY >= 144 to call TickFrame once. Serialize both operations instead of racing an ISR against the main loop.

With SIZE=1 each console submits one byte; the four-byte broadcast is ordered by players 1..4. The initial broadcast is discarded. Subsequent broadcasts contain the previous packet’s submissions. An all-0xFF four-byte broadcast is reserved as the restart indication.

LinkDmg07_ClearError

Reset the last-error code to zero.

Syntax

c
void LinkDmg07_ClearError();

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

SilenceFrames and diagnostic counters saturate at 255. Init resets them all; ordinary protocol restarts preserve diagnostic counters. ClearError clears only the error code.

Preserves received data, phase, connection information and the timeout latch. This call alone does not reconnect or resume reception.

Screens are captured from KOKURA’s DMG-07 model. Each console executes independently, and transmitted and received values are compared. Physical adapter/cable electrical behavior and timing are unverified. CGB screens display numeric values in blue.

Place kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs under one parent directory and open PowerShell there. Four-console examples launch the same ROM in four sessions. For DMG checks, replace --cgb=cgb with --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb with --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
LinkDmg07_ClearError();result[21]=LinkDmg07_LastError();result[22]=LinkDmg07_GetErrorCount();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Leave the first valid packet unread until another arrives. Expect SENT SEQ=3, PACKET SEQ=2 and ERROR=6; the read returns the latest 33/34/35/36. ClearError changes CLEAR ERROR to zero while ErrorCount remains one.

LinkDmg07_GetConnectedMask

Read the four-bit set of players in the last accepted status.

Syntax

c
u8 LinkDmg07_GetConnectedMask();

Return value

Bits 0..3 report connected players. Undiscovered is zero; four connected players is 15.

Conditions and limits

Library player numbers are 1..4; zero means undiscovered. Connection-mask bits 0..3 correspond to players 1..4. KOKURA --link-session slot values are 0..3, a separate numbering convention from the ROM API.

Returns cached discovery status rather than probing physical wiring. During transfer it reflects the most recent accepted notification.

Screens are captured from KOKURA’s DMG-07 model. Each console executes independently, and transmitted and received values are compared. Physical adapter/cable electrical behavior and timing are unverified. CGB screens display numeric values in blue.

Place kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs under one parent directory and open PowerShell there. Four-console examples launch the same ROM in four sessions. For DMG checks, replace --cgb=cgb with --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb with --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
result[1]=LinkDmg07_GetConnectedMask();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Run the same ROM on four consoles, each sending 32 plus its player number. Every console receives PLAYER 1..4 = 33/34/35/36. The first valid broadcast records SENT SEQ=2 and PACKET SEQ=1, showing the one-packet delay. The screen freezes that observation; a game continues polling afterwards.

LinkDmg07_GetDisconnectCount

Read recorded loss events: silence after seeing an adapter, or players disappearing from discovery status.

Syntax

c
u8 LinkDmg07_GetDisconnectCount();

Return value

Returns 0..255 events, not the number of lost players.

Conditions and limits

SilenceFrames and diagnostic counters saturate at 255. Init resets them all; ordinary protocol restarts preserve diagnostic counters. ClearError clears only the error code.

A deadline before any adapter has been observed does not increment it. Multiple players removed by one status change count as one event.

Screens are captured from KOKURA’s DMG-07 model. Each console executes independently, and transmitted and received values are compared. Physical adapter/cable electrical behavior and timing are unverified. CGB screens display numeric values in blue.

Place kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs under one parent directory and open PowerShell there. Four-console examples launch the same ROM in four sessions. For DMG checks, replace --cgb=cgb with --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb with --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
result[8]=LinkDmg07_GetDisconnectCount();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Run without an adapter. Expect PLAYER=0, START ERROR=2, SILENT FRAME=12, TIMEOUTS=1 and ERROR=4. DISCONNECTS stays zero because no adapter has ever been seen. An empty read preserves EMPTY BUFFER=77; ClearError produces CLEARED=0.

LinkDmg07_GetErrorCount

Read the count of received-protocol errors and unread-packet overwrites.

Syntax

c
u8 LinkDmg07_GetErrorCount();

Return value

Returns 0..255. Request validation/state errors and timeouts are not included.

Conditions and limits

SilenceFrames and diagnostic counters saturate at 255. Init resets them all; ordinary protocol restarts preserve diagnostic counters. ClearError clears only the error code.

The receive mailbox holds only the latest packet. Completion of another packet overwrites unread data, latches error 6 and increments ErrorCount. The adapter does not wait for the application to consume the mailbox.

Screens are captured from KOKURA’s DMG-07 model. Each console executes independently, and transmitted and received values are compared. Physical adapter/cable electrical behavior and timing are unverified. CGB screens display numeric values in blue.

Place kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs under one parent directory and open PowerShell there. Four-console examples launch the same ROM in four sessions. For DMG checks, replace --cgb=cgb with --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb with --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
result[19]=LinkDmg07_GetErrorCount();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Leave the first valid packet unread until another arrives. Expect SENT SEQ=3, PACKET SEQ=2 and ERROR=6; the read returns the latest 33/34/35/36. ClearError changes CLEAR ERROR to zero while ErrorCount remains one.

LinkDmg07_GetLastStatus

Read the last validated raw adapter status byte.

Syntax

c
u8 LinkDmg07_GetLastStatus();

Return value

The high nibble is the connection mask; the low three bits contain the local player number. Initially zero.

Conditions and limits

Library player numbers are 1..4; zero means undiscovered. Connection-mask bits 0..3 correspond to players 1..4. KOKURA --link-session slot values are 0..3, a separate numbering convention from the ROM API.

Rejects status with bit 3 set, player number zero or above four, or a changed local number after discovery. Rejection latches error 5 without storing that value as LastStatus.

LinkDmg07_GetPacketSequence

Read the sequence assigned to the most recently published packet.

Syntax

c
u8 LinkDmg07_GetPacketSequence();

Return value

Returns the eight-bit packet sequence without changing readiness.

Conditions and limits

Sequence numbers wrap from 255 to zero. At publication, PacketSequence equals SentSequence minus one. Later transmit starts advance SentSequence, so two getters sampled later need not differ by one.

The receive mailbox holds only the latest packet. Completion of another packet overwrites unread data, latches error 6 and increments ErrorCount. The adapter does not wait for the application to consume the mailbox.

LinkDmg07_GetPacketSlot

Read one player’s byte from cached packet storage.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall LinkDmg07_GetPacketSlot(u8 player_slot);

Parameters

player_slot

Physical player number, 1..4.

Return value

Conditions and limits

Library player numbers are 1..4; zero means undiscovered. Connection-mask bits 0..3 correspond to players 1..4. KOKURA --link-session slot values are 0..3, a separate numbering convention from the ROM API.

Neither checks nor consumes readiness. Returns zero just after initialization and may return retained bytes after consumption or a discovery reset. Do not use it as a new-data test.

Separate from the communication phase. Zero alone does not imply an established or usable connection.

LinkDmg07_GetSentSequence

Read the count of application submission bytes actually clocked out.

Syntax

c
u8 LinkDmg07_GetSentSequence();

Return value

Returns the eight-bit sent sequence. Counts the initial submission but excludes restart-control traffic.

Conditions and limits

Sequence numbers wrap from 255 to zero. At publication, PacketSequence equals SentSequence minus one. Later transmit starts advance SentSequence, so two getters sampled later need not differ by one.

With SIZE=1 each console submits one byte; the four-byte broadcast is ordered by players 1..4. The initial broadcast is discarded. Subsequent broadcasts contain the previous packet’s submissions. An all-0xFF four-byte broadcast is reserved as the restart indication.

Screens are captured from KOKURA’s DMG-07 model. Each console executes independently, and transmitted and received values are compared. Physical adapter/cable electrical behavior and timing are unverified. CGB screens display numeric values in blue.

Place kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs under one parent directory and open PowerShell there. Four-console examples launch the same ROM in four sessions. For DMG checks, replace --cgb=cgb with --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb with --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
result[6]=LinkDmg07_GetSentSequence();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Run the same ROM on four consoles, each sending 32 plus its player number. Every console receives PLAYER 1..4 = 33/34/35/36. The first valid broadcast records SENT SEQ=2 and PACKET SEQ=1, showing the one-packet delay. The screen freezes that observation; a game continues polling afterwards.

LinkDmg07_GetSilenceFrames

Read frames counted since the last processed serial completion.

Syntax

c
u8 LinkDmg07_GetSilenceFrames();

Return value

0..255; processed completion resets it, and each TickFrame increments it.

Conditions and limits

Call Poll repeatedly throughout the frame and TickFrame exactly once per frame. One Poll per VBlank cannot re-arm the port between adapter bytes. The shared header’s d_poll detects entry into LY >= 144 to call TickFrame once. Serialize both operations instead of racing an ISR against the main loop.

SilenceFrames and diagnostic counters saturate at 255. Init resets them all; ordinary protocol restarts preserve diagnostic counters. ClearError clears only the error code.

Screens are captured from KOKURA’s DMG-07 model. Each console executes independently, and transmitted and received values are compared. Physical adapter/cable electrical behavior and timing are unverified. CGB screens display numeric values in blue.

Place kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs under one parent directory and open PowerShell there. Four-console examples launch the same ROM in four sessions. For DMG checks, replace --cgb=cgb with --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb with --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

result[6]=LinkDmg07_GetSilenceFrames();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Run without an adapter. Expect PLAYER=0, START ERROR=2, SILENT FRAME=12, TIMEOUTS=1 and ERROR=4. DISCONNECTS stays zero because no adapter has ever been seen. An empty read preserves EMPTY BUFFER=77; ClearError produces CLEARED=0.

LinkDmg07_HasPacket

Inspect whether a completed four-byte data packet is unread.

Syntax

c
u8 LinkDmg07_HasPacket();

Return value

Returns 1 for unread data, otherwise 0.

Conditions and limits

With SIZE=1 each console submits one byte; the four-byte broadcast is ordered by players 1..4. The initial broadcast is discarded. Subsequent broadcasts contain the previous packet’s submissions. An all-0xFF four-byte broadcast is reserved as the restart indication.

The receive mailbox holds only the latest packet. Completion of another packet overwrites unread data, latches error 6 and increments ErrorCount. The adapter does not wait for the application to consume the mailbox.

LinkDmg07_Init

Reset discovery, receive storage and diagnostics, then arm reception for adapter clocks.

Syntax

c
void __stackcall LinkDmg07_Init(u8 rate);

Parameters

rate

Eight-bit RATE response to the adapter; zero selects the default 0x10.

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

This driver owns the serial port. Do not run ordinary Link or Link4 concurrently; include link_hwregs_gb.c and link_dmg07.c once each. The adapter supplies external clocks; the driver does not select CGB fast serial mode.

Library player numbers are 1..4; zero means undiscovered. Connection-mask bits 0..3 correspond to players 1..4. KOKURA --link-session slot values are 0..3, a separate numbering convention from the ROM API.

Sets SC to 0x80 and SB to 0x88; clears only the serial bits in IE and IF. It does not alter the other interrupt-enable bits or CPU IME state.

Screens are captured from KOKURA’s DMG-07 model. Each console executes independently, and transmitted and received values are compared. Physical adapter/cable electrical behavior and timing are unverified. CGB screens display numeric values in blue.

kitaqgb/lib/link_dmg07.h:50

Declaration notes (original source)
Initializes polling-only external-clock operation.  A zero RATE is replaced
with LINK_DMG07_DEFAULT_RATE.  This driver disables only the serial IRQ bit.

kitaqgb/lib/link_dmg07.c:282

c
void __stackcall LinkDmg07_Init(u8 rate) {
    u8 i;

    LinkDmg07_Rate = rate;
    if (LinkDmg07_Rate == 0) LinkDmg07_Rate = LINK_DMG07_DEFAULT_RATE;
    LinkDmg07_LocalByte = 0;
    LinkDmg07_SentSequence = 0;
    LinkDmg07_PacketSequence = 0;
    LinkDmg07_RestartState = LINK_DMG07_RESTART_NONE;
    LinkDmg07_SilenceFrames = 0;
    LinkDmg07_TimeoutCount = 0;
    LinkDmg07_DisconnectCount = 0;
    LinkDmg07_ErrorCount = 0;
    LinkDmg07_LastErrorCode = LINK_DMG07_ERR_NONE;
    LinkDmg07_SeenAdapter = 0;
    LinkDmg07_TimeoutLatched = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < LINK_DMG07_PACKET_BYTES; ++i) {
        LinkDmg07_RxBuild[(__safe_index u8)i] = 0;
        LinkDmg07_RxPacket[(__safe_index u8)i] = 0;
    }
    LinkDmg07_ResetToPingInternal();

    LinkHw_WriteIE((u8)(LinkHw_ReadIE() & LINK_DMG07_IRQ_SERIAL_CLEAR));
    LinkHw_WriteIF((u8)(LinkHw_ReadIF() & LINK_DMG07_IRQ_SERIAL_CLEAR));
    LinkDmg07_ArmInternal(LINK_DMG07_ACK);
}

LinkDmg07_LastError

Read the most recently latched error code.

Syntax

c
u8 LinkDmg07_LastError();

Return value

Returns error code 0..6.

Conditions and limits

Error codes are 0=none, 1=wrong phase, 2=not player 1, 3=not ready, 4=timeout, 5=protocol error and 6=unread packet overwritten. Requests succeed with zero; receive/pop operations succeed with one. A successful request does not clear an earlier error.

Reading does not clear it. Stores only the latest code, not a history of every error.

Screens are captured from KOKURA’s DMG-07 model. Each console executes independently, and transmitted and received values are compared. Physical adapter/cable electrical behavior and timing are unverified. CGB screens display numeric values in blue.

Place kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs under one parent directory and open PowerShell there. Four-console examples launch the same ROM in four sessions. For DMG checks, replace --cgb=cgb with --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb with --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
result[9]=LinkDmg07_LastError();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Run without an adapter. Expect PLAYER=0, START ERROR=2, SILENT FRAME=12, TIMEOUTS=1 and ERROR=4. DISCONNECTS stays zero because no adapter has ever been seen. An empty read preserves EMPTY BUFFER=77; ClearError produces CLEARED=0.

LinkDmg07_Poll

Process one completed serial byte in the current phase and immediately arm the next response.

Syntax

c
void LinkDmg07_Poll();

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

This driver owns the serial port. Do not run ordinary Link or Link4 concurrently; include link_hwregs_gb.c and link_dmg07.c once each. The adapter supplies external clocks; the driver does not select CGB fast serial mode.

Call Poll repeatedly throughout the frame and TickFrame exactly once per frame. One Poll per VBlank cannot re-arm the port between adapter bytes. The shared header’s d_poll detects entry into LY >= 144 to call TickFrame once. Serialize both operations instead of racing an ISR against the main loop.

Does nothing while SC’s start bit is set. Processing completion resets SilenceFrames and the timeout latch. Initialize before polling.

Screens are captured from KOKURA’s DMG-07 model. Each console executes independently, and transmitted and received values are compared. Physical adapter/cable electrical behavior and timing are unverified. CGB screens display numeric values in blue.

Place kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs under one parent directory and open PowerShell there. Four-console examples launch the same ROM in four sessions. For DMG checks, replace --cgb=cgb with --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb with --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
void d_poll(){LinkDmg07_Poll();if(D_LY>=144){if(d_vblank==0){d_vblank=1;LinkDmg07_TickFrame();}}else d_vblank=0;}

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Run the same ROM on four consoles, each sending 32 plus its player number. Every console receives PLAYER 1..4 = 33/34/35/36. The first valid broadcast records SENT SEQ=2 and PACKET SEQ=1, showing the one-packet delay. The screen freezes that observation; a game continues polling afterwards.

Declaration notes (original source)
Services at most one completed serial byte and immediately re-arms SC=$80.
Call continuously from the main loop, including between VBlanks.

kitaqgb/lib/link_dmg07.c:311

c
void LinkDmg07_Poll() {
    u8 value;
    u8 next;

    if ((LinkHw_ReadSC() & LINK_DMG07_SC_EXTERNAL_START) != 0) return;

    value = LinkHw_ReadSB();
    LinkDmg07_SilenceFrames = 0;
    LinkDmg07_TimeoutLatched = 0;
    LinkDmg07_SeenAdapter = 1;

    next = 0;
    if (LinkDmg07_Phase == LINK_DMG07_PHASE_PING) {
        next = LinkDmg07_ProcessPingInternal(value);
    } else if (LinkDmg07_Phase == LINK_DMG07_PHASE_REQUEST_AA) {
        next = LinkDmg07_ProcessRequestInternal(value);
    } else if (LinkDmg07_Phase == LINK_DMG07_PHASE_WAIT_CC) {
        next = LinkDmg07_ProcessWaitCcInternal(value);
    } else if (LinkDmg07_Phase == LINK_DMG07_PHASE_TRANSFER) {
        next = LinkDmg07_ProcessTransferInternal(value);
    } else {
        LinkDmg07_SetRuntimeErrorInternal(LINK_DMG07_ERR_PROTOCOL);
        LinkDmg07_ResetToPingInternal();
        next = LINK_DMG07_ACK;
    }

    LinkDmg07_ArmInternal(next);
}
LinkDmg07_ReadPacket

Copy the latest completed packet and clear its unread flag.

Syntax

c
u8 __stackcall LinkDmg07_ReadPacket(u8 *dst);

Parameters

dst

Four writable bytes; null discards the packet.

Return value

Returns 1 when consumed, 0 when empty. Empty reads leave dst unchanged.

Conditions and limits

With SIZE=1 each console submits one byte; the four-byte broadcast is ordered by players 1..4. The initial broadcast is discarded. Subsequent broadcasts contain the previous packet’s submissions. An all-0xFF four-byte broadcast is reserved as the restart indication.

The receive mailbox holds only the latest packet. Completion of another packet overwrites unread data, latches error 6 and increments ErrorCount. The adapter does not wait for the application to consume the mailbox.

Cached bytes remain available through GetPacketSlot after consumption. An empty ReadPacket does not copy those cached bytes again.

kitaqgb/lib/link_dmg07.h:99

Declaration notes (original source)
Consume the latest four-byte packet. A nonnull destination must hold four
bytes; null discards the packet. Packet storage remains after the flag clears.

kitaqgb/lib/link_dmg07.c:479

c
u8 __stackcall LinkDmg07_ReadPacket(u8 *dst) {
    if (LinkDmg07_PacketReady == 0) return 0;
    if (dst != 0) {
        // Keep this as a sequential pointer copy.  Besides being smaller for a
        // fixed four-byte packet, it avoids making a serial hot-path copy
        // depend on general variable-index pointer lowering.
        *dst = LinkDmg07_RxPacket[0];
        dst++;
        *dst = LinkDmg07_RxPacket[1];
        dst++;
        *dst = LinkDmg07_RxPacket[2];
        dst++;
        *dst = LinkDmg07_RxPacket[3];
    }
    LinkDmg07_PacketReady = 0;
    return 1;
}
LinkDmg07_RequestRestart

Schedule restart control traffic beginning at a transfer packet boundary.

Syntax

c
u8 LinkDmg07_RequestRestart();

Return value

Returns 0 in TRANSFER, otherwise 1. Repeated requests while pending/sending also return 0.

Conditions and limits

With SIZE=1 each console submits one byte; the four-byte broadcast is ordered by players 1..4. The initial broadcast is discarded. Subsequent broadcasts contain the previous packet’s submissions. An all-0xFF four-byte broadcast is reserved as the restart indication.

Error codes are 0=none, 1=wrong phase, 2=not player 1, 3=not ready, 4=timeout, 5=protocol error and 6=unread packet overwritten. Requests succeed with zero; receive/pop operations succeed with one. A successful request does not clear an earlier error.

Any player may request it. Preserves the current byte position, sends aligned 0xFF traffic, and returns to discovery after the adapter’s all-0xFF indication. Merely requesting it does not erase the local slot or receive pipeline.

kitaqgb/lib/link_dmg07.h:83

Declaration notes (original source)
Any physical slot may schedule FF FF FF FF at the next four-byte packet
boundary while remaining in TRANSFER phase.  The driver keeps sending aligned
FF bytes until it sees the adapter's complete all-FF indicator packet, then
returns to PING.  A transfer-phase silence timeout schedules the same recovery
automatically and preserves the current byte position for clocks that resume.

kitaqgb/lib/link_dmg07.c:445

c
u8 LinkDmg07_RequestRestart() {
    if (LinkDmg07_Phase != LINK_DMG07_PHASE_TRANSFER) {
        LinkDmg07_LastErrorCode = LINK_DMG07_ERR_STATE;
        return LINK_DMG07_ERR_STATE;
    }
    if (LinkDmg07_RestartState == LINK_DMG07_RESTART_NONE) {
        LinkDmg07_RestartState = LINK_DMG07_RESTART_PENDING;
    }
    return LINK_DMG07_ERR_NONE;
}
LinkDmg07_RequestTransmission

Schedule a start request from physical player 1 at the next discovery-packet boundary.

Syntax

c
u8 LinkDmg07_RequestTransmission();

Return value

Returns 0 when scheduled, 1 for the wrong phase, 2 when not player 1, or 3 when the local connection bit is absent.

Conditions and limits

Library player numbers are 1..4; zero means undiscovered. Connection-mask bits 0..3 correspond to players 1..4. KOKURA --link-session slot values are 0..3, a separate numbering convention from the ROM API.

Error codes are 0=none, 1=wrong phase, 2=not player 1, 3=not ready, 4=timeout, 5=protocol error and 6=unread packet overwritten. Requests succeed with zero; receive/pop operations succeed with one. A successful request does not clear an earlier error.

Can be scheduled only in PING. It does not itself wait for all four players; the example checks mask 15 in application code. Scheduling is asynchronous: aligned 0xAA traffic precedes the 0xCC confirmation.

kitaqgb/lib/link_dmg07.c:426

c
u8 LinkDmg07_RequestTransmission() {
    if (LinkDmg07_Phase != LINK_DMG07_PHASE_PING) {
        LinkDmg07_LastErrorCode = LINK_DMG07_ERR_STATE;
        return LINK_DMG07_ERR_STATE;
    }
    if (LinkDmg07_LocalSlot != 1) {
        LinkDmg07_LastErrorCode = LINK_DMG07_ERR_NOT_PLAYER1;
        return LINK_DMG07_ERR_NOT_PLAYER1;
    }
    if ((LinkDmg07_ConnectedMask & (u8)0x01) == 0) {
        LinkDmg07_LastErrorCode = LINK_DMG07_ERR_NOT_READY;
        return LINK_DMG07_ERR_NOT_READY;
    }
    LinkDmg07_StartRequested = 1;
    return LINK_DMG07_ERR_NONE;
}

LinkDmg07_TickFrame

Advance silence and start/restart watchdogs by one frame, requesting recovery at the deadline.

Syntax

c
void LinkDmg07_TickFrame();

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

Call Poll repeatedly throughout the frame and TickFrame exactly once per frame. One Poll per VBlank cannot re-arm the port between adapter bytes. The shared header’s d_poll detects entry into LY >= 144 to call TickFrame once. Serialize both operations instead of racing an ISR against the main loop.

SilenceFrames and diagnostic counters saturate at 255. Init resets them all; ordinary protocol restarts preserve diagnostic counters. ClearError clears only the error code.

The default deadline is 12 calls; define LINK_DMG07_TIMEOUT_FRAMES as 1..255 before inclusion to choose another deadline. A silence episode is counted once until another byte clears its latch. Transfer recovery preserves byte alignment; discovery/start recovery returns to discovery.

Screens are captured from KOKURA’s DMG-07 model. Each console executes independently, and transmitted and received values are compared. Physical adapter/cable electrical behavior and timing are unverified. CGB screens display numeric values in blue.

Place kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs under one parent directory and open PowerShell there. Four-console examples launch the same ROM in four sessions. For DMG checks, replace --cgb=cgb with --cgb=dmg and --hardware cgb with --hardware dmg throughout.

Usage example

c
void d_poll(){LinkDmg07_Poll();if(D_LY>=144){if(d_vblank==0){d_vblank=1;LinkDmg07_TickFrame();}}else d_vblank=0;}

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Run without an adapter. Expect PLAYER=0, START ERROR=2, SILENT FRAME=12, TIMEOUTS=1 and ERROR=4. DISCONNECTS stays zero because no adapter has ever been seen. An empty read preserves EMPTY BUFFER=77; ClearError produces CLEARED=0.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\dmg07_absent.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\dmg07_absent.gb --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=128k --no-cache --no-disasm
.\kokura\kokura-cli.exe .\out\dmg07_absent.gb --hardware cgb --run-frames 90 --png .\out\absent.png

kitaqgb/lib/link_dmg07.h:57

Declaration notes (original source)
Advances saturating frame-based silence and handshake timeout counters.

kitaqgb/lib/link_dmg07.c:369

c
void LinkDmg07_TickFrame() {
    LinkDmg07_SilenceFrames = LinkDmg07_IncrementSaturatingInternal(LinkDmg07_SilenceFrames);

    if ((LinkDmg07_Phase == LINK_DMG07_PHASE_REQUEST_AA) ||
        (LinkDmg07_Phase == LINK_DMG07_PHASE_WAIT_CC) ||
        (LinkDmg07_RestartState == LINK_DMG07_RESTART_SENDING)) {
        LinkDmg07_HandshakeFrames = LinkDmg07_IncrementSaturatingInternal(LinkDmg07_HandshakeFrames);
    } else {
        LinkDmg07_HandshakeFrames = 0;
    }

    if ((LinkDmg07_SilenceFrames >= LINK_DMG07_TIMEOUT_FRAMES) &&
        (LinkDmg07_TimeoutLatched == 0)) {
        LinkDmg07_TimeoutInternal(1);
        return;
    }

    if ((LinkDmg07_HandshakeFrames >= LINK_DMG07_TIMEOUT_FRAMES) &&
        (LinkDmg07_TimeoutLatched == 0)) {
        LinkDmg07_TimeoutInternal(0);
    }
}

physics2d.h — 2D motion and collision

Provides box integration/AABB contacts and an optional surface-response solver. Bodies use centers and half extents; active=0 excludes a slot and inv_mass_q8<=0 makes it static. KQRect instead uses top-left coordinates and width/height. Box-pair contacts do not use the body restitution field; surface responses use KQSurface2D coefficients.

Choose consistent integer units for positions, radii, half extents, velocities and gravity. One step is one simulation tick. The samples use one unit per pixel. These routines neither convert positions to Q8.8 automatically nor render them.

A world borrows its array. The caller allocates and owns body storage and keeps it alive. Initializing a world does not initialize its array elements.

kq2d_body_apply_friction

Scale both velocity components by a signed-byte coefficient divided by 256 without checking position or activity.

Syntax

c
void kq2d_body_apply_friction(KQBody2D* body, u8 friction_q8);

Parameters

body

Pointer to the body to modify. Fields not used by this operation are retained.

friction_q8

Velocity multiplier retained by this function. It is converted to s8, so 128..255 become negative coefficients.

Return value

No return value. This entry describes the fields updated and when they take effect.

Conditions and limits

Values 0..127 give multipliers 0..127/256. Values 128..255 become negative after the s8 conversion and reverse velocity. For positive damping across 0..255, use kq2d_scale_q8 on each velocity instead. Products truncate toward zero. NULL is ignored.

Usage example

c
kq2d_body_apply_friction(&temp,64);
    result[11]=temp.vx; result[12]=temp.vy;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Left shows the initial state; right shows one tick later. A red 16x16 box with center (24,24) and velocity (4,16) reaches (28,36), with Y velocity zero on the blue floor. Panel origins are screen (8,48) and (88,48). DMG renders all marks in black. RAM checks also cover initialization, setters, integration, rectangle/point queries and signed scaling.
