kq2d_body_apply_gravity

Add gravity to an active dynamic body and clamp each axis to +/-max_speed without updating position.

Syntax

c
void kq2d_body_apply_gravity(KQBody2D* body, s16 gravity_x, s16 gravity_y, s16 max_speed);

Parameters

body

Pointer to the body to modify. Fields not used by this operation are retained.

gravity_x

Acceleration added to X velocity by this call.

gravity_y

Acceleration added to Y velocity by this call.

max_speed

Speed limit; the entry specifies whether this limits each axis or the combined vector.

Return value

No return value. This entry describes the fields updated and when they take effect.

Conditions and limits

Choose consistent integer units for positions, radii, half extents, velocities and gravity. One step is one simulation tick. The samples use one unit per pixel. These routines neither convert positions to Q8.8 automatically nor render them.

Keep sums, differences, combined half extents and contact-correction products within signed 16-bit range. Velocity limits apply after addition and cannot prevent overflow during that addition.

Box integration and collision routines use shared scratch storage. Do not re-enter these physics routines from an interrupt.

Ignore NULL, inactive and nonpositive-inverse-mass bodies. Supply a nonnegative speed limit.

Usage example

kq2d_body_apply_gravity(&temp,5,-10,32);
    result[9]=temp.vx; result[10]=temp.vy;

Left shows the initial state; right shows one tick later. A red 16x16 box with center (24,24) and velocity (4,16) reaches (28,36), with Y velocity zero on the blue floor. Panel origins are screen (8,48) and (88,48). DMG renders all marks in black. RAM checks also cover initialization, setters, integration, rectangle/point queries and signed scaling.

Declaration notes (original source)
Add gravity and clamp each velocity axis separately for an active dynamic
body. Null, inactive and static bodies are ignored. Supply a nonnegative limit
and avoid overflow in the additions before clamping; position is unchanged.

kitaqgb/lib/physics2d.c:630

c
void kq2d_body_apply_gravity(KQBody2D* body, s16 gravity_x, s16 gravity_y, s16 max_speed)
{
    if (body == 0) return;
    if (body->active == 0) return;
    if (body->inv_mass_q8 <= 0) return;

    kq2d_asm_value = body->vx;
    kq2d_asm_operand = gravity_x;
    kq2d_add_s16_asm();
    kq2d_asm_limit = max_speed;
    kq2d_clamp_abs_s16_asm();
    body->vx = kq2d_asm_value;

    kq2d_asm_value = body->vy;
    kq2d_asm_operand = gravity_y;
    kq2d_add_s16_asm();
    kq2d_asm_limit = max_speed;
    kq2d_clamp_abs_s16_asm();
    body->vy = kq2d_asm_value;
}

kq2d_body_limit_speed

Estimate vector length conservatively and scale both axes together to limit combined speed.

Syntax

c
void kq2d_body_limit_speed(KQBody2D* body, s16 max_speed);

Parameters

body

Pointer to the body to modify. Fields not used by this operation are retained.

max_speed

Speed limit; the entry specifies whether this limits each axis or the combined vector.

Return value

No return value. This entry describes the fields updated and when they take effect.

Conditions and limits

Keep velocity magnitudes and a positive max_speed within 16383. A nonpositive limit zeros velocity. NULL is ignored, but activity and mass do not suppress modification. Integer quantization can undershoot the limit and tiny scale factors can produce zero.

Usage example

c
kq2d_body_limit_speed(&body,250);
    result[2]=body.vx; result[3]=body.vy;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The red body stays in place. Its green velocity line changes from (8,16) on the left to (2,-8) on the right, showing bounce and tangential friction against the blue surface. Panel origins are screen (8,48)/(88,48); the body center is local (24,40). Incoming speed is 16 and the crossing-time example returns 192/256. The speed-limit example reduces (300,400) to (147,196). All marks are black on DMG.

kitaqgb/lib/physics2d.h:92

Declaration notes (original source)
Conservative circular bound, with a shared Q8 scale for both components.
Quantizes toward zero; very small limits relative to input may yield zero.
Components and positive max_speed must be <= 16383 in magnitude.

kitaqgb/lib/physics2d.c:260

c
void kq2d_body_limit_speed(KQBody2D* body, s16 max_speed)
{
    u16 x;
    u16 y;
    u16 swap;
    u16 ratio;
    u16 length;
    if (body == 0) return;
    if (max_speed <= 0) { body->vx = 0; body->vy = 0; return; }
    x = (u16)body->vx;
    y = (u16)body->vy;
    if (body->vx < 0) x = (u16)(0 - body->vx);
    if (body->vy < 0) y = (u16)(0 - body->vy);
    if (x + y <= (u16)max_speed) return;
    if (x < y) { swap = x; x = y; y = swap; }
    // major + minor/2 bounds hypot from above for 0 <= minor <= major.
    if (x + (y >> 1) + 1 <= (u16)max_speed) return;
    // Round the minor/major ratio upward for the 65-entry upper-bound table.
    // The extra unit covers truncation when converting the estimate back to speed.
    ratio = (kq2d__fraction_q8(y, x) + 4) >> 2;
    if (ratio > 64) ratio = 64;
    length = x + (u16)kq2d_scale_q8((s16)x, (s16)kq2d_hypot_extra[(__safe_index u8)ratio]) + 1;
    if (length <= (u16)max_speed) return;
    ratio = kq2d__fraction_q8((u16)max_speed, length);
    body->vx = kq2d_scale_q8(body->vx, (s16)ratio);
    body->vy = kq2d_scale_q8(body->vy, (s16)ratio);
}
kq2d_body_resolve_surface

Use velocity relative to a moving surface to apply normal bounce, minimum bounce speed and tangential friction.

Syntax

c
s16 kq2d_body_resolve_surface(KQBody2D* body, const KQSurface2D* surface);

Parameters

body

Pointer to the body to modify. Fields not used by this operation are retained.

surface

Pointer to a KQSurface2D containing its normal, velocity, bounce and friction settings.

Return value

Returns the positive incoming normal speed, or 0 for NULL inputs or separating motion.

Conditions and limits

Use a Q8 unit normal with length 256. Keep relative components within +/-8191, threshold/kick nonnegative and coefficients in 0..255. Restitution applies only strictly above the threshold, with kick as a minimum rebound speed. NULL inputs or separating motion leave velocity unchanged. Contact detection and penetration correction are separate; activity and mass are not checked.

Usage example

c
result[6]=kq2d_body_resolve_surface(&body,&surface);
    result[7]=body.vx; result[8]=body.vy; result[9]=body.y;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The red body stays in place. Its green velocity line changes from (8,16) on the left to (2,-8) on the right, showing bounce and tangential friction against the blue surface. Panel origins are screen (8,48)/(88,48); the body center is local (24,40). Incoming speed is 16 and the crossing-time example returns 192/256. The speed-limit example reduces (300,400) to (147,196). All marks are black on DMG.

kitaqgb/lib/physics2d.h:95

Declaration notes (original source)
Kinematic surface response; returns incoming normal speed, or zero if separating.
Caller resolves penetration separately. Relative components must fit +/-8191.

kitaqgb/lib/physics2d.c:314

c
s16 kq2d_body_resolve_surface(KQBody2D* body, const KQSurface2D* surface)
{
    s16 vx;
    s16 vy;
    s16 speed;
    s16 tangent;
    s16 bounce = 0;
    s16 impulse;
    s16 friction;
    if (body == 0 || surface == 0) return 0;
    vx = (s16)(body->vx - surface->vx);
    vy = (s16)(body->vy - surface->vy);
    speed = (s16)(kq2d_scale_q8(vx,surface->nx_q8) + kq2d_scale_q8(vy,surface->ny_q8));
    if (speed >= 0) return 0;
    speed = (s16)(0 - speed);
    if (speed > surface->bounce_threshold) bounce = kq2d_scale_q8(speed,(s16)surface->restitution_q8);
    if (bounce < surface->kick) bounce = surface->kick;
    impulse = (s16)(speed + bounce);
    // A resting contact is a tangent constraint, not a tiny rounded bounce.
    if (bounce == 0) {
        tangent = (s16)(kq2d__rest_component(vy,surface->nx_q8) - kq2d__rest_component(vx,surface->ny_q8));
        friction = kq2d_scale_q8(impulse,(s16)surface->friction_q8);
        if (tangent > friction) tangent = (s16)(tangent - friction);
        else if (tangent < (s16)(0 - friction)) tangent = (s16)(tangent + friction);
        else tangent = 0;
        body->vx = (s16)(surface->vx - kq2d__rest_component(tangent,surface->ny_q8));
        body->vy = (s16)(surface->vy + kq2d__rest_component(tangent,surface->nx_q8));
        return speed;
    }
    body->vx = (s16)(body->vx + kq2d_scale_q8(impulse,surface->nx_q8));
    body->vy = (s16)(body->vy + kq2d_scale_q8(impulse,surface->ny_q8));
    if (surface->friction_q8 != 0) {
        tangent = (s16)(kq2d_scale_q8(vy,surface->nx_q8) - kq2d_scale_q8(vx,surface->ny_q8));
        friction = kq2d_scale_q8(impulse,(s16)surface->friction_q8);
        if (tangent > friction) tangent = friction;
        if (tangent < (s16)(0 - friction)) tangent = (s16)(0 - friction);
        body->vx = (s16)(body->vx + kq2d_scale_q8(tangent,surface->ny_q8));
        body->vy = (s16)(body->vy - kq2d_scale_q8(tangent,surface->nx_q8));
    }
    return speed;
}

void kq2d_integrate_body(KQWorld2D* world, KQBody2D* body)

Test strict overlap of two centered boxes on both X and Y.

Valid body pointer; the query ignores activity, mass and flags.

Return value

Returns 1 for interior overlap and 0 for touching or separated shapes.

Conditions and limits

Choose consistent integer units for positions, radii, half extents, velocities and gravity. One step is one simulation tick. The samples use one unit per pixel. These routines neither convert positions to Q8.8 automatically nor render them.

Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/physics2d.h:51

Declaration notes (original source)
Test strict overlap of two centered boxes; touching edges return false.
Both pointers must be valid. Active/mass flags are ignored, and coordinate
differences and extent sums must fit the signed 16-bit calculations.

kitaqgb/lib/physics2d.c:579

c
u8 kq2d_overlap_aabb(const KQBody2D* a, const KQBody2D* b)
{
    s16 dx = (s16)(b->x - a->x);
    s16 dy = (s16)(b->y - a->y);

    s16 adx = kq2d__abs_s16(dx);
    s16 ady = kq2d__abs_s16(dy);

    s16 sx = (s16)(a->half_x + b->half_x);
    s16 sy = (s16)(a->half_y + b->half_y);

    if (adx >= sx) return 0;
    if (ady >= sy) return 0;
    return 1;
}

Multiply by a signed coefficient divided by 256, truncating toward zero for either sign.

s16 kq2d_scale_q8(s16 value, s16 coefficient)
{
    // Eight-bit shift/add product in HL:C, with sign applied after truncation.
    __asm {
        LD_HL_IMM value
        LD_A_HL
        LD_E_A
        INC_HL
        LD_A_HL
        LD_D_A
        OR_E
        JP_Z kqscale_zero
        LD_HL_IMM coefficient
        LD_A_HL
        LD_C_A
        INC_HL
        LD_A_HL
        LD_B_A
        LD_A_C
        OR_A
        JR_NZ kqscale_fraction
        LD_A_B
        OR_A
        JP_Z kqscale_zero
        LD_H_D
        LD_L_E
        AND_IMM 128
        RET_Z
        JP kqscale_negate
kqscale_fraction:
        LD_A_D
        XOR_B
        AND_IMM 128
        PUSH_AF
        LD_A_D
        AND_IMM 128
        JR_Z kqscale_value_positive
        XOR_A
        SUB_E
        LD_E_A
        LD_A_IMM 0
        SBC_D
        LD_D_A

        SUB_C

kq2d_step

Integrate active dynamic bodies, then resolve contacts among active array entries.

Syntax

c
void kq2d_step(KQWorld2D* world);

Parameters

world

Pointer to the world holding the body array and simulation settings.

Return value

No return value. This entry describes the fields updated and when they take effect.

Conditions and limits

Choose consistent integer units for positions, radii, half extents, velocities and gravity. One step is one simulation tick. The samples use one unit per pixel. These routines neither convert positions to Q8.8 automatically nor render them.

A world borrows its array. The caller allocates and owns body storage and keeps it alive. Initializing a world does not initialize its array elements.

Keep sums, differences, combined half extents and contact-correction products within signed 16-bit range. Velocity limits apply after addition and cannot prevent overflow during that addition.

Contacts resolve along the shallower penetration axis, choosing Y on a tie. Position correction uses inverse masses, but two dynamic bodies receive their simple average axis velocity; collision with a static body zeros that component. This solver does not use restitution_q8. It is discrete collision handling and can miss fast crossings.

Box integration and collision routines use shared scratch storage. Do not re-enter these physics routines from an interrupt.

A NULL world or array is ignored. A zero solver_iterations value still performs one contact pass.

Usage example

c
kq2d_step(&world);
    result[22]=bodies[0].x; result[23]=bodies[0].y;
    result[24]=bodies[0].vx; result[25]=bodies[0].vy;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Left shows the initial state; right shows one tick later. A red 16x16 box with center (24,24) and velocity (4,16) reaches (28,36), with Y velocity zero on the blue floor. Panel origins are screen (8,48) and (88,48). DMG renders all marks in black. RAM checks also cover initialization, setters, integration, rectangle/point queries and signed scaling.

Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/physics2d.h:43

Declaration notes (original source)
Advance active dynamic bodies, then visit each active unordered pair for
the configured contact passes (zero means one). Static bodies still participate
as obstacles. The world borrows its array and shares non-reentrant ASM scratch.
This is discrete integration; fast bodies can pass through thin obstacles.

kitaqgb/lib/physics2d.c:794

c
void kq2d_step(KQWorld2D* world)
{
    if (world == 0) return;
    if (world->bodies == 0) return;

    KQBody2D* bodies = world->bodies;
    u8 count = world->body_count;

    // Integrate dynamic bodies.
    u8 i;
    for (i = 0; i < count; i++)
    {
        KQBody2D* b = &bodies[(__safe_index u8)i];
        if (b->active == 0) continue;
        if (b->inv_mass_q8 <= 0) continue;

        kq2d_asm_value = b->vx;
        kq2d_asm_operand = world->gravity_x;
        kq2d_add_s16_asm();
        kq2d_asm_limit = world->max_speed;
        kq2d_clamp_abs_s16_asm();
        b->vx = kq2d_asm_value;

        kq2d_asm_value = b->vy;
        kq2d_asm_operand = world->gravity_y;
        kq2d_add_s16_asm();
        kq2d_asm_limit = world->max_speed;
        kq2d_clamp_abs_s16_asm();
        b->vy = kq2d_asm_value;

        kq2d_asm_value = b->x;
        kq2d_asm_operand = b->vx;
        kq2d_add_s16_asm();
        b->x = kq2d_asm_value;

        kq2d_asm_value = b->y;
        kq2d_asm_operand = b->vy;
        kq2d_add_s16_asm();
        b->y = kq2d_asm_value;
    }

    // Solve contacts with a small fixed iteration count.
    u8 iterations = world->solver_iterations;
    if (iterations == 0) iterations = 1;

    u8 it;
    for (it = 0; it < iterations; it++)
    {
        for (i = 0; i < count; i++)
        {
            KQBody2D* a = &bodies[(__safe_index u8)i];
            if (a->active == 0) continue;

            u8 j;
            for (j = (u8)(i + 1); j < count; j++)
            {
                KQBody2D* b = &bodies[(__safe_index u8)j];
                if (b->active == 0) continue;
                kq2d__resolve_pair(a, b);
            }
        }
    }
}
kq2d_surface_toi_q8

Estimate the within-tick crossing time from signed start/end gaps under linear motion.

Syntax

Parameters

kitaqgb/lib/physics2d.h:98

Declaration notes (original source)
Linear crossing time in Q8 (0..256); positive separation is outside.
Returns 0 for initial overlap, 256 for no crossing. Gaps must fit +/-8191.

kitaqgb/lib/physics2d.c:291

c
u16 kq2d_surface_toi_q8(s16 start_gap, s16 end_gap)
{
    if (start_gap <= 0) return 0;
    if (end_gap >= 0) return 256;
    return kq2d__fraction_q8((u16)start_gap, (u16)(start_gap - end_gap));
}

physics2d_circle.h — Circle physics

Supports circle radius, inverse mass, restitution, tangential friction, world damping and bounds. The caller initializes every body field. Body friction_q8 and wall_friction_q8 describe tangential motion removed, whereas linear_damping_q8 describes velocity retained. Byte coefficients are divided by 256, so 255 is not exactly 1.0.

Choose consistent integer units for positions, radii, half extents, velocities and gravity. One step is one simulation tick. The samples use one unit per pixel. These routines neither convert positions to Q8.8 automatically nor render them.

Circle distance and normals are integer approximations. Reducing each component to at most 255 does not guarantee that the squared-distance sum fits 65535. Keep center differences, radius sums and inverse-mass sums representable, and keep inv_mass_q8 * 255 within 32767 in the weight calculation; the sample uses 64.

kq2dc_overlap_circle

Approximate interior overlap using reduced center distance and the radius sum.

Syntax

c
u8 kq2dc_overlap_circle(const KQCircleBody2D* a, const KQCircleBody2D* b);

Parameters

a

Valid pointer to the first circle.

b

Valid pointer to the second circle.

Return value

Returns 1 for interior overlap and 0 for touching or separated shapes.

Conditions and limits

Choose consistent integer units for positions, radii, half extents, velocities and gravity. One step is one simulation tick. The samples use one unit per pixel. These routines neither convert positions to Q8.8 automatically nor render them.

Circle distance and normals are integer approximations. Reducing each component to at most 255 does not guarantee that the squared-distance sum fits 65535. Keep center differences, radius sums and inverse-mass sums representable, and keep inv_mass_q8 * 255 within 32767 in the weight calculation; the sample uses 64.

Requires two valid pointers and positive radii. Activity and mass are ignored. Reduction and integer square roots can differ from an exact geometric distance test.

    balls[1].x=18; result[5]=kq2dc_overlap_circle(&balls[0],&balls[1]);

A red radius-6 circle moves from center (24,24) on the left to (54,24) on the right. Local bounds are (4,4)..(60,60). The right wall clamps the center to 54 and changes X velocity from 32 to -15: wall restitution 128/256 is followed by damping 255/256. Panel origins are screen (8,48)/(88,48). DMG shows the circle and boundary in black.

Declaration notes (original source)
Compare a reduced integer center distance with the reduced radius sum.
Valid pointers and positive radii are required; activity and mass are ignored.
This approximate test requires representable differences, radius sums and
squared-distance sum. Touching at the computed distance returns false.

kitaqgb/lib/physics2d_circle.c:397

c
u8 kq2dc_overlap_circle(const KQCircleBody2D* a, const KQCircleBody2D* b)
{
    s16 dx;
    s16 dy;
    s16 sdx;
    s16 sdy;
    u8 shift;
    u16 adx;
    u16 ady;
    u16 dist_sq;
    u16 dist_scaled;
    s16 radius_sum;
    u16 radius_sum_scaled;

    dx = (s16)(b->x - a->x);
    dy = (s16)(b->y - a->y);
    sdx = dx;
    sdy = dy;
    shift = kq2dc__reduce_vector(&sdx, &sdy);

    adx = (u16)kq2dc__abs_s16(sdx);
    ady = (u16)kq2dc__abs_s16(sdy);
    dist_sq = (u16)((adx * adx) + (ady * ady));
    dist_scaled = kq2dc__isqrt_u16(dist_sq);

    radius_sum = (s16)(a->radius + b->radius);
    radius_sum_scaled = kq2dc__scale_down_positive(radius_sum, shift);

    if (dist_scaled >= radius_sum_scaled) return 0;
    return 1;
}

Integrate circles, resolve bounds and circle contacts, then apply linear damping.

Syntax

void kq2dc_step(KQCircleWorld2D* world);

Parameters

world

Pointer to the world holding the body array and simulation settings.

Return value

No return value. This entry describes the fields updated and when they take effect.

Conditions and limits

Choose consistent integer units for positions, radii, half extents, velocities and gravity. One step is one simulation tick. The samples use one unit per pixel. These routines neither convert positions to Q8.8 automatically nor render them.

A world borrows its array. The caller allocates and owns body storage and keeps it alive. Initializing a world does not initialize its array elements.

Circle distance and normals are integer approximations. Reducing each component to at most 255 does not guarantee that the squared-distance sum fits 65535. Keep center differences, radius sums and inverse-mass sums representable, and keep inv_mass_q8 * 255 within 32767 in the weight calculation; the sample uses 64.

Finally snaps velocity components in -1..1 to zero. Even damping 255 loses some speed. Overlaps between resting circles can remain. Static circles are also moved inside enabled bounds. Zero iterations means one pass; NULL world/array is ignored. This discrete, quantized solver can visit contacts in a different order as velocities change.

Declaration notes (original source)
Integrate active dynamic bodies, apply bounds, solve contacts, then damp
velocity and snap components in -1..1 to zero. Zero solver iterations means one.
Pairs with both velocities zero are skipped, so resting overlaps can remain.
Bounds can reposition static bodies; null world/array inputs are ignored.

kitaqgb/lib/physics2d_circle.c:433

c
void kq2dc_step(KQCircleWorld2D* world)
{
    KQCircleBody2D* bodies;
    u8 count;
    u8 i;
    u8 iterations;
    u8 it;

    if (world == 0) return;
    if (world->bodies == 0) return;

    bodies = world->bodies;
    count = world->body_count;

    for (i = 0; i < count; i++)
    {
        KQCircleBody2D* body = &bodies[(__safe_index u8)i];
        if (body->active == 0) continue;
        if (body->inv_mass_q8 <= 0)
        {
            if (world->use_bounds != 0) kq2dc__resolve_bounds(world, body);
            continue;
        }

        body->vx = (s16)(body->vx + world->gravity_x);
        body->vy = (s16)(body->vy + world->gravity_y);
        body->vx = kq2dc__clamp_abs(body->vx, world->max_speed);
        body->vy = kq2dc__clamp_abs(body->vy, world->max_speed);

        body->x = (s16)(body->x + body->vx);
        body->y = (s16)(body->y + body->vy);

        if (world->use_bounds != 0) kq2dc__resolve_bounds(world, body);
    }

    iterations = world->solver_iterations;
    if (iterations == 0) iterations = 1;

    for (it = 0; it < iterations; it++)
    {
        for (i = 0; i < count; i++)
        {
            KQCircleBody2D* a = &bodies[(__safe_index u8)i];
            if (a->active == 0) continue;
            if (a->vx == 0 && a->vy == 0) continue;

            if (world->use_bounds != 0) kq2dc__resolve_bounds(world, a);

            {
                u8 j;
                for (j = 0; j < count; j++)
                {
                    KQCircleBody2D* b = &bodies[(__safe_index u8)j];
                    s16 radius_sum;
                    if (j == i) continue;
                    if (b->active == 0) continue;
                    // Avoid revisiting an earlier moving body, but still allow a moving body
                    // to resolve against a stationary slot with a lower index. Velocities are live
                    // solver state, so contact ordering can change which later pairs are visited.
                    if (j < i && (b->vx != 0 || b->vy != 0)) continue;
                    radius_sum = (s16)(a->radius + b->radius);
                    if (kq2dc__abs_s16((s16)(b->x - a->x)) >= radius_sum) continue;
                    if (kq2dc__abs_s16((s16)(b->y - a->y)) >= radius_sum) continue;
                    kq2dc__resolve_pair(a, b);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    for (i = 0; i < count; i++)
    {
        KQCircleBody2D* body = &bodies[(__safe_index u8)i];
        if (body->active == 0) continue;
        if (body->inv_mass_q8 <= 0) continue;

        body->vx = kq2dc__mul_q8(body->vx, world->linear_damping_q8);
        body->vy = kq2dc__mul_q8(body->vy, world->linear_damping_q8);

        if (body->vx >= -1 && body->vx <= 1) body->vx = 0;
        if (body->vy >= -1 && body->vy <= 1) body->vy = 0;

        if (world->use_bounds != 0) kq2dc__resolve_bounds(world, body);
    }
}

physics3d.h — 3D AABB physics

Physics for nonrotating 3D boxes represented by centers and per-axis half extents. Mass/inverse mass weight contacts, restitution_q8 controls bounce and ax/ay/az provide persistent acceleration. Rendering is separate. The sample draws front and top views of the same body to show depth movement and wall bounce.

Choose consistent integer units for positions, radii, half extents, velocities and gravity. One step is one simulation tick. The samples use one unit per pixel. These routines neither convert positions to Q8.8 automatically nor render them.

physics3d.c resides in ROM bank 2. The sample uses an MBC5 128 KB ROM, includes that implementation first and places main in bank 0. Do not change the ROM mapping externally during a call.

last_impact_speed records the maximum closing speed along a contact axis. Integration clears it for active dynamic bodies; static and inactive bodies retain it. Neither break_speed nor KQ3D_BODY_BROKEN triggers automatic destruction. The game decides when to break a body and changes flags/active itself.

void kq3d_body_set_mass(KQBody3D* body, s16 mass_q8)
{
    if (body == 0) return;

    body->mass_q8 = mass_q8;
    if (mass_q8 <= 0)
    {
        body->inv_mass_q8 = 0;
        return;
    }

    if (mass_q8 < 64) mass_q8 = 64;
    body->inv_mass_q8 = (s16)(32767 / mass_q8);
    if (body->inv_mass_q8 <= 0) body->inv_mass_q8 = 1;
}

kq3d_integrate_body

Clear one active dynamic body’s impact, add world gravity and body acceleration, clamp each velocity axis and advance position.

Syntax

c
void kq3d_integrate_body(KQWorld3D* world, KQBody3D* body);

Parameters

world

Pointer to the world holding the body array and simulation settings.

body

Pointer to the body to modify. Fields not used by this operation are retained.

Return value

No return value. This entry describes the fields updated and when they take effect.

Conditions and limits

Choose consistent integer units for positions, radii, half extents, velocities and gravity. One step is one simulation tick. The samples use one unit per pixel. These routines neither convert positions to Q8.8 automatically nor render them.

Keep sums, differences, combined half extents and contact-correction products within signed 16-bit range. Velocity limits apply after addition and cannot prevent overflow during that addition.

Box integration and collision routines use shared scratch storage. Do not re-enter these physics routines from an interrupt.

physics3d.c resides in ROM bank 2. The sample uses an MBC5 128 KB ROM, includes that implementation first and places main in bank 0. Do not change the ROM mapping externally during a call.

last_impact_speed records the maximum closing speed along a contact axis. Integration clears it for active dynamic bodies; static and inactive bodies retain it. Neither break_speed nor KQ3D_BODY_BROKEN triggers automatic destruction. The game decides when to break a body and changes flags/active itself.

ax/ay/az persist and apply again on the next integration. This function alone does not resolve contacts. NULL, inactive and static bodies are not modified.

Usage example

kitaqgb/lib/physics3d.c:357

c
u8 kq3d_overlap_aabb(const KQBody3D* a, const KQBody3D* b)
{
    s16 dx = kq3d__abs_s16((s16)(b->x - a->x));
    s16 dy = kq3d__abs_s16((s16)(b->y - a->y));
    s16 dz = kq3d__abs_s16((s16)(b->z - a->z));

    s16 sx = (s16)(a->half_x + b->half_x);
    s16 sy = (s16)(a->half_y + b->half_y);
    s16 sz = (s16)(a->half_z + b->half_z);

    if (dx >= sx) return 0;
    if (dy >= sy) return 0;
    if (dz >= sz) return 0;
    return 1;
}
kq3d_step

Integrate active dynamic bodies and resolve contact correction, bounce and impact records among active world entries.

Syntax

c
void kq3d_step(KQWorld3D* world);

Parameters

world

Pointer to the world holding the body array and simulation settings.

Return value

No return value. This entry describes the fields updated and when they take effect.

Conditions and limits

Choose consistent integer units for positions, radii, half extents, velocities and gravity. One step is one simulation tick. The samples use one unit per pixel. These routines neither convert positions to Q8.8 automatically nor render them.

A world borrows its array. The caller allocates and owns body storage and keeps it alive. Initializing a world does not initialize its array elements.

Keep sums, differences, combined half extents and contact-correction products within signed 16-bit range. Velocity limits apply after addition and cannot prevent overflow during that addition.

Box integration and collision routines use shared scratch storage. Do not re-enter these physics routines from an interrupt.

physics3d.c resides in ROM bank 2. The sample uses an MBC5 128 KB ROM, includes that implementation first and places main in bank 0. Do not change the ROM mapping externally during a call.

Contacts use the least-penetrating axis, preferring X, then Y, then Z on ties. Only closing motion produces a bounce, using inverse masses and the average restitution clamped to 0..256. Fast tunnelling, rotation, angular momentum and friction are not handled.

last_impact_speed records the maximum closing speed along a contact axis. Integration clears it for active dynamic bodies; static and inactive bodies retain it. Neither break_speed nor KQ3D_BODY_BROKEN triggers automatic destruction. The game decides when to break a body and changes flags/active itself.

A NULL world or array is ignored. A zero solver_iterations value still performs one contact pass.

The intermediate impact*(256+restitution) and correction*inverse-mass products are also s16. Keep products within 32767; for example, with restitution 256 keep impact at most 63.

Usage example

c
kq3d_step(&world);
    result[16]=bodies[0].x; result[17]=bodies[0].y; result[18]=bodies[0].z;
    result[19]=bodies[0].vx; result[20]=bodies[0].vz;
    result[21]=bodies[0].last_impact_speed; result[22]=bodies[0].flags;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

X velocity bounces from 16 to -14 while Z velocity stays 8. Impact is 16, but flags remain zero despite break_speed=1. Panel origins are screen (8,48)/(88,48). All marks are black on DMG.

kitaqgb/lib/physics3d.h:61

Declaration notes (original source)
Integrate active dynamic bodies and reset their impact values, then solve
each active unordered pair for the configured passes (zero means one).
Static bodies retain previous impact maxima until the game clears them.
Acceleration persists; flags and break thresholds remain game-owned.
This discrete solver shares non-reentrant ASM scratch and can miss fast crossings.

kitaqgb/lib/physics3d.c:492

c
void kq3d_step(KQWorld3D* world)
{
    if (world == 0) return;
    if (world->bodies == 0) return;

    KQBody3D* bodies = world->bodies;
    u8 count = world->body_count;

    u8 i;
    for (i = 0; i < count; i++)
    {
        KQBody3D* b = &bodies[(__safe_index u8)i];
        if (b->active == 0) continue;
        if (b->inv_mass_q8 <= 0) continue;

        b->last_impact_speed = 0;
        kq3d_asm_value = b->vx;
        kq3d_asm_operand = world->gravity_x;
        kq3d_add_s16_asm();
        kq3d_asm_operand = b->ax;
        kq3d_add_s16_asm();
        kq3d_asm_limit = world->max_speed;
        kq3d_clamp_abs_s16_asm();
        b->vx = kq3d_asm_value;

        kq3d_asm_value = b->vy;
        kq3d_asm_operand = world->gravity_y;
        kq3d_add_s16_asm();
        kq3d_asm_operand = b->ay;
        kq3d_add_s16_asm();
        kq3d_asm_limit = world->max_speed;
        kq3d_clamp_abs_s16_asm();
        b->vy = kq3d_asm_value;

        kq3d_asm_value = b->vz;
        kq3d_asm_operand = world->gravity_z;
        kq3d_add_s16_asm();
        kq3d_asm_operand = b->az;
        kq3d_add_s16_asm();
        kq3d_asm_limit = world->max_speed;
        kq3d_clamp_abs_s16_asm();
        b->vz = kq3d_asm_value;

        kq3d_asm_value = b->x;
        kq3d_asm_operand = b->vx;
        kq3d_add_s16_asm();
        b->x = kq3d_asm_value;

        kq3d_asm_value = b->y;
        kq3d_asm_operand = b->vy;
        kq3d_add_s16_asm();
        b->y = kq3d_asm_value;

        kq3d_asm_value = b->z;
        kq3d_asm_operand = b->vz;
        kq3d_add_s16_asm();
        b->z = kq3d_asm_value;
    }

    u8 iterations = world->solver_iterations;
    if (iterations == 0) iterations = 1;

    u8 it;
    for (it = 0; it < iterations; it++)
    {
        for (i = 0; i < count; i++)
        {
            KQBody3D* a = &bodies[(__safe_index u8)i];
            if (a->active == 0) continue;

            u8 j;
            for (j = (u8)(i + 1); j < count; j++)
            {
                KQBody3D* b = &bodies[(__safe_index u8)j];
                if (b->active == 0) continue;
                kq3d__resolve_pair(a, b);
            }
        }
    }
}

raster.h — Scroll tables for bands and scanlines

The Raster library provides an eight-entry band table and a LineX renderer that changes X on all 144 visible lines. Bands suit fixed HUDs, parallax, window changes and CGB color regions. LineX suits rippling titles and screen effects. Choose one driver; do not run both together.

Include raster.h and compile raster.c plus scroll.c. A shared table holds up to eight bands. Do not interleave direct Scroll_Split* or __scroll_split_* calls while building with Raster_*; they bypass the wrapper count and last-line bookkeeping.

Rebuild in VBlank or another interval where you control the display impact: clear, add entries, then commit. Clear stops the active splits too; this is not editing an independent back buffer. LY schedules an interrupt, and register writes take additional time. Use the separate Raster_LineX* family for per-scanline wave rendering; do not run both drivers together.

A scanline wave and an animated title entrance

Changing background X on each screen line bends pillars and lettering into a wave. This can introduce a warp, a boss encounter or a title. The preview below cycles through eight captured images; the ROM advances the wave phase on every frame.

Raster_Push operations schedule up to eight bands. Use Raster_LineXRunFrame for a separate horizontal offset on every scanline. Sprites and the window do not bend. The renderer occupies the CPU and masks interrupts during all 144 visible lines, so update game logic and audio between calls.

Continuous wave sample

Title entrance sample

The title enters from the right with a large wave, changes to a small ripple and then settles. It includes raster_wave.c from the same directory, so keep both source files together. The API entries below include build commands and individual usage notes.

Include raster.h and compile raster.c plus scroll.c. A shared table holds up to eight bands. Do not interleave direct Scroll_Split* or __scroll_split_* calls while building with Raster_*; they bypass the wrapper count and last-line bookkeeping.

Rebuild in VBlank or another interval where you control the display impact: clear, add entries, then commit. Clear stops the active splits too; this is not editing an independent back buffer. LY schedules an interrupt, and register writes take additional time. Use the separate Raster_LineX* family for per-scanline wave rendering; do not run both drivers together.

Raster_BuildHudBottom

Build a scrolling upper playfield and fixed bottom HUD. LY=0 uses camera coordinates; hud_y switches to background (0,0).

Syntax

c
u8 Raster_BuildHudBottom(u8 hud_y, u8 camera_x, u8 camera_y);

Parameters

hud_y

Split line, 1..143. Zero or 144 and above return BAD_RANGE.

camera_x

Background scroll byte, 0..255. SCX/SCY specify where to read the background map, not a screen-space position. Coordinates wrap across the 256-pixel background.

camera_y

Background scroll byte, 0..255. SCX/SCY specify where to read the background map, not a screen-space position. Coordinates wrap across the 256-pixel background.

Return value

Return KQ_RASTER_OK (0) on success or an error status 1..4. See the function constraints and Raster_GetLastError.

Conditions and limits

Include raster.h and compile raster.c plus scroll.c. A shared table holds up to eight bands. Do not interleave direct Scroll_Split* or __scroll_split_* calls while building with Raster_*; they bypass the wrapper count and last-line bookkeeping.

Rebuild in VBlank or another interval where you control the display impact: clear, add entries, then commit. Clear stops the active splits too; this is not editing an independent back buffer. LY schedules an interrupt, and register writes take additional time. Use the separate Raster_LineX* family for per-scanline wave rendering; do not run both drivers together.

Status codes are 0 OK, 1 FULL, 2 BAD_LY, 3 UNSORTED and 4 BAD_RANGE. Push operations check LY range, capacity and ordering in that order. A rejected entry does not grow the table. A later successful push or clear resets the error to zero, so check each return value when it occurs.

Valid parameters stop existing splits, clear the table and add the new bands. Invalid parameters preserve the table and count while storing BAD_RANGE. A successful build still requires Raster_Commit.

Usage example

c
Raster_BuildHudBottom(96,8,8);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Rows from 96 downward stay fixed. Camera (8,8) places the upper rectangles at (24,8) and (24,72), while the bottom rectangle stays at (32,112). FIXED BOTTOM HUD stays at the bottom.

Complete example program

Build command

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\raster_bands_hud_bottom.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\raster_bands.gb --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k --no-cache --no-disasm
Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/raster.h:73

Declaration notes (original source)
Build a scrolling upper playfield and fixed bottom HUD after validating the split.

kitaqgb/lib/raster.c:183

c
u8 Raster_BuildHudBottom(u8 hud_y, u8 camera_x, u8 camera_y)
{
    u8 r;

    if (hud_y == 0) return Raster_SetError(KQ_RASTER_BAD_RANGE);
    if (hud_y >= 144) return Raster_SetError(KQ_RASTER_BAD_RANGE);

    Raster_Clear();
    r = Raster_Push(0, camera_x, camera_y);
    if (r != KQ_RASTER_OK) return r;
    return Raster_Push(hud_y, 0, 0);
}

c
u8 Raster_BuildParallax2(u8 split_y, u8 far_scx, u8 near_scx, u8 scy)
{
    u8 r;

    if (split_y == 0) return Raster_SetError(KQ_RASTER_BAD_RANGE);
    if (split_y >= 144) return Raster_SetError(KQ_RASTER_BAD_RANGE);

    Raster_Clear();
    r = Raster_Push(0, far_scx, scy);
    if (r != KQ_RASTER_OK) return r;
    return Raster_Push(split_y, near_scx, scy);
}
Raster_BuildParallax3

Register scx0, scx1 and scx2 for bands beginning at LY=0, y1 and y2. Give far, middle and near layers different horizontal offsets while sharing Y scroll.

Syntax

c
u8 Raster_BuildParallax3(u8 y1, u8 y2, u8 scx0, u8 scx1, u8 scx2, u8 scy);

Parameters

y1

Split line; require 1 <= y1 < y2 <= 143.

y2

Split line; require 1 <= y1 < y2 <= 143.

scx0

Background scroll byte, 0..255. SCX/SCY specify where to read the background map, not a screen-space position. Coordinates wrap across the 256-pixel background.

scx1

Background scroll byte, 0..255. SCX/SCY specify where to read the background map, not a screen-space position. Coordinates wrap across the 256-pixel background.

scx2

Background scroll byte, 0..255. SCX/SCY specify where to read the background map, not a screen-space position. Coordinates wrap across the 256-pixel background.

scy

Background scroll byte, 0..255. SCX/SCY specify where to read the background map, not a screen-space position. Coordinates wrap across the 256-pixel background.

Return value

Return KQ_RASTER_OK (0) on success or an error status 1..4. See the function constraints and Raster_GetLastError.

Conditions and limits

Include raster.h and compile raster.c plus scroll.c. A shared table holds up to eight bands. Do not interleave direct Scroll_Split* or __scroll_split_* calls while building with Raster_*; they bypass the wrapper count and last-line bookkeeping.

Rebuild in VBlank or another interval where you control the display impact: clear, add entries, then commit. Clear stops the active splits too; this is not editing an independent back buffer. LY schedules an interrupt, and register writes take additional time. Use the separate Raster_LineX* family for per-scanline wave rendering; do not run both drivers together.

Status codes are 0 OK, 1 FULL, 2 BAD_LY, 3 UNSORTED and 4 BAD_RANGE. Push operations check LY range, capacity and ordering in that order. A rejected entry does not grow the table. A later successful push or clear resets the error to zero, so check each return value when it occurs.

Valid parameters stop existing splits, clear the table and add the new bands. Invalid parameters preserve the table and count while storing BAD_RANGE. A successful build still requires Raster_Commit.

Usage example

c
Raster_BuildParallax3(64,104,0,8,16,0);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Scheduled lines 64 and 104 select X offsets 0, 8 and 16. Rectangles at (32,16), (24,80) and (16,112) show the increasing displacement across three bands.

c
u8 Raster_BuildParallax3(u8 y1, u8 y2, u8 scx0, u8 scx1, u8 scx2, u8 scy)
{
    u8 r;

    if (y1 == 0) return Raster_SetError(KQ_RASTER_BAD_RANGE);
    if (y2 >= 144) return Raster_SetError(KQ_RASTER_BAD_RANGE);
    if (y2 <= y1) return Raster_SetError(KQ_RASTER_BAD_RANGE);

    Raster_Clear();
    r = Raster_Push(0, scx0, scy);
    if (r != KQ_RASTER_OK) return r;
    r = Raster_Push(y1, scx1, scy);
    if (r != KQ_RASTER_OK) return r;
    return Raster_Push(y2, scx2, scy);
}

Conditions and limits

Include raster.h and compile raster.c plus scroll.c. A shared table holds up to eight bands. Do not interleave direct Scroll_Split* or __scroll_split_* calls while building with Raster_*; they bypass the wrapper count and last-line bookkeeping.

Raster_Commit

Activate the constructed shared table. Even if a previous push failed, entries successfully added before it are activated; caller code must check each registration.

Syntax

c
u8 Raster_Commit();

Return value

Return the last stored error. Zero does not prove that every earlier registration succeeded.

Conditions and limits

Include raster.h and compile raster.c plus scroll.c. A shared table holds up to eight bands. Do not interleave direct Scroll_Split* or __scroll_split_* calls while building with Raster_*; they bypass the wrapper count and last-line bookkeeping.

Rebuild in VBlank or another interval where you control the display impact: clear, add entries, then commit. Clear stops the active splits too; this is not editing an independent back buffer. LY schedules an interrupt, and register writes take additional time. Use the separate Raster_LineX* family for per-scanline wave rendering; do not run both drivers together.

Status codes are 0 OK, 1 FULL, 2 BAD_LY, 3 UNSORTED and 4 BAD_RANGE. Push operations check LY range, capacity and ordering in that order. A rejected entry does not grow the table. A later successful push or clear resets the error to zero, so check each return value when it occurs.

A nonempty table sets the VBlank/STAT IE bits and executes EI, enabling interrupts; other IE bits are preserved. An empty table disables split scheduling without restoring the global interrupt configuration.

Raster_LineXGetOffset

Calculate SCX for a requested line without changing state, the display or the phase.

Syntax

c
u8 Raster_LineXGetOffset(const RasterLineX* effect, u8 ly);

Parameters

effect

Pointer to an initialized RasterLineX that remains valid throughout the call.

ly

Line coordinate to query (0..255); visible lines are 0..143. The lookup wraps at the wave period instead of reporting a range error.

Return value

Eight-bit SCX equal to base X plus that row’s displacement. The sample lookup at phase 8, line 0 returns 17.

Conditions and limits

SCX is an eight-bit value and the background wraps at 256 pixels. Negative displacements use modulo-256 byte values. Populate the map beyond the visible viewport as well.

The effect changes horizontal background scrolling; sprites and the window do not bend. RunFrame owns the CPU and masks interrupts during all 144 visible lines. Update game logic and audio between calls, and do not combine this renderer with a STAT raster interrupt driver.

Images come from DMG and CGB runs in KOKURA. Every pixel of the 160×144 scene, including pillars and text, is compared with the expected per-line coordinates. Hardware timing has not been tested.

Place kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs under one parent directory and open PowerShell there. The ROM supports both DMG and CGB; select dmg or cgb with KOKURA --hardware.

Usage example

c
wave_lookup = Raster_LineXGetOffset(&wave, 0);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The pillars and letters bend horizontally by up to 24 pixels. One wave spans 64 scanlines, and its phase advances by one line per frame. CGB uses blue pillars and lettering. Look for a different horizontal offset on each row, rather than uniform movement of the whole screen.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\raster_wave.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\raster_wave.gb --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --no-cache --no-disasm
.\kokura\kokura-cli.exe .\out\raster_wave.gb --hardware cgb --run-frames 120 --png .\out\raster_wave.png
Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/raster.h:91

Declaration notes (original source)
Look up the selected periodic profile at LY + phase and add base X modulo
256. An unknown profile returns the unmodified base X.

kitaqgb/lib/raster.c:264

c
u8 Raster_LineXGetOffset(const RasterLineX* effect, u8 ly)
{
    u8 index;

    if (effect->profile == KQ_RASTER_LINE_X_TITLE) {
        index = (u8)((ly + effect->phase) & 15);
        return (u8)(effect->base_x + Raster_LineXXTitle[(__safe_index u8)index]);
    }

    if (effect->profile == KQ_RASTER_LINE_TRAVEL_GATE) {
        index = (u8)((ly + effect->phase) & 63);
        return (u8)(effect->base_x + Raster_LineXTravelGate[(__safe_index u8)index]);
    }

    return effect->base_x;
}

Raster_LineXRunFrame

Wait for VBlank and render the following 144 visible lines with per-line background X. Afterwards advance the divider counter and update phase at the selected interval.

Syntax

c
void Raster_LineXRunFrame(RasterLineX* effect);

Parameters

effect

Pointer to an initialized RasterLineX that remains valid throughout the call.

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

If the LCD is off, return immediately without changing the effect. Otherwise block until SCX has been updated for all 144 rows, restore the interrupt-enable state and synchronize the Scroll helper with the final SCX. Return does not guarantee that VBlank is active. Before writing directly to VRAM, wait for VBlank or use a transfer routine that manages safe access timing.

kitaqgb/lib/raster.h:96

Declaration notes (original source)
Render all 144 visible lines with one SCX write per line, then advance phase.
This foreground renderer masks interrupts during the visible frame. Do game
and audio work between calls; do not combine it with a STAT raster driver.
Returns without changing the effect when the LCD is off.

kitaqgb/lib/raster.c:298

c
void Raster_LineXRunFrame(RasterLineX* effect)
{
    u8 interrupt_state;
    if ((Raster_LineXLcdc & 0x80) == 0) return;
    Raster_LineXTable = Raster_LineXFlat;
    Raster_LineXMask = 15;
    if (effect->profile == KQ_RASTER_LINE_X_TITLE) {
        Raster_LineXTable = Raster_LineXXTitle;
    }
    if (effect->profile == KQ_RASTER_LINE_TRAVEL_GATE) {
        Raster_LineXTable = Raster_LineXTravelGate;
        Raster_LineXMask = 63;
    }
    Raster_LineXPhase = effect->phase;
    Raster_LineXBase = effect->base_x;
    interrupt_state = __critical_enter();
    __asm {
        PUSH_AF
        PUSH_BC
        PUSH_DE
        PUSH_HL
        // Use the current VBlank when the preceding frame ended there.
        // Waiting for another VBlank edge would leave every second frame flat.
raster_linex_vblank:
        LDH_A_MEM 0x44
        CP_IMM 144
        JR_C raster_linex_vblank
        LD_B_IMM 0
        LD_A_MEM Raster_LineXPhase
        LD_C_A
        LD_A_MEM Raster_LineXMask
        LD_D_A
        LD_A_MEM Raster_LineXBase
        LD_E_A
raster_linex_line:
        LD_A_B
        ADD_C
        AND_D
        LD_L_A
        LD_H_IMM 0
        PUSH_DE
        LD_A_MEM Raster_LineXTable
        LD_E_A
        LD_A_MEM Raster_LineXTable+1
        LD_D_A
        ADD_HL_DE
        POP_DE
        LD_A_HL
        ADD_E
        PUSH_AF
raster_linex_wait:
        LDH_A_MEM 0x44
        CP_B
        JR_NZ raster_linex_wait
        POP_AF
        LDH_MEM_A 0x43
        INC_B
        LD_A_B
        CP_IMM 144
        JR_NZ raster_linex_line
        POP_HL
        POP_DE
        POP_BC
        POP_AF
    }
    // Synchronize the scroll helper's tracked state with the last hardware write.
    __scroll_bg_x_set(Raster_LineXScx);
    __critical_leave(interrupt_state);
    effect->frame_counter++;
    if (effect->frame_counter >= effect->frame_divider) {
        effect->frame_counter = 0;
        effect->phase = (u8)(effect->phase + effect->phase_step);
    }
}
Raster_LineXSetPhase

Set the wave position directly, preserving base X, speed and the divider counter.

Syntax

c
void Raster_LineXSetPhase(RasterLineX* effect, u8 phase);

Parameters

effect

Pointer to an initialized RasterLineX that remains valid throughout the call.

phase

Eight-bit phase value; the selected wave repeats every 16 or 64 steps.

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

SCX is an eight-bit value and the background wraps at 256 pixels. Negative displacements use modulo-256 byte values. Populate the map beyond the visible viewport as well.

The effect changes horizontal background scrolling; sprites and the window do not bend. RunFrame owns the CPU and masks interrupts during all 144 visible lines. Update game logic and audio between calls, and do not combine this renderer with a STAT raster interrupt driver.

Images come from DMG and CGB runs in KOKURA. Every pixel of the 160×144 scene, including pillars and text, is compared with the expected per-line coordinates. Hardware timing has not been tested.

Place kitaqgb, kokura and kitaq-docs under one parent directory and open PowerShell there. The ROM supports both DMG and CGB; select dmg or cgb with KOKURA --hardware.

Usage example

c
Raster_LineXSetPhase(&wave, 8);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The pillars and letters bend horizontally by up to 24 pixels. One wave spans 64 scanlines, and its phase advances by one line per frame. CGB uses blue pillars and lettering. Look for a different horizontal offset on each row, rather than uniform movement of the whole screen.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\raster_wave.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\raster_wave.gb --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --no-cache --no-disasm
.\kokura\kokura-cli.exe .\out\raster_wave.gb --hardware cgb --run-frames 120 --png .\out\raster_wave.png

Raster_Push

Append one band that changes background SCX/SCY at the scheduled LY. This background-only operation does not change the window or colors.

Syntax

c
u8 Raster_Push(u8 ly, u8 scx, u8 scy);

Parameters

ly

Visible scheduled line, 0..143, strictly greater than the previous entry in the table. A first entry at LY=0 is applied by VBlank handling to establish the frame-start state.

scx

Background scroll byte, 0..255. SCX/SCY specify where to read the background map, not a screen-space position. Coordinates wrap across the 256-pixel background.

scy

Background scroll byte, 0..255. SCX/SCY specify where to read the background map, not a screen-space position. Coordinates wrap across the 256-pixel background.

Return value

Return KQ_RASTER_OK (0) on success or an error status 1..4. See the function constraints and Raster_GetLastError.

Conditions and limits

Include raster.h and compile raster.c plus scroll.c. A shared table holds up to eight bands. Do not interleave direct Scroll_Split* or __scroll_split_* calls while building with Raster_*; they bypass the wrapper count and last-line bookkeeping.

Rebuild in VBlank or another interval where you control the display impact: clear, add entries, then commit. Clear stops the active splits too; this is not editing an independent back buffer. LY schedules an interrupt, and register writes take additional time. Use the separate Raster_LineX* family for per-scanline wave rendering; do not run both drivers together.

Status codes are 0 OK, 1 FULL, 2 BAD_LY, 3 UNSORTED and 4 BAD_RANGE. Push operations check LY range, capacity and ordering in that order. A rejected entry does not grow the table. A later successful push or clear resets the error to zero, so check each return value when it occurs.

Usage example

c
Raster_Push(0,0,0);Raster_Push(64,8,0);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Red rectangles (black on DMG), each 24 by 16 pixels, appear at (32,16), (24,80) and (16,112). Lower bands shift farther left. Internal results record count 3, error 0 and commit result 0.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\raster_bands_bands.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\raster_bands.gb --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k --no-cache --no-disasm
Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/raster.h:50

Declaration notes (original source)
Append a validated background-scroll band and advance the monotonic-LY
bookkeeping. A successful append clears the previous error.

kitaqgb/lib/raster.c:95

c
u8 Raster_Push(u8 ly, u8 scx, u8 scy)
{
    u8 r;

    r = Raster_CheckPush(ly);
    if (r != KQ_RASTER_OK) return r;

    Scroll_SplitPush(ly, scx, scy);

    Raster_LastLyValue = ly;
    Raster_HasLastLy = 1;
    Raster_CountValue++;
    Raster_LastErrorValue = KQ_RASTER_OK;
    return KQ_RASTER_OK;
}
Raster_PushBgColor0

Append a band that changes color zero of CGB background palette zero during the frame. It does not select a different palette or change its other three colors. Registration on DMG does not produce a color effect.

Syntax

c
u8 Raster_PushBgColor0(u8 ly, u16 rgb15);

Parameters

ly

Visible scheduled line, 0..143, strictly greater than the previous entry in the table. A first entry at LY=0 is applied by VBlank handling to establish the frame-start state.

rgb15

RGB15: red in bits 0..4, green in 5..9, blue in 10..14. 0x001F is red, 0x03E0 green and 0x7C00 blue. The input is not range-checked.

Return value

Return KQ_RASTER_OK (0) on success or an error status 1..4. See the function constraints and Raster_GetLastError.

Conditions and limits

Include raster.h and compile raster.c plus scroll.c. A shared table holds up to eight bands. Do not interleave direct Scroll_Split* or __scroll_split_* calls while building with Raster_*; they bypass the wrapper count and last-line bookkeeping.

Rebuild in VBlank or another interval where you control the display impact: clear, add entries, then commit. Clear stops the active splits too; this is not editing an independent back buffer. LY schedules an interrupt, and register writes take additional time. Use the separate Raster_LineX* family for per-scanline wave rendering; do not run both drivers together.

Status codes are 0 OK, 1 FULL, 2 BAD_LY, 3 UNSORTED and 4 BAD_RANGE. Push operations check LY range, capacity and ordering in that order. A rejected entry does not grow the table. A later successful push or clear resets the error to zero, so check each return value when it occurs.

Color updates use BCPS/BCPD and do not preserve the previous BCPS index. Set the index explicitly when foreground code writes palettes too. The handler waits for an accessible LCD mode, so the visible color boundary can follow the scheduled LY.

Usage example

c
Raster_PushBgColor0(0,0x7C00);Raster_PushBgColor0(64,0x001F);Raster_PushBgColor0(112,0x03E0);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

In the verified CGB normal-speed capture, rows 0..65 are blue, 66..113 red and 114..143 green. Scheduled LY values are 0, 64 and 112; interrupt and palette-access latency contribute to the visible boundaries. There is no DMG color version.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell

.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\raster_bands_color.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\raster_bands.gb --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k --no-cache --no-disasm

Raster_PushBgWindowScreen

Update background scroll and window coordinates in a single band. The wrapper adds BG and WIN and converts window screen X to WX.

Syntax

c
u8 Raster_PushBgWindowScreen(u8 ly, u8 scx, u8 scy, u8 screen_x, u8 screen_y, u8 flags);

Parameters

ly

Visible scheduled line, 0..143, strictly greater than the previous entry in the table. A first entry at LY=0 is applied by VBlank handling to establish the frame-start state.

scx

Background scroll byte, 0..255. SCX/SCY specify where to read the background map, not a screen-space position. Coordinates wrap across the 256-pixel background.

scy

Background scroll byte, 0..255. SCX/SCY specify where to read the background map, not a screen-space position. Coordinates wrap across the 256-pixel background.

screen_x

Screen X coordinate of the window left edge. The wrapper adds seven to form WX. Normally use 0..159. Values of 249 or more wrap during byte addition; do not use them as a way to hide the window.

screen_y

Window WY in pixels from the top edge. Unlike X, Y needs no addition of seven. WY values of 144 or more have no start line in the visible area.

flags

Normally pass WIN_SHOW or WIN_HIDE. The wrapper adds WIN, so zero is sufficient to update coordinates without changing visibility. Other supported bits pass through; avoid unintended BG or color operations.

Return value

Return KQ_RASTER_OK (0) on success or an error status 1..4. See the function constraints and Raster_GetLastError.

Conditions and limits

Include raster.h and compile raster.c plus scroll.c. A shared table holds up to eight bands. Do not interleave direct Scroll_Split* or __scroll_split_* calls while building with Raster_*; they bypass the wrapper count and last-line bookkeeping.

Rebuild in VBlank or another interval where you control the display impact: clear, add entries, then commit. Clear stops the active splits too; this is not editing an independent back buffer. LY schedules an interrupt, and register writes take additional time. Use the separate Raster_LineX* family for per-scanline wave rendering; do not run both drivers together.

Status codes are 0 OK, 1 FULL, 2 BAD_LY, 3 UNSORTED and 4 BAD_RANGE. Push operations check LY range, capacity and ordering in that order. A rejected entry does not grow the table. A later successful push or clear resets the error to zero, so check each return value when it occurs.

Usage example

c
Raster_PushBgWindowScreen(0,8,0,24,48,KQ_RASTER_WIN_SHOW);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Background X=8 moves the red background rectangle to (24,16). The window origin remains (24,48), keeping its blue rectangle at (32,56). This shows the independent coordinate systems.

Raster_PushEx

Append an extended band that performs the background, window, visibility or color operations selected by flags. Use Raster_Push for ordinary background-only changes with fewer arguments.

Syntax

c
u8 Raster_PushEx(u8 ly, u8 scx, u8 scy, u8 wx, u8 wy, u8 flags);

Parameters

ly

Visible scheduled line, 0..143, strictly greater than the previous entry in the table. A first entry at LY=0 is applied by VBlank handling to establish the frame-start state.

scx

Background scroll byte, 0..255. SCX/SCY specify where to read the background map, not a screen-space position. Coordinates wrap across the 256-pixel background.

scy

Background scroll byte, 0..255. SCX/SCY specify where to read the background map, not a screen-space position. Coordinates wrap across the 256-pixel background.

wx

Raw hardware WX value. Add seven to an ordinary screen X coordinate; WX=7 places the window at the left edge. This function does not clamp or validate WX.

wy

Window WY in pixels from the top edge. Unlike X, Y needs no addition of seven. WY values of 144 or more have no start line in the visible area.

flags

Flags: BG=1 updates background scroll, WIN=2 updates WX/WY, WIN_SHOW=4 shows the window, WIN_HIDE=8 hides it, BG_COLOR0=16 updates CGB background color zero. Unknown upper bits are discarded. With both SHOW and HIDE, SHOW is applied last. Color updates reuse SCX/SCY payload fields; do not combine them with ordinary background scrolling.

Return value

Return KQ_RASTER_OK (0) on success or an error status 1..4. See the function constraints and Raster_GetLastError.

Conditions and limits

Include raster.h and compile raster.c plus scroll.c. A shared table holds up to eight bands. Do not interleave direct Scroll_Split* or __scroll_split_* calls while building with Raster_*; they bypass the wrapper count and last-line bookkeeping.

Rebuild in VBlank or another interval where you control the display impact: clear, add entries, then commit. Clear stops the active splits too; this is not editing an independent back buffer. LY schedules an interrupt, and register writes take additional time. Use the separate Raster_LineX* family for per-scanline wave rendering; do not run both drivers together.

Status codes are 0 OK, 1 FULL, 2 BAD_LY, 3 UNSORTED and 4 BAD_RANGE. Push operations check LY range, capacity and ordering in that order. A rejected entry does not grow the table. A later successful push or clear resets the error to zero, so check each return value when it occurs.

Usage example

c
Raster_PushEx(104,16,0,7,0,KQ_RASTER_BG|KQ_RASTER_WIN_HIDE);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Red rectangles (black on DMG), each 24 by 16 pixels, appear at (32,16), (24,80) and (16,112). Lower bands shift farther left. Internal results record count 3, error 0 and commit result 0.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\raster_bands_bands.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\raster_bands.gb --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k --no-cache --no-disasm

kitaqgb/lib/raster.h:52

Declaration notes (original source)
Append a validated extended band after masking flags to supported operations.

kitaqgb/lib/raster.c:112

c
u8 Raster_PushEx(u8 ly, u8 scx, u8 scy, u8 wx, u8 wy, u8 flags)
{
    u8 r;

    r = Raster_CheckPush(ly);
    if (r != KQ_RASTER_OK) return r;

    // Masking removes unknown bits but does not reject conflicting supported operations.
    flags = (u8)(flags & KQ_RASTER_FLAG_MASK);
    Scroll_SplitPushEx(ly, scx, scy, wx, wy, flags);

    Raster_LastLyValue = ly;
    Raster_HasLastLy = 1;
    Raster_CountValue++;
    Raster_LastErrorValue = KQ_RASTER_OK;
    return KQ_RASTER_OK;
}

c
u8 Raster_PushWindowScreen(u8 ly, u8 screen_x, u8 screen_y, u8 flags);

Parameters

ly

Visible scheduled line, 0..143, strictly greater than the previous entry in the table. A first entry at LY=0 is applied by VBlank handling to establish the frame-start state.

screen_x

Screen X coordinate of the window left edge. The wrapper adds seven to form WX. Normally use 0..159. Values of 249 or more wrap during byte addition; do not use them as a way to hide the window.

screen_y

Window WY in pixels from the top edge. Unlike X, Y needs no addition of seven. WY values of 144 or more have no start line in the visible area.

flags

Normally pass WIN_SHOW or WIN_HIDE. The wrapper adds WIN, so zero is sufficient to update coordinates without changing visibility. Other supported bits pass through; avoid unintended BG or color operations.

Return value

Return KQ_RASTER_OK (0) on success or an error status 1..4. See the function constraints and Raster_GetLastError.

Conditions and limits

Include raster.h and compile raster.c plus scroll.c. A shared table holds up to eight bands. Do not interleave direct Scroll_Split* or __scroll_split_* calls while building with Raster_*; they bypass the wrapper count and last-line bookkeeping.

Rebuild in VBlank or another interval where you control the display impact: clear, add entries, then commit. Clear stops the active splits too; this is not editing an independent back buffer. LY schedules an interrupt, and register writes take additional time. Use the separate Raster_LineX* family for per-scanline wave rendering; do not run both drivers together.

Status codes are 0 OK, 1 FULL, 2 BAD_LY, 3 UNSORTED and 4 BAD_RANGE. Push operations check LY range, capacity and ordering in that order. A rejected entry does not grow the table. A later successful push or clear resets the error to zero, so check each return value when it occurs.

Usage example

c
Raster_PushWindowScreen(0,24,48,KQ_RASTER_WIN_SHOW);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Passing screen (24,48) directly produces the same blue window rectangle at (32,56) as the raw example. The library adds seven to X. The upper red background rectangle is at (32,16).

rpg.h — Random numbers, text, maps, saves and RPG/ADV/SLG services

Absolute text helpers draw directly on the background map. text_window opens a framed area, text_clear_rect fills a region, and text_print_xy writes tile bytes without control decoding. text_print_u8, text_print_u16 and text_print_s16 convert numbers to decimal with only the required cells. Reserve and clear a full field when replacing values of different lengths.

The RNG functions declared in rpg.h are implemented in lib/rng.c. They share the compiler's GB generator: rng_seed resets it, rng8/rng_next8 consume one byte, rng16/rng_next16 consume two, and rand_range/rng_range, rng_chance and weighted_choice adapt draws for gameplay choices. Compile rng.c with your program when calling these library functions. For reproducible tests, keep the seed and call order fixed; modulo-based choices do not promise exact probabilities.

RLE decoding uses count/value byte pairs and a zero count terminator. rle_decode reads an ordinary pointer into RAM; rle_decode_far reads a ROM-bank-qualified pointer into RAM; __rle_decode_vram expands banked input directly to VRAM with LCD-aware stores. The RAM functions live in lib/rle.c, while the direct VRAM operation is compiler-generated. All three return output bytes and require a valid stream and enough destination space.

Game-state storage declared in rpg.h is implemented by lib/flags.c. The three flag functions operate on 2048 independent Boolean bits; quest_state and quest_set_state operate on 64 independent bytes for game-defined stages. Compile flags.c when using them, keep IDs within those limits, and use a separate save system if progress must survive power-off.

Windowed dialogue shares one active rectangle, cursor and character-speed setting. text_open initializes the area, text_close erases it, and text_set_speed sets per-character VBlank waits. text_print and text_print_far interpret control streams; text_choice runs a blocking vertical selector. Load the tiles, fit the area and plan how the game handles these blocking calls.

Provides map/metatile drawing, scripts, SRAM saves and pathfinding. Ordinary cells are 8×8 pixels; metatiles are 16×16. Loading/drawing, movement masks and attack masks are separate operations; the game coordinates graphics loading and event execution.

Search uses about 4 KiB of shared, non-reentrant workspace. Limit maps to 1024 cells and explored distances to 254. Distance 0xFF means unreached, so a 255-step route is not representable. Cost/mask outputs need width*height writable bytes.

Defaults to four 512-byte slots, each with a six-byte header and up to 506 payload bytes. The sample uses MBC5 with 8 KiB SRAM. Calls finish with RAM disabled and do not restore its previous bank or enable state.

Menus support both blocking selection and separate input/draw calls driven by the game loop. The inventory menu displays item names and quantities.

camera_center

Center an ordinary-map cell in a 20×18-tile viewport, clamping at map edges.

Syntax

c
void camera_center(u8 x, u8 y);

Parameters

x

Cell X coordinate.

y

Cell Y coordinate.

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

The origin starts at max(x−10,0), max(y−9,0), clamps to map edges, then writes the low bytes of origin*8 to SCX/SCY. Metatile mode does not apply it. It does not stream new rows or columns into VRAM.

Usage example

c
camera_center(5,4);result[9]=*((u8*)0xFF43);result[10]=*((u8*)0xFF42);

Expected result

The left grid shows movement costs within three steps; the right shows a shortest route from S to G. Green asterisks trace nine steps around a red three-cell wall; blue digits show costs. DMG uses the same layout in black. RAM checks also demonstrate that the attack mask ignores walls.

kitaqgb/lib/map.c:105

c
void camera_center(u8 x, u8 y)
{
    u8 tile_x = 0;
    u8 tile_y = 0;
    u8 max_x = 0;
    u8 max_y = 0;

    map_camera_x = x;
    map_camera_y = y;

    if (map_loaded == 0) return;

    if (map_current.width > 20) max_x = (u8)(map_current.width - 20);
    if (map_current.height > 18) max_y = (u8)(map_current.height - 18);

    if (x > 10) tile_x = (u8)(x - 10);
    if (y > 9) tile_y = (u8)(y - 9);

    if (tile_x > max_x) tile_x = max_x;
    if (tile_y > max_y) tile_y = max_y;

    __scroll_bg_set((u8)(tile_x << 3), (u8)(tile_y << 3));
}
far_read16

Read a little-endian word through a bank-qualified pointer.

Syntax

c
#define far_read16(p) __farpeek16((p).bank, (p).ptr)

Parameters

p

far_ptr_t containing bank and ptr, where ptr is a CPU-visible address.

Return value

The word as u16.

Conditions and limits

The macro reads p.bank and p.ptr separately; do not pass a side-effecting expression. The intrinsic temporarily selects the ROM bank and restores it. Avoid concurrent bank changes from interrupts.

result[1]=far_read16(far);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Read hexadecimal 34 12 AB from another ROM bank: first byte 52, little-endian word 4660 and copied final byte 171.

flag_clear

Clear one game flag to 0 without clearing the neighboring flags. Use it when an event condition is undone or when explicitly initializing a flag. Clearing an already clear flag leaves it at zero.

Syntax

c
void flag_clear(u16 id);

Parameters

id

Flag number, 0–2047, passed as u16. The byte offset is id / 8 and the bit within it is id % 8, starting at the least significant bit. The wider parameter type does not enlarge the fixed 2048-flag store.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

The function does not validate the ID. Keep flag IDs below 2048 and quest IDs below 64; out-of-range access can read or overwrite unrelated RAM. The examples use explicit initialization rather than depending on startup contents.

flags.c owns 256 bytes for flags and 64 separate bytes for quests in RAM. These functions do not access cartridge save RAM and do not save across power cycles. To persist progress, your game must serialize the flag and quest values through its save system and restore them when loading.

Include rpg.h and compile lib/flags.c with the game. The arrays are private to that source file; use the flag/quest APIs to access them. Their storage is shared by all callers, so coordinate writes from the main loop and interrupt handlers yourself.

Usage example

c
flag_clear(9);flag_clear(9); // Mark it closed; clearing twice still leaves 0.
cleared=flag_get(9);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This sample clears door flag 9 after setting it. DOOR CLOSED displays 000 even though clear is called twice. The earlier DOOR OPEN value remains visible as 001 so you can compare the two stored observations.

The complete program displays decimal results on white: black text on DMG and blue text on CGB. FAILED must be 000. The captured screens show only RAM-state behavior; they do not demonstrate saving a game.

On the DMG emulator, verification exercised every flag ID from 0 through 2047, repeated set/clear calls, adjacent entries, and all 256 state values for each of 64 quests. A final 256-byte flag pattern and 64 quest bytes were compared with expected data. Both teaching screens were checked after 240 frames. Physical hardware and save persistence were not tested.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null

flag_get

Read one on/off game flag from the library's RAM bit array. Use it to ask whether a door is open, an item has been collected, or another game-defined event has happened. Reading a flag does not change it.

Syntax

c
u8 flag_get(u16 id);

Parameters

id

Flag number, 0–2047, passed as u16. The byte offset is id / 8 and the bit within it is id % 8, starting at the least significant bit. The wider parameter type does not enlarge the fixed 2048-flag store.

Return value

A normalized u8 Boolean: 0 when the flag is clear, 1 when set. This GB library calls the GB __bit_test intrinsic, which normalizes the result.

Conditions and limits

The function does not validate the ID. Keep flag IDs below 2048 and quest IDs below 64; out-of-range access can read or overwrite unrelated RAM. The examples use explicit initialization rather than depending on startup contents.

flags.c owns 256 bytes for flags and 64 separate bytes for quests in RAM. These functions do not access cartridge save RAM and do not save across power cycles. To persist progress, your game must serialize the flag and quest values through its save system and restore them when loading.

Draw 10×9 metatiles from the requested origin and remember that camera position for dirty redraws.

c

Declaration notes (original source)
Draw a 10-by-9 metatile viewport as 20-by-18 individual background tiles.
Out-of-range cells use definition zero; palette attributes are not written.
Remember the camera and clear the dirty flag after the full redraw.

kitaqgb/lib/map.c:212

c
void map_draw_visible(u8 camera_tx, u8 camera_ty)
{
    u8 my;

    if (map_meta_loaded == 0) return;

    map_camera_x = camera_tx;
    map_camera_y = camera_ty;

    my = 0;
    while (my < 9) {
        u8 mx = 0;
        while (mx < 10) {
            u8 tx = (u8)(camera_tx + mx);
            u8 ty = (u8)(camera_ty + my);
            u8 sx = (u8)(mx << 1);
            u8 sy = (u8)(my << 1);
            metatile_t meta;
            u8 id = map_get_metatile(tx, ty);
            map_read_metatile(id, &meta);
            __settile_xy(sx, sy, meta.tile_tl);
            __settile_xy((u8)(sx + 1), sy, meta.tile_tr);
            __settile_xy(sx, (u8)(sy + 1), meta.tile_bl);
            __settile_xy((u8)(sx + 1), (u8)(sy + 1), meta.tile_br);
            mx++;
        }
        my++;
    }
    map_dirty = 0;
}

Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:290

Declaration notes (original source)
Use metatile collision when that mode is active; otherwise read one packed
collision bit. Missing maps/out-of-range cells block movement, but a valid
ordinary map without a collision array is entirely passable.

kitaqgb/lib/map.c:68

c
u8 map_is_blocked(u8 x, u8 y)
{
    u16 index;
    u8 value;

    if (map_meta_loaded != 0) return map_is_solid(x, y);
    if (map_loaded == 0) return 1;
    if (x >= map_current.width || y >= map_current.height) return 1;
    if (map_current.collision_bits == 0) return 0;

    index = __map_index(x, y, map_current.width);
    // Collision uses least-significant bit first within each row-major group of eight cells.
    value = __farpeek8(map_bank, map_current.collision_bits + (index >> 3));
    if ((value & (u8)(1 << (index & 7))) != 0) return 1;
    return 0;
}
