map_load

Load an ordinary-map descriptor and draw up to 20×18 tiles from its upper-left corner into the selected background map.

Syntax

c
void map_load(u8 bank, const map_t* map);

Parameters

bank

ROM bank for the descriptor, collision bits and events.

map

Packed nine-byte map_t. tiles contains width*height tile IDs; collision_bits packs cells least-significant bit first; events stores one byte per cell. Tile reads use bank_tiles.

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

There is one shared active map. The descriptor is copied, but its arrays must remain readable for as long as needed. Load tile graphics into VRAM separately.

Coordinates address cells in the current map: 8×8 pixels for ordinary tiles, 16×16 pixels for metatiles.

Cells outside a small map are not cleared. For ordinary maps, bank_tiles=0 means bank zero; it does not inherit the descriptor bank.

Usage example

c
map_load(0,maps);result[2]=map_current_width();result[3]=map_current_height();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The left grid shows movement costs within three steps; the right shows a shortest route from S to G. Green asterisks trace nine steps around a red three-cell wall; blue digits show costs. DMG uses the same layout in black. RAM checks also demonstrate that the attack mask ignores walls.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\batch3_map_path.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\batch3_map_path.gb --no-cache --no-disasm --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k --ramsize=none
Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:286

Declaration notes (original source)
Load the nine-byte ordinary-map descriptor and draw up to 20 by 18 tiles
from its top-left corner. Drawing does not upload tile graphics or clear
background cells beyond smaller map dimensions.

kitaqgb/lib/map.c:35

c
void map_load(u8 bank, const map_t* map)
{
    u8 row;
    u8 h;
    u8 w;

    // The literal copy size depends on the packed map_t layout; changing that layout requires updating this copy.
    __farmemcpy(&map_current, bank, map, 9);
    map_bank = bank;
    map_loaded = 1;
    map_meta_loaded = 0;

    w = map_current.width;
    h = map_current.height;
    if (w > 20) w = 20;
    if (h > 18) h = 18;

    row = 0;
    while (row < h) {
        u8 x = 0;
        u16 base_index = __map_index(0, row, map_current.width);
        while (x < w) {
            map_row[x] = __farpeek8(map_current.bank_tiles, map_current.tiles + base_index + x);
            x++;
        }
        __settile_row(0, row, map_row, w);
        row++;
    }
}

Declaration notes (original source)
Report whether an event exists at the cell. Ordinary maps expose a Boolean
byte-presence test; metatile maps reduce their event ID to a Boolean here.

kitaqgb/lib/map.c:87

c
u8 map_trigger_at(u8 x, u8 y)
{
    u16 index;
    u8 value;

    if (map_meta_loaded != 0) return (u8)(map_get_event(x, y) != 0);
    if (map_loaded == 0) return 0;
    if (x >= map_current.width || y >= map_current.height) return 0;
    if (map_current.events == 0) return 0;

    index = __map_index(x, y, map_current.width);
    value = __farpeek8(map_bank, ((const u8*)map_current.events) + index);
    return (u8)((value != 0) ? 1 : 0);
}

Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:273

Declaration notes (original source)
Draw the current menu and cursor without waiting or sampling input. The
caller schedules suitable display timing and keeps item text within bounds.

kitaqgb/lib/menu.c:94

c
void menu_draw(menu_state_t* state)
{
    u8 i;
    if (state == 0) return;

    text_open(state->x, state->y, state->w, state->h);
    i = 0;
    while (i < state->count) {
        u8 py = (u8)(state->y + 1 + i);
        const u8* s = state->items[i];
        u8 px = (u8)(state->x + 2);
        __settile_xy((u8)(state->x + 1), py, (i == state->cursor) ? TEXT_TILE_CURSOR : TEXT_TILE_FILL);
        while (*s != 0) {
            __settile_xy(px, py, *s);
            px++;
            s++;
        }
        i++;
    }
}

Display inventory names and two-digit quantities and let the player choose an item.

Syntax

Parameters

Readable item_t array containing IDs, quantities and names.

count

Item count: 1–15 for a visible list, or zero for an empty list.

Declaration notes (original source)
Run a blocking item menu, drawing names and two-digit quantities. Return
the selected index or 0xFF on empty input/B; this does not consume an item.

kitaqgb/lib/menu.c:176

c
u8 menu_inventory(const item_t* items, u8 count)
{
    u8 cursor;
    u8 prev;
    u8 i;

    if (count == 0) return 0xFF;

    text_open(1, 1, 18, (u8)(count + 2));
    cursor = 0;
    prev = 0;

    while (1) {
        for (i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            u8 py = (u8)(2 + i);
            const u8* s = items[i].name;
            u8 px = 3;
            __settile_xy(2, py, (i == cursor) ? TEXT_TILE_CURSOR : TEXT_TILE_FILL);
            while (*s != 0) {
                __settile_xy(px, py, *s);
                px++;
                s++;
            }
            menu_draw_ascii_qty(15, py, items[i].qty);
        }

        __wait_vblank();
        {
            u16 kt = __readpadex(prev);
            u8 trigger;
            prev = (u8)kt;
            trigger = (u8)(kt >> 8);

            if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_UP) != 0) {
                if (cursor == 0) cursor = (u8)(count - 1);
                else cursor--;
            }
            if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_DOWN) != 0) {
                cursor++;
                if (cursor >= count) cursor = 0;
            }
            if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_A) != 0) return cursor;
            if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_B) != 0) return 0xFF;
        }
    }
}
menu_run

Run a selection menu that displays its items and waits for confirmation or cancellation.

Syntax

c
u8 menu_run(const menu_t* menu);

Parameters

menu

Non-null menu_t specifying position, size, items, count and starting cursor. An out-of-range starting cursor falls back to zero.

Return value

Returns the zero-based selection, or 255 for B/cancellation or an empty list.

Conditions and limits

New UP/DOWN presses wrap at the ends, with no held-key repeat. A wins over B when both are pressed. Keys already held on entry count as new presses. menu->cursor supplies the starting position and is not updated with the result. The window remains after return. Load frame, cursor and text tiles beforehand. The caller retains the item array and strings. Text is neither automatically wrapped nor clipped; choose positions, counts and label lengths that fit the window.

Usage example

c
result[0]=menu_run(&menu);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

DOWN then A selects SHIELD, index 1, from SWORD/SHIELD/POTION. The stored starting cursor remains zero.

kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:262

Declaration notes (original source)
Run a blocking menu loop with wraparound up/down selection, A to accept
and B to cancel. Return 0xFF for an empty menu or cancellation. Item strings
and menu dimensions must fit the visible tile area.

kitaqgb/lib/menu.c:25

c
u8 menu_run(const menu_t* menu)
{
    u8 cursor;
    u8 prev;

    if (menu->count == 0) return 0xFF;

    text_open(menu->x, menu->y, menu->w, menu->h);
    cursor = menu->cursor;
    if (cursor >= menu->count) cursor = 0;
    prev = 0;

    while (1) {
        u8 i;
        for (i = 0; i < menu->count; i++) {
            u8 py = (u8)(menu->y + 1 + i);
            __settile_xy((u8)(menu->x + 1), py, (i == cursor) ? TEXT_TILE_CURSOR : TEXT_TILE_FILL);
            {
                const u8* s = menu->items[i];
                u8 px = (u8)(menu->x + 2);
                while (*s != 0) {
                    __settile_xy(px, py, *s);
                    px++;
                    s++;
                }
            }
        }

        __wait_vblank();
        {
            u16 kt = __readpadex(prev);
            u8 trigger;
            prev = (u8)kt;
            trigger = (u8)(kt >> 8);

            if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_UP) != 0) {
                if (cursor == 0) cursor = (u8)(menu->count - 1);
                else cursor--;
            }
            if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_DOWN) != 0) {
                cursor++;
                if (cursor >= menu->count) cursor = 0;
            }
            if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_A) != 0) return cursor;
            if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_B) != 0) return 0xFF;
        }
    }
}

Read one controller transition and update the cursor, selection and cancellation state.

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

Null or an empty list is a no-op. It neither waits for a frame nor draws; call it about once per game-loop frame. UP/DOWN wraps without held-key repeat. B is processed after A, so simultaneous A/B cancels.

kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:277

Declaration notes (original source)
Sample new button presses and update cursor/selection state without drawing.
Selected and cancelled results remain latched; a B press in the same update
as A clears selection and leaves cancellation set.

kitaqgb/lib/menu.c:118

c
void menu_update(menu_state_t* state)
{
    u16 kt;
    u8 trigger;

    if (state == 0) return;
    if (state->count == 0) return;

    kt = __readpadex(state->prev_keys);
    state->prev_keys = (u8)kt;
    trigger = (u8)(kt >> 8);

    if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_UP) != 0) {
        if (state->cursor == 0) state->cursor = (u8)(state->count - 1);
        else state->cursor--;
    }
    if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_DOWN) != 0) {
        state->cursor++;
        if (state->cursor >= state->count) state->cursor = 0;
    }
    if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_A) != 0) {
        state->selected = state->cursor;
    }
    if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_B) != 0) {
        state->cancelled = 1;
        state->selected = 0xFF;
    }
}

path_find_bfs

Find a shortest cardinal route and write its directions in start-to-goal order.

Syntax

c
u8 path_find_bfs(u8 sx, u8 sy, u8 gx, u8 gy, u8* out_path, u8 max_len);

Parameters

sx

In-bounds start cell X.

sy

Start cell Y.

gx

Goal cell X; a blocked goal distinct from the origin is rejected.

gy

Goal cell Y.

out_path

Writable array of at least max_len bytes; 0=up, 1=right, 2=down, 3=left.

max_len

Output capacity; an excessive route fails rather than being truncated.

Return value

Returns route length; zero means unreachable, invalid coordinates, insufficient max_len, or an already reached goal.

Conditions and limits

Coordinates address cells in the current map: 8×8 pixels for ordinary tiles, 16×16 pixels for metatiles.

Search uses about 4 KiB of shared, non-reentrant workspace. Limit maps to 1024 cells and explored distances to 254. Distance 0xFF means unreached, so a 255-step route is not representable. Cost/mask outputs need width*height writable bytes.

max_len limits output, not the search radius. Do not use output as a new route after failure.

Usage example

c
result[49]=path_find_bfs(0,2,5,2,route,30);x=0;y=2;for(i=0;i<result[49];i++){if(route[i]==0)y--;if(route[i]==1)x++;if(route[i]==2)y++;if(route[i]==3)x--;}result[50]=x;result[51]=y;result[52]=path_find_bfs(0,2,5,2,route,2);result[53]=path_find_bfs(0,2,2,2,route,30);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The left grid shows movement costs within three steps; the right shows a shortest route from S to G. Green asterisks trace nine steps around a red three-cell wall; blue digits show costs. DMG uses the same layout in black. RAM checks also demonstrate that the attack mask ignores walls.

Complete example program

Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:361

Declaration notes (original source)
Find a shortest cardinal path with BFS and write direction codes 0=up,
1=right, 2=down, 3=left. Return its byte length, or zero for failure or an
already-reached goal. The caller supplies max_len output bytes and respects
the shared workspace/distance limits; excessive paths are not truncated.

kitaqgb/lib/slg_path.c:78

c
u8 path_find_bfs(u8 sx, u8 sy, u8 gx, u8 gy, u8* out_path, u8 max_len)
{
    u8 w = map_current_width();
    u8 h = map_current_height();
    u16 total;
    u16 head = 0;
    u16 tail = 0;
    u16 start;
    u16 goal;
    u8 found = 0;

    if (w == 0 || h == 0) return 0;
    if (sx >= w || sy >= h || gx >= w || gy >= h) return 0;
    if ((sx != gx || sy != gy) && map_is_blocked(gx, gy) != 0) return 0;

    total = (u16)((u16)w * (u16)h);
    __memset(path_dist, 0xFF, total);

    start = __map_index(sx, sy, w);
    goal = __map_index(gx, gy, w);

    path_dist[start] = 0;
    path_queue[tail++] = start;

    while (head < tail) {
        u16 cur = path_queue[head++];
        u8 cost = path_dist[cur];
        u8 y = (u8)(cur / w);
        u8 x = (u8)(cur - ((u16)y * (u16)w));

        if (cur == goal) {
            found = 1;
            break;
        }

        if (y > 0) {
            u16 next = (u16)(cur - w);
            if (path_dist[next] == 0xFF && map_is_blocked(x, (u8)(y - 1)) == 0) {
                path_dist[next] = (u8)(cost + 1);
                path_queue[tail++] = next;
            }
        }
        if ((u8)(x + 1) < w) {
            u16 next = (u16)(cur + 1);
            if (path_dist[next] == 0xFF && map_is_blocked((u8)(x + 1), y) == 0) {
                path_dist[next] = (u8)(cost + 1);
                path_queue[tail++] = next;
            }
        }
        if ((u8)(y + 1) < h) {
            u16 next = (u16)(cur + w);
            if (path_dist[next] == 0xFF && map_is_blocked(x, (u8)(y + 1)) == 0) {
                path_dist[next] = (u8)(cost + 1);
                path_queue[tail++] = next;
            }
        }
        if (x > 0) {
            u16 next = (u16)(cur - 1);
            if (path_dist[next] == 0xFF && map_is_blocked((u8)(x - 1), y) == 0) {
                path_dist[next] = (u8)(cost + 1);
                path_queue[tail++] = next;
            }
        }
    }

    // Reject unreachable or oversized paths before reconstructing output.
    if (found == 0) return 0;
    if (path_dist[goal] > max_len) return 0;

    {
        // Walk backward through decreasing costs, recording forward directions in
        // reverse order. The fixed neighbor order makes tied routes deterministic.
        u8 len = 0;
        u16 cur = goal;

        while (cur != start) {
            u8 cur_cost = path_dist[cur];
            u8 y = (u8)(cur / w);
            u8 x = (u8)(cur - ((u16)y * (u16)w));

            if (y > 0 && path_dist[(u16)(cur - w)] == (u8)(cur_cost - 1)) {
                path_rev[len++] = 2;
                cur = (u16)(cur - w);
                continue;
            }
            if ((u8)(x + 1) < w && path_dist[(u16)(cur + 1)] == (u8)(cur_cost - 1)) {
                path_rev[len++] = 3;
                cur = (u16)(cur + 1);
                continue;
            }
            if ((u8)(y + 1) < h && path_dist[(u16)(cur + w)] == (u8)(cur_cost - 1)) {
                path_rev[len++] = 0;
                cur = (u16)(cur + w);
                continue;
            }
            if (x > 0 && path_dist[(u16)(cur - 1)] == (u8)(cur_cost - 1)) {
                path_rev[len++] = 1;
                cur = (u16)(cur - 1);
                continue;
            }
            return 0;
        }

        // Reverse the recovered directions so the first output step starts at the origin.
        while (len != 0) {
            len--;
            out_path[path_dist[goal] - 1 - len] = path_rev[len];
        }

        return path_dist[goal];
    }
}
quest_set_state

Replace one quest's entire state byte. The meaning of each value belongs to your game: for example, you can use 1 for accepted and 3 for completed. The function does not check whether that transition is allowed and does not trigger rewards or callbacks.

Syntax

c
void quest_set_state(u8 quest_id, u8 state);

Parameters

quest_id

Quest number, 0–63, passed as u8. It directly indexes one of 64 state bytes; it is a game-defined ID, not a pointer or a count of completed quests.

state

New u8 state, 0–255. All eight bits replace the previous value. The library assigns no built-in meanings to the values and does not reserve 0 or 255.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

The function does not validate the ID. Keep flag IDs below 2048 and quest IDs below 64; out-of-range access can read or overwrite unrelated RAM. The examples use explicit initialization rather than depending on startup contents.

flags.c owns 256 bytes for flags and 64 separate bytes for quests in RAM. These functions do not access cartridge save RAM and do not save across power cycles. To persist progress, your game must serialize the flag and quest values through its save system and restore them when loading.

Include rpg.h and compile lib/flags.c with the game. The arrays are private to that source file; use the flag/quest APIs to access them. Their storage is shared by all callers, so coordinate writes from the main loop and interrupt handlers yourself.

Usage example

c
quest_set_state(2,1); // In this game, 1 means accepted.
started=quest_state(2);
quest_set_state(2,3); // In this game, 3 means completed; replace the whole byte.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This sample stores 1, then overwrites it with 3 for quest 2. ACCEPTED shows the first observation, 001, and COMPLETED shows the replacement, 003. LAST QUEST is 255 after storing 255 at quest ID 63, the last valid entry.

The complete program displays decimal results on white: black text on DMG and blue text on CGB. FAILED must be 000. The captured screens show only RAM-state behavior; they do not demonstrate saving a game.

On the DMG emulator, verification exercised every flag ID from 0 through 2047, repeated set/clear calls, adjacent entries, and all 256 state values for each of 64 quests. A final 256-byte flag pattern and 64 quest bytes were compared with expected data. Both teaching screens were checked after 240 frames. Physical hardware and save persistence were not tested.

rand_range

Choose a zero-based value below max by taking rng8() % max. For example, a bound of 10 gives a usable index from 0 through 9. A zero bound returns zero immediately without drawing.

Syntax

c
u8 rand_range(u8 max);

Parameters

max

Exclusive upper bound, as u8 (0–255). For max > 0 the result is smaller than max. This parameter cannot express 256; use rng8 when you want the full byte result without modulo reduction.

Return value

For max > 0, a u8 in 0 through max−1 after one draw. For max == 0, zero without a draw. Even max == 1 consumes one draw although its result is always zero.

Conditions and limits

Modulo reduction can favor some outcomes when the input range is not divisible by the bound. The underlying generator also need not be uniform. Treat bounded results and chance thresholds as gameplay approximations rather than exact probabilities.

These calls share persistent state. Reproduction requires the same target, seed and sequence of calls, including calls made by other helpers. Keep seed and draw operations in one execution context; these checks do not establish safe concurrent use from an interrupt handler.

GB and FC use different algorithms and do not promise the same sequence for the same seed. These are deterministic gameplay generators, not a source of cryptographic randomness; the tests check implementation behavior, not statistical quality or period.

Include rpg.h and compile lib/rng.c alongside your game when using the library functions. The __rng_seed and __rng8 intrinsics themselves are emitted by the compiler; a program using only those two needs no rng.c object.

Usage example

c
rng_seed(0x1234);
bounded=rand_range(10); // An index from 0 through 9; this seed yields 2.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This sample chooses an index below 10. RANGE 10 displays 00002 because the first byte from seed 0x1234 is 2. ZERO BOUND is 00000 and the following NEXT BYTE is still 00002, confirming that the zero-bound call did not draw.

The complete program prints decimal results on a white background: black text on DMG, blue text on CGB. FAILED must read 00000. The pictures show the actual emulator output of this sample.

Verification compared 32 outputs and eight subsequent byte draws per case with an independent host model: 93 GB cases and 18 FC cases, including constant/runtime seeds and GB range/chance/weight boundaries. The teaching screens were checked after 240 emulator frames. Physical hardware and statistical quality were not tested.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\rng_choices.c .\kitaqgb\lib\rng.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\rng_choices.gb --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --no-cache --no-disasm
Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:199

Declaration notes (original source)
Reduce a random byte modulo max; zero returns zero without consuming randomness.
Modulo reduction is biased unless max divides the generator range.

kitaqgb/lib/rng.c:37

c
u8 rand_range(u8 max)
{
    if (max == 0) return 0;
    return (u8)(rng8() % max);
}
range_fill_move

Flood cardinal neighbors at unit cost with breadth-first search to build movement costs.

Syntax

c

Parameters

sx

In-bounds start cell X.

sy

Start cell Y.

move

Movement limit 0..254; zero reaches only the origin.

out_costmap

Writable width*height cost array: 255 unreached, zero at the origin.

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

Coordinates address cells in the current map: 8×8 pixels for ordinary tiles, 16×16 pixels for metatiles.

Search uses about 4 KiB of shared, non-reentrant workspace. Limit maps to 1024 cells and explored distances to 254. Distance 0xFF means unreached, so a 255-step route is not representable. Cost/mask outputs need width*height writable bytes.

Missing maps or invalid origins leave output unchanged. Blocked destination cells are not entered.

Usage example

c
range_fill_move(0,2,3,costs);for(i=0;i<30;i++)result[13+i]=costs[i];

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The left grid shows movement costs within three steps; the right shows a shortest route from S to G. Green asterisks trace nine steps around a red three-cell wall; blue digits show costs. DMG uses the same layout in black. RAM checks also demonstrate that the attack mask ignores walls.

Declaration notes (original source)

limit and rejecting blocked destinations. Initialize output to 0xFF only
after validating the map and origin; invalid input leaves output unchanged.

kitaqgb/lib/slg_path.c:14

c
void range_fill_move(u8 sx, u8 sy, u8 move, u8* out_costmap)
{
    u8 w = map_current_width();
    u8 h = map_current_height();
    u16 total;
    u16 head = 0;
    u16 tail = 0;
    u16 start;

    if (w == 0 || h == 0) return;
    if (sx >= w || sy >= h) return;

    total = (u16)((u16)w * (u16)h);
    __memset(out_costmap, 0xFF, total);

    start = __map_index(sx, sy, w);
    out_costmap[start] = 0;
    path_queue[tail++] = start;

    while (head < tail) {
        u16 cur = path_queue[head++];
        u8 cost = out_costmap[cur];
        u8 y = (u8)(cur / w);
        u8 x = (u8)(cur - ((u16)y * (u16)w));

        if (cost >= move) continue;

        if (y > 0) {
            u16 next = (u16)(cur - w);
            if (out_costmap[next] == 0xFF && map_is_blocked(x, (u8)(y - 1)) == 0) {
                out_costmap[next] = (u8)(cost + 1);
                path_queue[tail++] = next;
            }
        }
        if ((u8)(x + 1) < w) {
            u16 next = (u16)(cur + 1);
            if (out_costmap[next] == 0xFF && map_is_blocked((u8)(x + 1), y) == 0) {
                out_costmap[next] = (u8)(cost + 1);
                path_queue[tail++] = next;
            }
        }
        if ((u8)(y + 1) < h) {
            u16 next = (u16)(cur + w);
            if (out_costmap[next] == 0xFF && map_is_blocked(x, (u8)(y + 1)) == 0) {
                out_costmap[next] = (u8)(cost + 1);
                path_queue[tail++] = next;
            }
        }
        if (x > 0) {
            u16 next = (u16)(cur - 1);
            if (out_costmap[next] == 0xFF && map_is_blocked((u8)(x - 1), y) == 0) {
                out_costmap[next] = (u8)(cost + 1);
                path_queue[tail++] = next;
            }
        }
    }
}
rle_decode

Expand a run-length encoded byte stream into ordinary writable RAM. Each count/value pair repeats one byte count times; a zero count ends the stream. Use this path when the encoded data is already readable through an ordinary pointer and you want to inspect or modify the expanded bytes before uploading them.

Syntax

c
u16 rle_decode(void* dst, const void* src);

Parameters

dst

Pointer to enough writable RAM for the entire expanded stream. No capacity is passed to the function. Keep the output separate from the encoded source so that writes cannot overwrite pairs that have not yet been read.

src

Readable pointer to count/value byte pairs terminated by a zero count. The count is 1–255 for an ordinary run; the repeated value can be any byte, including zero. A terminating zero has no following value byte. The pointer must remain readable in the current mapping throughout the call.

Return value

Number of bytes written, as u16. An immediate zero count produces zero bytes and returns 0. The terminator is not copied. Keep the expanded length representable in u16; the return value has no separate error code and is not a tile count.

Conditions and limits

The encoding is byte-oriented, not text-oriented. For example, {3, 0x12, 2, 0xA5, 0} expands to five bytes: 12 12 12 A5 A5. Values are hexadecimal in that output listing. A zero value inside a nonzero-count pair is ordinary data, not the end marker.

There is no encoded-size, output-capacity or malformed-data argument. Validate assets when creating or loading them, provide the zero terminator, and calculate their expanded size before decoding. An invalid or unterminated stream can read past the source and write past the destination.

The RAM decoders use ordinary stores and do not synchronize with LCD access periods. Keep their destinations in RAM. To display the result, upload it separately with a suitable VRAM copy API, as the sample does while the LCD is stopped.

Do not let an interrupt routine change the ROM mapping or reuse the far-copy helper while a bank-qualified fetch is in progress. The helpers use shared bank bookkeeping. Place a near decoder and its source in compatible mappings; switching to a function's bank must not hide an ordinary source pointer.

rle_decode and rle_decode_far are declared in rpg.h and implemented in lib/rle.c. Compile that implementation once with your game. The complete example includes rle.c after #pragma bank 0 so that its caller and decoders stay in the common bank; do not also pass rle.c as a separate input for this example. The __rle_decode_vram intrinsic itself needs no library implementation file.

Usage example

c
near_count=rle_decode(near_buffer+1,local_rle); // 48 bytes in writable RAM.
__vram_copy(0x8800,near_buffer+1,near_count); // Upload those bytes while the LCD is off.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This example expands nine encoded bytes into a guarded RAM buffer, then copies the 48-byte result to tile-data address 0x8800. RLE TO RAM reads 048. The top row is red on CGB and shows the three tiles decoded through this ordinary-pointer path.

Each row contains, from left to right, an 8×8 filled square, an 8×8 one-pixel outline, and a filled 4×8 rectangle occupying the left half of an 8×8 tile. Their tile columns are 2, 5 and 8 (pixel x = 16, 40 and 64). The three rows start at pixel y = 32, 72 and 112. DMG uses black shapes; CGB uses red, green and blue by row. FAILED must be 000. The numbers are byte counts: three 16-byte GB tiles require 48 decoded bytes.

The verification matrix checks 42 cases covering an empty stream, a one-byte run, zero-valued data, a 255-byte run, 510-byte output across a destination page, and encoded data across a source page. It compares all 528 observed destination/guard bytes, output length and restored ROM mapping. Direct VRAM cases include LCD on/off on DMG and CGB, plus CGB VBK 1. The two teaching screens are checked after 240 emulator frames. Invalid assets, concurrent interrupt use and physical hardware are not covered.

Complete example program

Build command

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\rle_shapes.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\rle_shapes.gb --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k --no-cache --no-disasm
Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:382

Declaration notes (original source)
Expand count/value byte pairs until a zero count terminates the stream.
The caller must provide a valid terminator and sufficient destination storage;
there are no source or destination bounds parameters. Return the 16-bit byte count.

kitaqgb/lib/rle.c:8

c
u16 rle_decode(void* dst, const void* src)
{
    const u8* in = (const u8*)src;
    u8* out = (u8*)dst;
    u16 total = 0;

    while (1) {
        u8 count = *in++;
        u8 value;
        if (count == 0) break;
        value = *in++;
        while (count != 0) {
            *out++ = value;
            total++;
            count--;
        }
    }

    return total;
}
rle_decode_far

Expand the same count/value format into RAM while reading each encoded byte through __farpeek8 with the supplied ROM bank. Use it for compressed assets stored in a switchable ROM bank. The destination remains an ordinary RAM pointer; the bank argument describes the source.

Syntax

c
u16 rle_decode_far(void* dst, u8 bank, const void* src);

Parameters

dst

Pointer to enough writable RAM for the entire expanded stream. No capacity is passed to the function. Keep the output separate from the encoded source so that writes cannot overwrite pairs that have not yet been read.

bank

Source ROM bank number as u8. The bank and CPU address must match your cartridge mapper and asset placement. Bank selection is restored after each encoded-byte fetch; it is not a destination VRAM-bank selector and cannot express a 9-bit MBC5 bank number.

src

CPU pointer to the encoded stream in the supplied bank. The function increments this address, but keeps the bank number fixed. Keep the full stream, including its terminating zero, inside a readable mapping; crossing 0x7FFF does not automatically continue in the next ROM bank.

Return value

Number of bytes written, as u16. An immediate zero count produces zero bytes and returns 0. The terminator is not copied. Keep the expanded length representable in u16; the return value has no separate error code and is not a tile count.

Conditions and limits

The encoding is byte-oriented, not text-oriented. For example, {3, 0x12, 2, 0xA5, 0} expands to five bytes: 12 12 12 A5 A5. Values are hexadecimal in that output listing. A zero value inside a nonzero-count pair is ordinary data, not the end marker.

There is no encoded-size, output-capacity or malformed-data argument. Validate assets when creating or loading them, provide the zero terminator, and calculate their expanded size before decoding. An invalid or unterminated stream can read past the source and write past the destination.

The RAM decoders use ordinary stores and do not synchronize with LCD access periods. Keep their destinations in RAM. To display the result, upload it separately with a suitable VRAM copy API, as the sample does while the LCD is stopped.

Do not let an interrupt routine change the ROM mapping or reuse the far-copy helper while a bank-qualified fetch is in progress. The helpers use shared bank bookkeeping. Place a near decoder and its source in compatible mappings; switching to a function's bank must not hide an ordinary source pointer.

rle_decode and rle_decode_far are declared in rpg.h and implemented in lib/rle.c. Compile that implementation once with your game. The complete example includes rle.c after #pragma bank 0 so that its caller and decoders stay in the common bank; do not also pass rle.c as a separate input for this example. The __rle_decode_vram intrinsic itself needs no library implementation file.

Usage example

c
far_count=rle_decode_far(far_buffer+1,2,banked_rle); // Read encoded pairs from ROM bank 2.
if(*rle_bank_marker!=0xA1)failures++; // ROM bank 1 must be visible again.
__vram_copy(0x8830,far_buffer+1,far_count);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This example reads the encoded stream from ROM bank 2, expands 48 bytes into RAM, and uploads them at 0x8830. BANKED RAM reads 048. The middle row is green on CGB. A marker in ROM bank 1 is also checked to verify restoration of the caller's mapping.

Each row contains, from left to right, an 8×8 filled square, an 8×8 one-pixel outline, and a filled 4×8 rectangle occupying the left half of an 8×8 tile. Their tile columns are 2, 5 and 8 (pixel x = 16, 40 and 64). The three rows start at pixel y = 32, 72 and 112. DMG uses black shapes; CGB uses red, green and blue by row. FAILED must be 000. The numbers are byte counts: three 16-byte GB tiles require 48 decoded bytes.

The verification matrix checks 42 cases covering an empty stream, a one-byte run, zero-valued data, a 255-byte run, 510-byte output across a destination page, and encoded data across a source page. It compares all 528 observed destination/guard bytes, output length and restored ROM mapping. Direct VRAM cases include LCD on/off on DMG and CGB, plus CGB VBK 1. The two teaching screens are checked after 240 emulator frames. Invalid assets, concurrent interrupt use and physical hardware are not covered.

kitaqgb/lib/rle.c:34

c
u16 rle_decode_far(void* dst, u8 bank, const void* src)
{
    const u8* p = (const u8*)src;
    u8* out = (u8*)dst;
    u16 total = 0;

    while (1) {
        u8 count = __farpeek8(bank, p);
        u8 value;
        p++;
        if (count == 0) break;

        p++;
        while (count != 0) {

            total++;
            count--;
        }
    }

    return total;
}
rng16

Build an unsigned 16-bit value from two successive rng8 draws. The first byte becomes bits 15–8 and the second becomes bits 7–0. Use this when one byte cannot represent the value range you need.

Syntax

c
u16 rng16();

Return value

One u16 result (0–65535), formed as (first_byte << 8) | second_byte. Exactly two byte draws are consumed; this does not establish a uniform distribution of all 65536 values.

Conditions and limits

These calls share persistent state. Reproduction requires the same target, seed and sequence of calls, including calls made by other helpers. Keep seed and draw operations in one execution context; these checks do not establish safe concurrent use from an interrupt handler.

GB and FC use different algorithms and do not promise the same sequence for the same seed. These are deterministic gameplay generators, not a source of cryptographic randomness; the tests check implementation behavior, not statistical quality or period.

Include rpg.h and compile lib/rng.c alongside your game when using the library functions. The __rng_seed and __rng8 intrinsics themselves are emitted by the compiler; a program using only those two needs no rng.c object.

Usage example

c
rng_seed(0x1234);
word=rng16(); // First draw 2 is high, second draw 34 is low: 0x0222 = 546.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This sample demonstrates word assembly. After reseeding with 0x1234, bytes 2 and 34 form 0x0222, so RNG16 displays 00546. FIRST and SECOND show the corresponding byte values separately.

The complete program prints decimal results on a white background: black text on DMG, blue text on CGB. FAILED must read 00000. The pictures show the actual emulator output of this sample.

Verification compared 32 outputs and eight subsequent byte draws per case with an independent host model: 93 GB cases and 18 FC cases, including constant/runtime seeds and GB range/chance/weight boundaries. The teaching screens were checked after 240 emulator frames. Physical hardware and statistical quality were not tested.

rng_chance

Make a yes/no choice using rng_range(100) < percent. This is useful for approximate gameplay chances, such as deciding whether an enemy drops an item. Zero always returns false; values of 100 or more always return true, and neither endpoint consumes a draw.

Syntax

c
u8 rng_chance(u8 percent);

Parameters

percent

Requested chance as u8. Values 1–99 use one modulo-reduced byte; 0 returns false, and 100–255 return true. The intermediate values are approximate thresholds, not a guarantee of exact percentages.

Return value

Normalized Boolean: 0 for false or 1 for true. A call with a threshold from 1 through 99 consumes one byte draw.

Conditions and limits

Modulo reduction can favor some outcomes when the input range is not divisible by the bound. The underlying generator also need not be uniform. Treat bounded results and chance thresholds as gameplay approximations rather than exact probabilities.

These calls share persistent state. Reproduction requires the same target, seed and sequence of calls, including calls made by other helpers. Keep seed and draw operations in one execution context; these checks do not establish safe concurrent use from an interrupt handler.

GB and FC use different algorithms and do not promise the same sequence for the same seed. These are deterministic gameplay generators, not a source of cryptographic randomness; the tests check implementation behavior, not statistical quality or period.

Include rpg.h and compile lib/rng.c alongside your game when using the library functions. The __rng_seed and __rng8 intrinsics themselves are emitted by the compiler; a program using only those two needs no rng.c object.

Usage example

c
rng_seed(0x1234);
chance=rng_chance(50); // Here 2 % 100 < 50, so the result is 1 (true).

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This sample performs one approximate 50-percent decision. The seeded byte is 2, and 2 % 100 < 50 is true, so CHANCE 50 displays 00001. One successful draw does not demonstrate a 50-percent long-run success rate.

The complete program prints decimal results on a white background: black text on DMG, blue text on CGB. FAILED must read 00000. The pictures show the actual emulator output of this sample.

The teaching screens were checked after 240 emulator frames. Physical hardware and statistical quality were not tested.

u8 rng_chance(u8 percent)
{

}

rng_range

Call rand_range with the same exclusive upper bound. This spelling groups bounded selection with the other rng_ functions; it uses the same byte draw and modulo operation, including the no-draw result for a zero bound.

Syntax

c
u8 rng_range(u8 max);

Parameters

max

Exclusive upper bound, as u8 (0–255). For max > 0 the result is smaller than max. This parameter cannot express 256; use rng8 when you want the full byte result without modulo reduction.

Return value

For max > 0, a u8 in 0 through max−1 after one draw. For max == 0, zero without a draw. Even max == 1 consumes one draw although its result is always zero.

Conditions and limits

Modulo reduction can favor some outcomes when the input range is not divisible by the bound. The underlying generator also need not be uniform. Treat bounded results and chance thresholds as gameplay approximations rather than exact probabilities.

These calls share persistent state. Reproduction requires the same target, seed and sequence of calls, including calls made by other helpers. Keep seed and draw operations in one execution context; these checks do not establish safe concurrent use from an interrupt handler.

GB and FC use different algorithms and do not promise the same sequence for the same seed. These are deterministic gameplay generators, not a source of cryptographic randomness; the tests check implementation behavior, not statistical quality or period.

Include rpg.h and compile lib/rng.c alongside your game when using the library functions. The __rng_seed and __rng8 intrinsics themselves are emitted by the compiler; a program using only those two needs no rng.c object.

Usage example

c
rng_seed(0x1234);
alias=rng_range(10); // The same exclusive upper bound and result, 2.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This sample compares two spellings of bounded selection. Reseeding before each call makes ALIAS 10 and RANGE 10 both display 00002. The upper bound 10 itself is excluded.

The complete program prints decimal results on a white background: black text on DMG, blue text on CGB. FAILED must read 00000. The pictures show the actual emulator output of this sample.

Verification compared 32 outputs and eight subsequent byte draws per case with an independent host model: 93 GB cases and 18 FC cases, including constant/runtime seeds and GB range/chance/weight boundaries. The teaching screens were checked after 240 emulator frames. Physical hardware and statistical quality were not tested.

rng_seed

Set the seed through the GB library interface. This is a wrapper around __rng_seed, so it resets the same shared state used by rng8, rng16 and the selection helpers; it does not create a separate generator.

Syntax

c
void rng_seed(u16 seed);

Parameters

seed

Unsigned 16-bit seed, 0–65535. Both bytes are stored as supplied. Choose and record the seed before the sequence of gameplay draws you want to reproduce.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

A zero state is accepted. On the next byte draw, the GB generator substitutes 0x5AA5 before advancing; __rng_seed(0) followed by __rng8() therefore returns 122. Repeatedly reseeding restarts the sequence instead of adding randomness.

These calls share persistent state. Reproduction requires the same target, seed and sequence of calls, including calls made by other helpers. Keep seed and draw operations in one execution context; these checks do not establish safe concurrent use from an interrupt handler.

Validate a slot's header, payload bounds and checksum without copying the

kitaqgb/lib/save.c:182

c
u8 save_exists(u8 slot)
{
    u16 base;
    u16 stored_len;
    u8 stored_sum;

    if (slot >= SAVE_SLOT_COUNT) return 0;

    base = save_slot_base(slot);
    save_enable();

    if (save_read_abs(base + 0) != SAVE_MAGIC0) {
        save_disable();
        return 0;
    }
    if (save_read_abs(base + 1) != SAVE_MAGIC1) {
        save_disable();
        return 0;
    }
    if (save_read_abs(base + 2) != SAVE_VERSION) {
        save_disable();
        return 0;
    }

    stored_len = (u16)save_read_abs(base + 3);
    stored_len |= (u16)((u16)save_read_abs(base + 4) << 8);
    stored_sum = save_read_abs(base + 5);

    if (stored_len > (u16)(SAVE_SLOT_SIZE - SAVE_HEADER_SIZE)) {
        save_disable();
        return 0;
    }
    if (save_checksum_ram((u16)(base + SAVE_HEADER_SIZE), stored_len) != stored_sum) {
        save_disable();
        return 0;
    }

    save_disable();
    return 1;
}

c
u8 save_read(u8 slot, void* data, u16 len)
{
    u8* dst = (u8*)data;
    u16 base;
    u16 stored_len;
    u8 stored_sum;
    u16 i;

    if (slot >= SAVE_SLOT_COUNT) return 0;

    base = save_slot_base(slot);
    save_enable();

    if (save_read_abs(base + 0) != SAVE_MAGIC0) {
        save_disable();
        return 0;
    }
    if (save_read_abs(base + 1) != SAVE_MAGIC1) {
        save_disable();
        return 0;
    }
    if (save_read_abs(base + 2) != SAVE_VERSION) {
        save_disable();
        return 0;
    }

    stored_len = (u16)save_read_abs(base + 3);
    stored_len |= (u16)((u16)save_read_abs(base + 4) << 8);
    stored_sum = save_read_abs(base + 5);

    if (stored_len != len || stored_len > (u16)(SAVE_SLOT_SIZE - SAVE_HEADER_SIZE)) {
        save_disable();
        return 0;
    }
    if (save_checksum_ram((u16)(base + SAVE_HEADER_SIZE), stored_len) != stored_sum) {
        save_disable();
        return 0;
    }

    i = 0;
    while (i < stored_len) {
        dst[i] = save_read_abs((u16)(base + SAVE_HEADER_SIZE + i));
        i++;
    }

    save_disable();
    return 1;
}

kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:326

Declaration notes (original source)
Validate slot and payload length, write payload bytes, then write the header
and checksum. Return one after completing the writes; interruption can leave
a partially replaced slot, so this is not transactional save storage.

kitaqgb/lib/save.c:81

c
u8 save_write(u8 slot, const void* data, u16 len)
{
    const u8* src = (const u8*)data;
    u16 base;
    u16 i;
    u8 sum = 0;

    if (slot >= SAVE_SLOT_COUNT) return 0;
    if (len > (u16)(SAVE_SLOT_SIZE - SAVE_HEADER_SIZE)) return 0;

    base = save_slot_base(slot);
    save_enable();

    i = 0;
    while (i < len) {
        u8 v = src[i];
        save_write_abs((u16)(base + SAVE_HEADER_SIZE + i), v);
        sum = (u8)(sum + v);
        i++;
    }

    save_write_abs(base + 0, SAVE_MAGIC0);
    save_write_abs(base + 1, SAVE_MAGIC1);
    save_write_abs(base + 2, SAVE_VERSION);
    save_write_abs(base + 3, (u8)(len & 0xFF));
    save_write_abs(base + 4, (u8)(len >> 8));
    save_write_abs(base + 5, sum);

    save_disable();
    return 1;
}

script_step

Advance commands until output, choice, waiting or completion yields control.

Syntax

c
u8 script_step();

Return value

0=TEXT/CHOICE yield; 1=waiting; 2=finished or inactive. Unknown opcodes also terminate with 2.

Conditions and limits

Opcodes: 00 END; 01 TEXT(bank,ptr16); 02 SET_FLAG(id16); 03 CLEAR_FLAG(id16); 04 JUMP(bank,ptr16); 05 IF_FLAG(id16,bank,ptr16); 06 CHOICE(count,table16); 07 WAIT(n); 08 CALL_EVENT(bank,ptr16). Words are little-endian. Keep strings, pointer tables and instructions readable and within their mapped banks.

WAIT n returns 1 on decoding, then waits for n more calls. CALL_EVENT has only one saved return slot. CHOICE needs a nonzero count and blocks internally until selection. A non-yielding jump loop blocks the game loop, so ensure execution reaches a terminator or yielding command.

Expected result

Jump from bank 1 to bank 2, set flag 19 and wait. Initial two waiting calls return 1; destination flag becomes 1; completion after WAIT returns 2. The flag proves control reached the other bank.

execution ends (2). Control/flag commands continue within the same call, so

kitaqgb/lib/script.c:125

c
u8 script_step()
{
    if (script_active == 0) return 2;
    if (script_wait != 0) {
        script_wait--;
        return 1;
    }

    while (script_active != 0) {
        u8 op = script_read8();

        // An END returns to the one saved caller when present; otherwise it ends the script.
        if (op == SCRIPT_OP_END) {
            if (script_return_active != 0) {
                script_bank = script_return_bank;
                script_pc = script_return_pc;
                script_return_active = 0;
                continue;
            }
            script_active = 0;
            return 2;
        }

        if (op == SCRIPT_OP_TEXT) {
            u8 bank = script_read8();
            u16 ptr = script_read16();
            text_print_far(bank, (const u8*)ptr);
            return 0;
        }

        if (op == SCRIPT_OP_SET_FLAG) {
            u16 id = script_read16();
            flag_set(id);
            continue;
        }

        if (op == SCRIPT_OP_CLEAR_FLAG) {
            u16 id = script_read16();
            flag_clear(id);
            continue;
        }

        if (op == SCRIPT_OP_JUMP) {
            // Read all operands in the source bank before installing the destination.
            u8 bank = script_read8();
            u16 ptr = script_read16();
            script_bank = bank;
            script_pc = (const u8*)ptr;
            continue;
        }

        // Read all branch operands before switching bank/address so an untaken branch
        // still consumes the full instruction.
        if (op == SCRIPT_OP_IF_FLAG) {
            u16 id = script_read16();
            u8 bank = script_read8();
            u16 ptr = script_read16();
            if (flag_get(id) != 0) {
                script_bank = bank;
                script_pc = (const u8*)ptr;
            }
            continue;
        }

        if (op == SCRIPT_OP_CHOICE) {
            u8 count = script_read8();
            u16 table = script_read16();
            script_last_choice = script_choice(script_bank, (const u8*)table, count);
            return 0;
        }

        if (op == SCRIPT_OP_WAIT) {
            script_wait = script_read8();
            return 1;
        }

        // Save the continuation only when the single return slot is empty. Nested
        // calls replace the current script but do not push another return address.
        if (op == SCRIPT_OP_CALL_EVENT) {
            u8 bank = script_read8();
            u16 ptr = script_read16();
            if (script_return_active == 0) {
                script_return_active = 1;
                script_return_bank = script_bank;
                script_return_pc = script_pc;
            }
            script_bank = bank;
            script_pc = (const u8*)ptr;
            continue;
        }

        // Unknown opcodes terminate with the same return code as END; there is no distinct malformed-stream error.
        script_active = 0;
        return 2;
    }

    return 2;
}

text_choice

Draw a vertical list inside the active text area and wait for a selection. UP and DOWN move a cursor with wraparound; A accepts and B cancels. The loop redraws choices and polls once after a VBlank wait. It returns a zero-based index or 255 for cancellation or an empty list.

Syntax

c
u8 text_choice(const u8* const* choices, u8 count);

Parameters

choices

Pointer to an array of count readable string pointers. Each string ends in zero and contains raw tile IDs; choice labels do not interpret dialogue control codes. Keep the pointer table and strings mapped until selection finishes.

count

Number of choices. Zero returns 255 immediately without reading the pointer table. For a nonempty list, provide at least count interior rows and enough width for one cursor cell plus the longest label. There is no clipping or scrolling.

Return value

Index from 0 to count−1 when A accepts. The value 255 means B cancelled or count was zero; distinguish these situations in the calling code if needed. The function does not close the text area or clear the list.

Conditions and limits

Use a valid BG-map rectangle and load font/frame tiles first. The software text area uses the BG map selected by LCDC bit 3; it does not enable the hardware Window layer. Use VBK 0 on CGB for tile numbers and set color attributes separately. The examples provide the ASCII-mapped font and frame, cursor and page-indicator tiles. Dialogue and choice labels use byte-sized tile IDs, not UTF-8 decoding. To display characters outside the supplied font, provide the glyph tiles and encode the text for those IDs; keep dialogue control-byte values reserved.

Open and size the area before calling. The choice routine uses its stored position without checking whether the area is open. Labels start two columns inside the left edge and one row below the top; the cursor occupies the cell immediately to their left. Printing the choices does not use the dialogue character-speed setting.

The input loop reacts to new presses, with UP processed before DOWN and A before B. Holding a direction does not repeat the movement; release and press again. Since the previous button mask starts at zero, a held button can act immediately on entry. A simultaneous move and A returns the moved-to index, although the last drawn cursor may still show the preceding position.

These are blocking helpers: they do not call your game update, music service or rendering loop while waiting. With the LCD off, __wait_vblank returns immediately, so character speed and WAIT do not create frame delays. Keep the LCD enabled for timed dialogue and frame-paced input polling. Use a game-side state machine when other work must advance during a conversation.

The underlying safe tile writes wait for writable LCD modes when the LCD is on and use DI/EI around writes. They can enable interrupts rather than preserving an initially disabled interrupt state. Do not call these blocking helpers from an interrupt handler or depend on them to preserve that state.

Each complete example includes text.c once. Build the example with the library and manual-sample include directories; do not also add lib/text.c as another source input. The far-stream example uses MBC5 with a 64 KiB ROM so its bank-2 data is present.

Usage example

c
selected=text_choice(dialogue_choices,3);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Press DOWN once and then A. In the captured run, the right-pointing cursor is beside SHIELD at tile (2,4), and SELECTED shows 1. The three labels start at (3,3), (3,4) and (3,5). The frame, cursor and labels are green on CGB and black on DMG; the result and instructions remain black.

The emulator checks compare complete BG-map contents and the four sample images. Additional runs cover open/close state, ordinary and banked control streams, timed waits, explicit and automatic page waits, A/B/START advance, held buttons, wraparound choices, empty lists and simultaneous-input priority. Checkpoints before and after scripted input verify that page waits actually block. Physical hardware and interrupt concurrency are not tested.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\dialogue_choice.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\dialogue_choice.gb --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k --no-cache --no-disasm
Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:231

Declaration notes (original source)
Redraw choices and block for edge-triggered navigation: UP/DOWN wrap, A
accepts, and B returns 0xFF. Zero choices also returns 0xFF. Choice strings
use raw tile bytes, and the caller must fit them inside the available rows.

kitaqgb/lib/text.c:316

c
u8 text_choice(const u8* const* choices, u8 count)
{
    u8 cursor;
    u8 prev;

    if (count == 0) return 0xFF;

    cursor = 0;
    prev = 0;
    while (1) {
        u8 i;
        for (i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            u8 py = (u8)(text_y + 1 + i);
            __settile_xy((u8)(text_x + 1), py, (i == cursor) ? TEXT_TILE_CURSOR : TEXT_TILE_FILL);
            text_draw_string_at((u8)(text_x + 2), py, choices[i]);
        }

        __wait_vblank();
        {
            u16 kt = __readpadex(prev);
            u8 trigger;
            prev = (u8)kt;
            trigger = (u8)(kt >> 8);

            if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_UP) != 0) {
                if (cursor == 0) cursor = (u8)(count - 1);
                else cursor--;
            }
            if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_DOWN) != 0) {
                cursor++;
                if (cursor >= count) cursor = 0;
            }
            if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_A) != 0) return cursor;
            if ((trigger & PAD_KEY_B) != 0) return 0xFF;
        }
    }
}
text_clear_rect

Fill a rectangular area of the background tile map with TEXT_TILE_FILL. Use it to erase a label, clear a numeric field or blank part of a panel. It does not move the active text cursor, close the text area or change its dimensions.

Syntax

c
void text_clear_rect(u8 x, u8 y, u8 w, u8 h);

Parameters

x

Starting column in 8×8 background-map cells. Keep the complete output within columns 0–31. With no background scrolling, the visible columns are 0–19.

y

Starting row in 8×8 background-map cells, 0–31. With no background scrolling, rows 0–17 are visible. A rectangle must also fit vertically.

w

Width in tile cells. For text_window this includes both border columns, leaving max(w−2, 0) interior columns. For text_clear_rect it is the number of cells to fill on each row.

h

Height in tile cells. For text_window this includes the top and bottom borders, leaving max(h−2, 0) interior rows. For text_clear_rect it is the number of rows to fill.

Return value

No return value. The function writes tile-map cells before returning; it does not return a character count or a status code.

Conditions and limits

These functions paint the BG map selected by LCDC bit 3. The text window is a software text area on that map, not the hardware Window layer. Keep CGB VBK at 0 for tile numbers; these calls do not set color attributes, palettes or scrolling.

Load the font and frame graphics before drawing. Default frame IDs are 1–6, the fill tile is 0, and decimal digits start at ASCII 0 (tile 48). The minus sign uses ASCII - (tile 45). The sample supplies six frame tiles and the manual font whose glyph IDs match ASCII.

Keep rectangles and text inside the 32×32 map. Rectangle fills do not clip their width or height to the map boundary. A zero width or height fills nothing; text_window still records that area as open, with no usable interior.

The public numeric functions choose a field exactly as wide as the new value. They do not erase leftover cells to its right. Writing 7 over 12345 at the same position displays 72345. To obtain just 7, clear the reserved five-cell field with text_clear_rect before printing. Reserve six cells for a signed 16-bit field.

The tile-write intrinsics check LCD state: with LCD off they write immediately; with LCD on they wait for writable LCD modes and use DI/EI around writes. That path can enable interrupts on return, so do not assume it preserves a disabled interrupt state. The samples and byte-level tests here perform their writes with LCD off.

The complete sample includes text.c once so its library implementation is compiled with the program. Do not also pass lib/text.c as a separate input for this sample. To customize TEXT_* tile constants, define them before including rpg.h and the implementation; apply the same definitions wherever the library is compiled.

Usage example

c
text_clear_rect(7,5,5,1);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The frame initially contains KEEP ERASE KEEP on row 5. Clearing five cells at (7,5) removes ERASE while both KEEP labels and the frame remain. The CLEAN row also clears a five-cell number field before writing 7.

Verification compares every visible pixel and all 1024 BG-map bytes in both sample screens. Separate DMG/CGB ROMs check all 256 unsigned byte values, decimal digit boundaries and signed extremes, preserving dots beside each numeric output as guards. Layout checks include empty and narrow rectangles, map-edge placement, raw control-valued tile bytes and the window cursor after absolute writes. These are emulator tests, not physical-hardware tests.

text_print

Read a control stream through an ordinary pointer and write its character tiles at the active window cursor. The function interprets newlines, timed waits and page waits, wrapping at the interior width. It returns only after reaching END, so page waits can block until a button is pressed.

Syntax

c
void text_print(const u8* str);

Parameters

str

Readable pointer to a stream terminated by TEXT_CTRL_END (0). Keep the whole stream mapped, including any operand after WAIT, throughout blocking waits. No buffer length or validity check is provided.

Return value

No return value. Any drawing or blocking waits occur before the function returns.

Conditions and limits

Use a valid BG-map rectangle and load font/frame tiles first. The software text area uses the BG map selected by LCDC bit 3; it does not enable the hardware Window layer. Use VBK 0 on CGB for tile numbers and set color attributes separately. The examples provide the ASCII-mapped font and frame, cursor and page-indicator tiles. Dialogue and choice labels use byte-sized tile IDs, not UTF-8 decoding. To display characters outside the supplied font, provide the glyph tiles and encode the text for those IDs; keep dialogue control-byte values reserved.

Control bytes: 0x00 ends the stream; 0x0A moves to a new interior row; 0x01 consumes the next byte as a VBlank-wait count, including zero; 0x02 waits for page advance, clears the interior and resets the cursor. Other bytes are tile IDs. A WAIT operand of zero is not an END marker.

Moving below the last interior row, either through a newline or automatic wrapping, shows the page-wait marker, waits for A, B or START, clears the interior and resumes at its first cell. This replaces the page rather than scrolling its rows. An explicit 0x02 waits without adding the marker. The page poll starts with no remembered buttons, so a button already held when the wait begins can advance it.

Ordinary characters are ignored while the area is closed or has no usable interior. Control bytes are still interpreted: WAIT can still block, and page controls can wait or clear the stored area. Therefore text_print on a closed area is not a general no-op.

These are blocking helpers: they do not call your game update, music service or rendering loop while waiting. With the LCD off, __wait_vblank returns immediately, so character speed and WAIT do not create frame delays. Keep the LCD enabled for timed dialogue and frame-paced input polling. Use a game-side state machine when other work must advance during a conversation.

The underlying safe tile writes wait for writable LCD modes when the LCD is on and use DI/EI around writes. They can enable interrupts rather than preserving an initially disabled interrupt state. Do not call these blocking helpers from an interrupt handler or depend on them to preserve that state.

Each complete example includes text.c once. Build the example with the library and manual-sample include directories; do not also add lib/text.c as another source input. The far-stream example uses MBC5 with a 64 KiB ROM so its bank-2 data is present.

kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:224

Declaration notes (original source)
Decode an END-terminated stream of tile bytes and newline/wait/page controls.
WAIT consumes a following frame-count byte. The source must remain readable
through blocking waits; the routine does not validate stream length.

kitaqgb/lib/text.c:261

c
void text_print(const u8* str)
{
    while (*str != TEXT_CTRL_END) {
        u8 c = *str++;
        if (c == TEXT_CTRL_NEWLINE) {
            text_newline();
            continue;
        }
        if (c == TEXT_CTRL_WAIT) {
            u8 frames = *str++;
            text_delay_frames(frames);
            continue;
        }
        if (c == TEXT_CTRL_PAGE_WAIT) {
            text_wait_advance();
            text_clear_inside();
            text_reset_cursor();
            continue;
        }
        text_put_tile(c);
    }
}

kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:227

Declaration notes (original source)
Decode the same text controls while fetching each byte from the specified
ROM bank. The pointer advances within that bank; it does not roll into the next bank.

kitaqgb/lib/text.c:286

c
void text_print_far(u8 bank, const u8* str)
{
    const u8* p = str;
    while (1) {
        u8 c = __farpeek8(bank, p);
        p++;
        if (c == TEXT_CTRL_END) return;
        if (c == TEXT_CTRL_NEWLINE) {
            text_newline();
            continue;
        }
        if (c == TEXT_CTRL_WAIT) {
            u8 frames = __farpeek8(bank, p);
            p++;
            text_delay_frames(frames);
            continue;
        }
        if (c == TEXT_CTRL_PAGE_WAIT) {
            text_wait_advance();
            text_clear_inside();
            text_reset_cursor();
            continue;
        }
        text_put_tile(c);
    }
}
text_print_s16

Draw a signed 16-bit decimal value. A negative value begins with the minus tile and then its magnitude; zero and positive values have no sign. The longest output is -32768, which occupies six cells.

Syntax

c
void text_print_s16(u8 x, u8 y, s16 value);

Parameters

x

Starting column in 8×8 background-map cells. Keep the complete output within columns 0–31. With no background scrolling, the visible columns are 0–19.

y

Starting row in 8×8 background-map cells, 0–31. With no background scrolling, rows 0–17 are visible. A rectangle must also fit vertically.

value

Signed value from −32768 to 32767. The sample casts the 16-bit pattern 32768 (0x8000) to s16 to display −32768.

Return value

No return value. The function writes tile-map cells before returning; it does not return a character count or a status code.

Conditions and limits

These functions paint the BG map selected by LCDC bit 3. The text window is a software text area on that map, not the hardware Window layer. Keep CGB VBK at 0 for tile numbers; these calls do not set color attributes, palettes or scrolling.

Load the font and frame graphics before drawing. Default frame IDs are 1–6, the fill tile is 0, and decimal digits start at ASCII 0 (tile 48). The minus sign uses ASCII - (tile 45). The sample supplies six frame tiles and the manual font whose glyph IDs match ASCII.

Keep rectangles and text inside the 32×32 map. Rectangle fills do not clip their width or height to the map boundary. A zero width or height fills nothing; text_window still records that area as open, with no usable interior.

The public numeric functions choose a field exactly as wide as the new value. They do not erase leftover cells to its right. Writing 7 over 12345 at the same position displays 72345. To obtain just 7, clear the reserved five-cell field with text_clear_rect before printing. Reserve six cells for a signed 16-bit field.

The tile-write intrinsics check LCD state: with LCD off they write immediately; with LCD on they wait for writable LCD modes and use DI/EI around writes. That path can enable interrupts on return, so do not assume it preserves a disabled interrupt state. The samples and byte-level tests here perform their writes with LCD off.

The complete sample includes text.c once so its library implementation is compiled with the program. Do not also pass lib/text.c as a separate input for this sample. To customize TEXT_* tile constants, define them before including rpg.h and the implementation; apply the same definitions wherever the library is compiled.

Usage example

c
text_print_s16(11,12,(s16)32768);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The S16 row shows -32768 starting at (11,12), using six cells including the minus sign. It is green on CGB. This exercises the lowest signed 16-bit value, whose positive magnitude does not fit in s16.

Verification compares every visible pixel and all 1024 BG-map bytes in both sample screens. Separate DMG/CGB ROMs check all 256 unsigned byte values, decimal digit boundaries and signed extremes, preserving dots beside each numeric output as guards. Layout checks include empty and narrow rectangles, map-edge placement, raw control-valued tile bytes and the window cursor after absolute writes. These are emulator tests, not physical-hardware tests.

void text_print_s16(u8 x, u8 y, s16 value)
{
    u16 magnitude;
    if (value < 0) {
        __settile_xy(x, y, (u8)'-');
        magnitude = (u16)((s16)0 - value);
        text_print_u16_width((u8)(x + 1), y, magnitude, text_dec_digits_u16(magnitude));
        return;
    }
    text_print_u16(x, y, (u16)value);
}

text_set_speed

Set the number of VBlank waits performed after each ordinary character written by text_print or text_print_far. Zero removes these per-character waits. Opening or closing an area does not reset this setting. Explicit WAIT commands still wait even when the character speed is zero.

Syntax

c
void text_set_speed(u8 speed);

Parameters

speed

VBlank waits after each displayed character, from 0 to 255. This is a wait count, not milliseconds. The setting does not affect text_print_xy, numeric helpers or the choice list.

Return value

No return value. Any drawing or blocking waits occur before the function returns.

Conditions and limits

Use a valid BG-map rectangle and load font/frame tiles first. The software text area uses the BG map selected by LCDC bit 3; it does not enable the hardware Window layer. Use VBK 0 on CGB for tile numbers and set color attributes separately. The examples provide the ASCII-mapped font and frame, cursor and page-indicator tiles. Dialogue and choice labels use byte-sized tile IDs, not UTF-8 decoding. To display characters outside the supplied font, provide the glyph tiles and encode the text for those IDs; keep dialogue control-byte values reserved.

These are blocking helpers: they do not call your game update, music service or rendering loop while waiting. With the LCD off, __wait_vblank returns immediately, so character speed and WAIT do not create frame delays. Keep the LCD enabled for timed dialogue and frame-paced input polling. Use a game-side state machine when other work must advance during a conversation.

The underlying safe tile writes wait for writable LCD modes when the LCD is on and use DI/EI around writes. They can enable interrupts rather than preserving an initially disabled interrupt state. Do not call these blocking helpers from an interrupt handler or depend on them to preserve that state.

Each complete example includes text.c once. Build the example with the library and manual-sample include directories; do not also add lib/text.c as another source input. The far-stream example uses MBC5 with a 64 KiB ROM so its bank-2 data is present.

Usage example

c
text_set_speed(2);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The flow example uses speed 2 for the near and banked dialogue and includes a WAIT operand of 12. The finished image shows the text after those waits; a separate frame trace checks speed 3, an explicit five-wait command and a four-wait command while closed. A final screenshot alone is not used to verify timing.

The emulator checks compare complete BG-map contents and the four sample images. Additional runs cover open/close state, ordinary and banked control streams, timed waits, explicit and automatic page waits, A/B/START advance, held buttons, wraparound choices, empty lists and simultaneous-input priority. Checkpoints before and after scripted input verify that page waits actually block. Physical hardware and interrupt concurrency are not tested.

unit_attack_range

Mark cells whose Manhattan distance lies between atk_min and atk_max, inclusive.

Syntax

c
u8 unit_attack_range(unit_t* u, u8* out_mask);

Parameters

u

Valid unit_t: cell position, move in steps, inclusive atk_min/atk_max range, hp and acted for action eligibility.

out_mask

Writable width*height bytes; receives zero or one for each cell.

Return value

Returns 1 for an available map, 0 for zero dimensions.

Conditions and limits

Coordinates address cells in the current map: 8×8 pixels for ordinary tiles, 16×16 pixels for metatiles.

Ignores obstacles, line of sight and friendly units. Keep evaluated distances at most 255. If minimum range exceeds maximum range, every cell is zero.

Usage example

c
result[46]=unit_attack_range(&hero,mask);result[47]=mask[12];result[48]=mask[14];

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The left grid shows movement costs within three steps; the right shows a shortest route from S to G. Green asterisks trace nine steps around a red three-cell wall; blue digits show costs. DMG uses the same layout in black. RAM checks also demonstrate that the attack mask ignores walls.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\batch3_map_path.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\batch3_map_path.gb --no-cache --no-disasm --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k --ramsize=none
Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:352

Declaration notes (original source)
Mark cells whose Manhattan distance falls within the inclusive attack range.
This geometric mask does not test obstacles, line of sight or other units.

kitaqgb/lib/slg_unit.c:38

c
u8 unit_attack_range(unit_t* u, u8* out_mask)
{
    u8 w = map_current_width();
    u8 h = map_current_height();
    u8 y;

    if (w == 0 || h == 0) return 0;

    __memset(out_mask, 0, (u16)((u16)w * (u16)h));
    y = 0;
    while (y < h) {
        u8 x = 0;
        while (x < w) {
            u8 dist = __manhattan(u->x, u->y, x, y);
            if (dist >= u->atk_min && dist <= u->atk_max) {
                out_mask[__map_index(x, y, w)] = 1;
            }
            x++;
        }
        y++;
    }
    return 1;
}

unit_move_range

Build a movement mask of cells reachable within the unit’s move allowance.

Syntax

c
u8 unit_move_range(unit_t* u, u8* out_mask);

Parameters

u

Valid unit_t: cell position, move in steps, inclusive atk_min/atk_max range, hp and acted for action eligibility.

out_mask

Writable width*height bytes; receives zero or one for each cell.

Return value

Returns 1 for an available map, 0 for zero dimensions. The unit’s origin must be in bounds.

Conditions and limits

Coordinates address cells in the current map: 8×8 pixels for ordinary tiles, 16×16 pixels for metatiles.

Search uses about 4 KiB of shared, non-reentrant workspace. Limit maps to 1024 cells and explored distances to 254. Distance 0xFF means unreached, so a 255-step route is not representable. Cost/mask outputs need width*height writable bytes.

The origin is seeded as reachable even when blocked. HP, acted and other units do not affect the movement mask.

Usage example

c
result[43]=unit_move_range(&hero,mask);result[44]=mask[12];result[45]=mask[14];

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The left grid shows movement costs within three steps; the right shows a shortest route from S to G. Green asterisks trace nine steps around a red three-cell wall; blue digits show costs. DMG uses the same layout in black. RAM checks also demonstrate that the attack mask ignores walls.
