kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:349

Declaration notes (original source)
Build movement costs, then convert reachable cells to one and unreachable
0xFF cells to zero. The caller provides one output byte per current-map cell
and a valid unit origin; path-search workspace limits also apply.

kitaqgb/lib/slg_unit.c:15

c
u8 unit_move_range(unit_t* u, u8* out_mask)
{
    u8 w = map_current_width();
    u8 h = map_current_height();
    u16 total;
    u16 i;

    if (w == 0 || h == 0) return 0;

    // A valid origin is required: the fill leaves storage unchanged on invalid origins, but this loop still converts it.
    range_fill_move(u->x, u->y, u->move, out_mask);
    total = (u16)((u16)w * (u16)h);
    i = 0;
    while (i < total) {
        out_mask[i] = (u8)((out_mask[i] == 0xFF) ? 0 : 1);
        i++;
    }
    return 1;
}
weighted_choice

Select an item index from a list of relative byte weights. The function sums the weights, reduces one rng16 draw modulo that total, then finds the first cumulative interval containing the result. With weights [1, 3, 6], indices 0, 1 and 2 own intervals 0, 1–3 and 4–9.

Syntax

c
u8 weighted_choice(const u8* weights, u8 count);

Parameters

weights

Pointer to count readable u8 weights. The array is not modified. Zero-weight items are skipped when the total is positive. With count == 0 the pointer is not read and may be null; otherwise provide a valid array.

count

Number of weights, 0–255. At most 255 weights of 255 sum to 65025, which fits the function's u16 accumulator. The function scans the list to total the weights, then scans until it finds the selected interval.

Return value

For a positive total, an index from 0 through count−1 after two byte draws. If count is zero or every weight is zero, returns zero without drawing. That fallback is indistinguishable from a valid selection of index 0, so check empty or all-zero lists yourself when that distinction matters.

Conditions and limits

The weights define relative interval sizes, not guaranteed observed percentages. Both the rng16 output distribution and reduction modulo the total affect the actual frequencies. A positive total always consumes two byte draws, even if only one item has a nonzero weight.

These calls share persistent state. Reproduction requires the same target, seed and sequence of calls, including calls made by other helpers. Keep seed and draw operations in one execution context; these checks do not establish safe concurrent use from an interrupt handler.

GB and FC use different algorithms and do not promise the same sequence for the same seed. These are deterministic gameplay generators, not a source of cryptographic randomness; the tests check implementation behavior, not statistical quality or period.

Include rpg.h and compile lib/rng.c alongside your game when using the library functions. The __rng_seed and __rng8 intrinsics themselves are emitted by the compiler; a program using only those two needs no rng.c object.

Usage example

c
weights[0]=1;weights[1]=3;weights[2]=6;
rng_seed(0x1234);
chosen=weighted_choice(weights,3); // 546 % 10 = 6 selects index 2.
empty=weighted_choice((const u8*)0,0); // No items: 0 is a fallback, not a chosen item.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This sample assigns weights 1, 3 and 6 to three items. The seeded word 546 gives remainder 6, which lies in index 2's interval 4–9; WEIGHT INDEX displays 00002. EMPTY LIST displays 00000 as an empty-list fallback, not a successful choice of item 0.

The complete program prints decimal results on a white background: black text on DMG, blue text on CGB. FAILED must read 00000. The pictures show the actual emulator output of this sample.

Verification compared 32 outputs and eight subsequent byte draws per case with an independent host model: 93 GB cases and 18 FC cases, including constant/runtime seeds and GB range/chance/weight boundaries. The teaching screens were checked after 240 emulator frames. Physical hardware and statistical quality were not tested.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\rng_choices.c .\kitaqgb\lib\rng.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\rng_choices.gb --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --no-cache --no-disasm
Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/rpg.h:203

Declaration notes (original source)
Select an index from cumulative byte weights using a 16-bit random draw.
A zero total, including an empty list, returns zero; callers must distinguish
that case from a valid index. Modulo reduction can introduce a small bias.

kitaqgb/lib/rng.c:61

c
u8 weighted_choice(const u8* weights, u8 count)
{
    u8 i;
    u16 total;
    u16 pick;
    u16 acc;

    // At most 255 byte weights sum to 65025, so this accumulator fits u16.
    // A nonempty list requires count readable weight bytes.
    total = 0;
    i = 0;
    while (i < count) {
        total = (u16)(total + (u16)weights[i]);
        i++;
    }

    if (total == 0) return 0;

    pick = (u16)(rng16() % total);
    acc = 0;
    i = 0;
    while (i < count) {
        acc = (u16)(acc + (u16)weights[i]);
        if (pick < acc) return i;
        i++;
    }

    return (u8)(count - 1);
}

scene.h — Scene registration, changes and updates

Dispatch a scene table’s enter, update, draw and exit handlers to switch between screens such as a title and gameplay.

scene_change

Exit the current scene, if any, and enter the requested scene.

Syntax

c
void scene_change(u8 scene_id);

Parameters

scene_id

Index of the scene to enter, from 0 through count−1.

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

Out-of-range IDs are ignored. A valid change runs exit, stores the new ID and change flag, then runs enter. Selecting the same ID still runs exit and enter. The caller owns the scene table. Keep it and the targets of its ordinary function pointers valid while in use. Null callbacks are skipped. Do not recursively change scenes or replace the table from enter/exit callbacks.

Usage example

c
scene_change(0);scene_change(9);result[11]=events;result[12]=scene_was_changed();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

The program activates 0, ignores invalid ID 9, transitions 0→1 and re-enters 1→1, checking callback order.

Selecting the current ID still performs exit/enter. Callbacks run synchronously.

kitaqgb/lib/scene.c:27

c
void scene_change(u8 scene_id)
{
    SceneFunc fn;

    if (scene_id >= scene_count) return;

    // Exit/enter handlers must not recursively change scenes or replace this shared table.
    if (scene_has_current != 0) {
        fn = scene_table[(__safe_index u8)scene_current].exit;
        if (fn != 0) fn();
    }

    scene_current = scene_id;
    scene_has_current = 1;
    scene_changed = 1;

    fn = scene_table[(__safe_index u8)scene_current].enter;
    if (fn != 0) fn();
}

scroll.h — Background, window and split scrolling

Control immediate and buffered background/window scrolling and up to eight raster splits. Distinguish getter-managed current values, live hardware registers and pending values.

Scroll_BgAdd

Add signed deltas to tracked background coordinates and apply them immediately.

Syntax

c
void Scroll_BgAdd(s8 dx, s8 dy);

Parameters

dx

Signed horizontal pixel delta, −128 through 127.

dy

Signed vertical pixel delta, −128 through 127.

Return value

No return value. The affected state and when it takes effect are described in this entry.

Conditions and limits

No wait is performed. Immediate setters/additions synchronize the affected pending pair to current values and clear its dirty flag. Even a single-axis immediate setter cancels the other pending axis in the same pair. Results wrap modulo 256. Additions start from tracked current values, not pending values or temporary raster register values. This function wraps __scroll_bg_add.

Usage example

c
Scroll_BgAdd(-20,3);result[22]=M_SCX;result[23]=M_SCY;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Use Scroll functions to learn immediate updates, staging, flushing, addition and visibility. Flushing changes BG X from 250 to 16 and WX from 23 to 39. The window bit is 32 after show and 0 after hide.

Complete example program

Scroll_GetWindowX

Read the tracked current window WX value.

Syntax

c
u8 Scroll_GetWindowX();

Return value

Returns the tracked current byte, 0–255. WX includes its seven-pixel hardware offset.

Conditions and limits

This is not a hardware-register read. It excludes pending buffered values, direct register writes and temporary values applied by raster splits. This function wraps __scroll_win_x_get.

Usage example

c
result[12]=Scroll_GetWindowX();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Use Scroll functions to learn immediate updates, staging, flushing, addition and visibility. Flushing changes BG X from 250 to 16 and WX from 23 to 39. The window bit is 32 after show and 0 after hide.

Scroll_SetBg

Parameters

Scroll_SplitCommit

Capture base window visibility and arm the first scanline event in the split table.

Syntax

c
void Scroll_SplitCommit();

Return value

No return value. The affected state and when it takes effect are described in this entry.

Conditions and limits

The shared table holds eight entries. Appending neither applies nor sorts them, and excess entries are ignored. Rebuild with reset→push→commit at a safe frame boundary and space events far enough apart for the handler to finish. Interrupt latency means the scheduled line and first affected pixel need not coincide. A nonempty table enables VBlank/STAT in IE and executes EI. An empty table disables the LYC source but does not restore IE or CPU interrupt state. This function wraps __scroll_split_commit.

Usage example

c
Scroll_SplitCommit();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Use Scroll wrappers for three background-scroll bands. Events at LY=64 and 104 change X to 8 and 16, positioning 24×16 rectangles at (32,16), (24,80) and (16,112). The image makes each band’s displacement visible.

Append an event that changes color zero of CGB background palette zero.

Syntax

ly

Scanline event number; use 0–143 for visible events and append in ascending order. A first entry at zero is applied during VBlank.

CGB-only. Uses one entry in the eight-slot split table through the extended split operation. Palette writes wait for accessible PPU time. In this normal-speed CGB sample, LY=64/112 events become visible from rows 66/114. Do not equate the event line with the first rendered line.

Change CGB background color zero during the frame. At normal speed, this sample renders rows 0–65 blue, 66–113 red and 114–143 green. Events are scheduled at 0, 64 and 112; interrupt handling and palette access add latency. DMG does not provide these color palettes.

Append a split entry whose flags select background, window, visibility or background-color-zero operations.

Syntax

void Scroll_SplitPushEx(u8 ly, u8 scx, u8 scy, u8 wx, u8 wy, u8 flags);

Parameters

ly

Scanline event number; use 0–143 for visible events and append in ascending order. A first entry at zero is applied during VBlank.

scx

Horizontal background scroll, 0–255 pixels; increasing it moves the background left.

scy

Vertical background scroll, 0–255 pixels; increasing it moves the background up.

Raw WX byte, 0–255: add 7 to the desired screen X; the left edge uses 7.

slg.h — Boards, move lists and undo

A byte-valued board, bounded move list and undo-record stack. The game combines these operations to apply moves or undo records to its board.

slg_board_clear

Fill every cell of the board with the requested value.

Syntax

c
void slg_board_clear(SLGBoard* board, u8 value);

Parameters

board

The SLGBoard to operate on; initialization requires non-NULL storage.

value

Byte value to store; the game assigns its meaning, such as a piece or terrain type.

Return value

No return value. The affected state and when it takes effect are described in this entry.

Conditions and limits

Storage is supplied by the caller. Initialization neither allocates nor erases it. Board coordinates are measured in cells.

Usage example

c
slg_board_clear(&board,0);result[1]=cells[0];result[2]=cells[11];

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Learn the separate roles of boards, move lists and undo records. Board initialization retains 9; a third append to a two-slot list returns 0. Popping alone leaves the board at 8; explicitly applying the retrieved record restores 7.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\batch2_board.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\batch2_board.gb --no-cache --no-disasm --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k
Implementation and source

kitaqgb/lib/slg.h:33

Declaration notes (original source)
Fill every cell with value; a null board is ignored. A valid board must own
enough accessible cell storage for its declared dimensions.

kitaqgb/lib/slg_board.c:36

c
void slg_board_clear(SLGBoard* board, u8 value)
{
    u16 total;
    u16 i;
    u8* p;
    if (board == 0) return;
    total = (u16)((u16)board->width * (u16)board->height);
    i = 0;
    p = board->cells;
    while (i < total) {
        *p = value;
        p++;
        i++;
    }
}

Read one cell; a NULL board or out-of-bounds coordinate returns zero.

c
u8 slg_board_get(const SLGBoard* board, u8 x, u8 y)
{
    u8* p;
    if (board == 0) return 0;
    if (x >= board->width || y >= board->height) return 0;
    p = slg_cell_ptr((SLGBoard*)board, x, y);
    return *p;
}

u8 slg_move_list_push(SLGMoveList* list, u8 x, u8 y, u8 value)
{
    SLGMove* move;

    if (list->count >= list->capacity) return 0;
    move = &list->items[(__safe_index u8)list->count];
    move->x = x;
    move->y = y;
    move->value = value;
    list->count++;
    return 1;
}

kitaqgb/lib/slg_board.c:128

c
u8 slg_undo_pop(SLGUndoStack* stack, SLGMove* out_move)
{
    if (stack == 0) return 0;
    if (stack->count == 0) return 0;
    stack->count--;
    if (out_move != 0) {
        out_move->x = stack->items[stack->count].x;
        out_move->y = stack->items[stack->count].y;
        out_move->value = stack->items[stack->count].value;
    }
    return 1;
}

sprite.h — OBJ allocation, positioning, metasprites and animation

Sprites are movable hardware objects, normally 8×8 or 8×16 pixels, described by entries in Object Attribute Memory (OAM). Allocate slots, set their position, tile and attributes in shadow OAM, then transfer that data. A metasprite combines several slots into one object. GB provides 40 slots with a 10-per-scanline limit; FC provides 64 with an 8-per-scanline limit.

GB attributes: bit 4 selects DMG palette OBP1; bits 5/6 flip X/Y; bit 7 places the sprite behind nonzero background pixels. On CGB, bits 0..2 select the object palette and bit 3 the tile-data VRAM bank; the DMG palette-select bit is not used for native CGB colors.

The example uses the full GB sprite library. Defining KQ_SPRITE_MINIMAL_RUNTIME omits sprite_free, sprite_set_pos, sprite_count_used, both scanline queries, metasprite_draw and anim_update from sprite.c; do not enable it when using those functions.

anim_update

Advance a SpriteAnim timer and return the selected tile number. After ticks_per_frame calls, move to the next consecutive tile; wrap to the first frame after frame_count frames. The caller applies the result with sprite_set_tile.

Syntax

c
u8 anim_update(SpriteAnim* anim);

Parameters

anim

Writable SpriteAnim state with first_tile, frame_count, frame, ticks and ticks_per_frame. Keep frame below frame_count and ticks below ticks_per_frame when those counts are nonzero.

Return value

Selected eight-bit tile number; 0 for a null state pointer. The function does not write OAM.

Conditions and limits

A zero frame_count returns first_tile without advancing; zero ticks_per_frame freezes the current frame. Calls, not video frames, advance the timer. Tile arithmetic wraps at 256 and does not skip alternate tiles in 8×16 mode.

The example uses the full GB sprite library. Defining KQ_SPRITE_MINIMAL_RUNTIME omits sprite_free, sprite_set_pos, sprite_count_used, both scanline queries, metasprite_draw and anim_update from sprite.c; do not enable it when using those functions.

Usage example

c
sprite_example_animation.first_tile=128;sprite_example_animation.frame_count=2;
sprite_example_animation.frame=0;sprite_example_animation.ticks=0;
sprite_example_animation.ticks_per_frame=2;
sprite_example_expect(anim_update(&sprite_example_animation)==128);
tile=anim_update(&sprite_example_animation);
sprite_example_expect(tile==129);sprite_set_tile(5,tile);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

With first_tile=128, two frames and two calls per frame, the first update returns arrow tile 128 and the second returns square tile 129. The square shown beside ANIMATION proves that the returned tile was applied to OAM.

This program teaches sprite allocation, positioning, flips, composite objects, overlap, animation and the scanline limit. The two digits at the upper right must be 00: every in-program check passed. Each arrow and square occupies an 8×8 tile.

NORMAL shows a right-pointing arrow at (88,16). FLIP X points left at (88,32); FLIP Y vertically mirrors the arrow at (88,48). META places two arrows at (88,64) and (96,64). OVERLAP puts the arrow at (88,80) in front of the square at (92,80), with the square visible through transparent arrow pixels. ANIMATION shows the square at (88,96). The areas at (120,16) and (120,32) remain empty after hiding and freeing their slots.

CGB and FC arrows use a green shaft, red outline and blue tip details; the square is green. Transparent pixels reveal the white GB background or black FC background. DMG uses light gray, dark gray and black instead of red, green and blue.

The row below SCAN LIMIT starts at (8,128). The program submits 11 GB sprites or 9 FC sprites on that line, deliberately one too many. Expect 10 visible arrows on GB and 8 on FC; the final submitted arrow is absent. The software peak and warning checks must still report 11/9 and 1.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\sprite_shapes.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\sprite_shapes.gb --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --no-cache --no-disasm

kitaqgb/lib/sprite.h:86

Declaration notes (original source)
Advance animation ticks/frame with wrapping frame selection and return the
resulting tile. Zero ticks-per-frame freezes animation; null state returns zero.

kitaqgb/lib/sprite.c:211

c
u8 anim_update(SpriteAnim* anim)
{
    if (anim == 0) return 0;
    if (anim->frame_count == 0) return anim->first_tile;
    if (anim->ticks_per_frame == 0) return (u8)(anim->first_tile + anim->frame);

    anim->ticks++;
    if (anim->ticks >= anim->ticks_per_frame) {
        anim->ticks = 0;
        anim->frame++;
        if (anim->frame >= anim->frame_count) anim->frame = 0;
    }
    return (u8)(anim->first_tile + anim->frame);
}
metasprite_draw

Place a counted array of sprite parts in consecutive slots. Each part supplies a signed offset, tile and attributes. The routine activates new slots, overwrites existing active slots and stops at the slot limit.

Syntax

c
u8 metasprite_draw(u8 first_id, u8 x, u8 y, const MetaSpritePart* parts, u8 count);

Parameters

first_id

Slot ID in 0..SPRITE_MAX-1: 0..39 by default on GB, 0..63 on FC. Out-of-range IDs are ignored.

x

Horizontal position in pixels, stored as an unsigned byte. This is a pixel coordinate, not a tile coordinate.

y

Screen Y coordinate in pixels. The GB wrapper adds 16 before storing it in OAM.

parts

Readable array containing at least count MetaSpritePart records. Each four-byte record contains signed dx/dy offsets followed by tile and flags; there is no terminator.

count

Number of parts, as an unsigned byte. Zero performs no writes. Fewer parts are written if the consecutive slot range reaches SPRITE_MAX.

Return value

Number of parts written, from 0 to count. Check this result to detect truncation at the slot limit.

Conditions and limits

Position, tile, attribute and hide operations change shadow data. They do not allocate a slot or immediately change the hardware OAM; transfer the completed frame with sprite_flush_oam.

Offsets are signed bytes added to the supplied origin, then wrapped to eight bits. Keep the part array readable for the whole call. Writing an active slot replaces its contents; the function does not protect another object's slots.

The example uses the full GB sprite library. Defining KQ_SPRITE_MINIMAL_RUNTIME omits sprite_free, sprite_set_pos, sprite_count_used, both scanline queries, metasprite_draw and anim_update from sprite.c; do not enable it when using those functions.

Usage example

c
sprite_example_expect(metasprite_draw(10,88,SPRITE_EXAMPLE_Y(64),sprite_example_pair,2)==2);
sprite_example_expect(sprite_count_used()==9); // Sparse IDs count actual active slots.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Initialization yields zero allocated slots. Eight allocations return IDs 0..7. Hiding slot 6 keeps the count at 8; freeing slot 7 twice leaves 7. Placing the pair in slots 10 and 11 raises the count to 9.

OVERLAP puts the arrow at (88,80) in front of the square at (92,80), with the square visible through transparent arrow pixels. ANIMATION shows the square at (88,96). The areas at (120,16) and (120,32) remain empty after hiding and freeing their slots.

CGB and FC arrows use a green shaft, red outline and blue tip details; the square is green. Transparent pixels reveal the white GB background or black FC background. DMG uses light gray, dark gray and black instead of red, green and blue.

kitaqgb/lib/sprite.h:83

Declaration notes (original source)
Place consecutive parts, counting each newly activated slot once. Existing
active slots are overwritten without increasing the allocation count. Return
the number written; an invalid first slot or zero count writes nothing.

kitaqgb/lib/sprite.c:191

c
u8 metasprite_draw(u8 first_id, u8 x, u8 y, const MetaSpritePart* parts, u8 count)
{
    u8 i = 0;
    while (i < count) {
        u8 id = (u8)(first_id + i);
        if (id >= SPRITE_MAX) return i;
        if (kq_sprite_active[id] == 0) {
            kq_sprite_active[id] = 1;
            kq_sprite_used = (u8)(kq_sprite_used + 1);
        }
        sprite_set_pos(id, (u8)(x + parts[i].dx), (u8)(y + parts[i].dy));
        sprite_set_tile(id, parts[i].tile);
        sprite_set_flags(id, parts[i].flags);
        i++;
    }
    return count;
}

kitaqgb/lib/sprite.h:53

Declaration notes (original source)
Claim the first free slot, hide it, and return its ID; return 0xFF when full.
Previously stored tile/flag bytes are retained until the caller replaces them.

kitaqgb/lib/sprite.c:60

c
u8 sprite_alloc()
{
    u8 i = 0;
    while (i < SPRITE_MAX) {
        if (kq_sprite_active[i] == 0) {
            kq_sprite_active[i] = 1;
            kq_sprite_used++;
            sprite_hide(i);
            return i;
        }
        i++;
    }
    return 0xFF;
}
sprite_count_used

Return the number of allocated slots, including hidden sprites and slots activated by metasprite_draw. This is an allocation count, not the number of sprites visible on screen.

This program teaches sprite allocation, positioning, flips, composite objects, overlap, animation and the scanline limit. The two digits at the upper right must be 00: every in-program check passed. Each arrow and square occupies an 8×8 tile.

NORMAL shows a right-pointing arrow at (88,16). FLIP X points left at (88,32); FLIP Y vertically mirrors the arrow at (88,48). META places two arrows at (88,64) and (96,64). OVERLAP puts the arrow at (88,80) in front of the square at (92,80), with the square visible through transparent arrow pixels. ANIMATION shows the square at (88,96). The areas at (120,16) and (120,32) remain empty after hiding and freeing their slots.

CGB and FC arrows use a green shaft, red outline and blue tip details; the square is green. Transparent pixels reveal the white GB background or black FC background. DMG uses light gray, dark gray and black instead of red, green and blue.

The row below SCAN LIMIT starts at (8,128). The program submits 11 GB sprites or 9 FC sprites on that line, deliberately one too many. Expect 10 visible arrows on GB and 8 on FC; the final submitted arrow is absent. The software peak and warning checks must still report 11/9 and 1.

void sprite_flush_oam_now()
{
    SpriteDmaRoutine dma;
    if (kq_sprite_dma_ready == 0) {

    __asm {

    }

void sprite_free(u8 id)
{

void sprite_init()
{
    u8 i = 0;
    kq_sprite_used = 0;
    kq_sprite_height = 8;
    kq_sprite_dma_ready = 0;
    while (i < SPRITE_MAX) {
        kq_sprite_active[i] = 0;
        kq_sprite_oam[i].y = 0;
        kq_sprite_oam[i].x = 0;
        kq_sprite_oam[i].tile = 0;
        kq_sprite_oam[i].flags = 0;
        i++;
    }
}

Estimate the largest number of active sprites overlapping one visible scanline from their tracked vertical positions and kq_sprite_height.

kitaqgb/lib/sprite.h:79

Declaration notes (original source)
Estimate the largest overlap of active, non-hidden shadow sprites across
visible scanlines using the configured sprite height. This is a software
overlap count, not a rendered-pixel or hardware-priority simulation.

kitaqgb/lib/sprite.c:158

c
u8 sprite_max_scanline_count()
{
    u8 line = 0;
    u8 best = 0;
    while (line < 144) {
        u8 i = 0;
        u8 count = 0;
        u8 ly_oam = (u8)(line + 16);
        while (i < SPRITE_MAX) {
            u8 sy = kq_sprite_oam[i].y;
            if (kq_sprite_active[i] != 0 && sy != 0) {
                if (ly_oam >= sy && ly_oam < (u8)(sy + kq_sprite_height)) {
                    count++;
                }
            }
            i++;
        }
        if (count > best) best = count;
        line++;
    }
    return best;
}
sprite_set_flags

Replace the entire sprite attribute byte. Combine the platform's flag constants to select flips, palette and background priority; omitted bits are cleared.

Syntax

c
void sprite_set_flags(u8 id, u8 flags);

Parameters

id

Slot ID in 0..SPRITE_MAX-1: 0..39 by default on GB, 0..63 on FC. Out-of-range IDs are ignored.

flags

Complete hardware attribute byte, built with the SPRITE_FLAG_* constants for this platform. Combine flags with bitwise OR (|).

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

Position, tile, attribute and hide operations change shadow data. They do not allocate a slot or immediately change the hardware OAM; transfer the completed frame with sprite_flush_oam.

GB attributes: bit 4 selects DMG palette OBP1; bits 5/6 flip X/Y; bit 7 places the sprite behind nonzero background pixels. On CGB, bits 0..2 select the object palette and bit 3 the tile-data VRAM bank; the DMG palette-select bit is not used for native CGB colors.

The example uses the full GB sprite library. Defining KQ_SPRITE_MINIMAL_RUNTIME omits sprite_free, sprite_set_pos, sprite_count_used, both scanline queries, metasprite_draw and anim_update from sprite.c; do not enable it when using those functions.

Move a GB sprite in shadow OAM using screen pixel coordinates. The function adds the hardware offsets of 8 to X and 16 to Y.

Syntax

void sprite_set_pos(u8 id, u8 x, u8 y);

Parameters

id

Slot ID in 0..SPRITE_MAX-1: 0..39 by default on GB, 0..63 on FC. Out-of-range IDs are ignored.

x

Horizontal position in pixels, stored as an unsigned byte. This is a pixel coordinate, not a tile coordinate.

Screen Y coordinate in pixels. The GB wrapper adds 16 before storing it in OAM.

None (void).

Position, tile, attribute and hide operations change shadow data. They do not allocate a slot or immediately change the hardware OAM; transfer the completed frame with sprite_flush_oam.

Coordinate additions use eight-bit arithmetic and wrap modulo 256; the library does not clip to the screen. A valid slot may be edited even when its allocation flag is clear.

sprite_set_tile

Replace the tile number of one shadow OAM entry. This selects graphics already in tile memory; it neither uploads graphics nor allocates a sprite.

Syntax

c
void sprite_set_tile(u8 id, u8 tile);

Parameters

id

Slot ID in 0..SPRITE_MAX-1: 0..39 by default on GB, 0..63 on FC. Out-of-range IDs are ignored.

tile

Eight-bit tile number. Load its graphics first. Hardware rules for 8×16 sprites still apply; this function does not adjust the number for paired tiles.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

Position, tile, attribute and hide operations change shadow data. They do not allocate a slot or immediately change the hardware OAM; transfer the completed frame with sprite_flush_oam.

The example uses the full GB sprite library. Defining KQ_SPRITE_MINIMAL_RUNTIME omits sprite_free, sprite_set_pos, sprite_count_used, both scanline queries, metasprite_draw and anim_update from sprite.c; do not enable it when using those functions.

Usage example

c
sprite_set_tile(5,129); // Select the green square beside ANIMATION.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

With first_tile=128, two frames and two calls per frame, the first update returns arrow tile 128 and the second returns square tile 129. The square shown beside ANIMATION proves that the returned tile was applied to OAM.

This program teaches sprite allocation, positioning, flips, composite objects, overlap, animation and the scanline limit. The two digits at the upper right must be 00: every in-program check passed. Each arrow and square occupies an 8×8 tile.

NORMAL shows a right-pointing arrow at (88,16). FLIP X points left at (88,32); FLIP Y vertically mirrors the arrow at (88,48). META places two arrows at (88,64) and (96,64). OVERLAP puts the arrow at (88,80) in front of the square at (92,80), with the square visible through transparent arrow pixels. ANIMATION shows the square at (88,96). The areas at (120,16) and (120,32) remain empty after hiding and freeing their slots.

CGB and FC arrows use a green shaft, red outline and blue tip details; the square is green. Transparent pixels reveal the white GB background or black FC background. DMG uses light gray, dark gray and black instead of red, green and blue.

The row below SCAN LIMIT starts at (8,128). The program submits 11 GB sprites or 9 FC sprites on that line, deliberately one too many. Expect 10 visible arrows on GB and 8 on FC; the final submitted arrow is absent. The software peak and warning checks must still report 11/9 and 1.

system.h — Startup, frame counts, waits and interrupts

Manage frame-wait counts, callbacks after waits, and maskable CPU interrupt control.

system_disable_interrupts

Disable maskable CPU interrupts.

Syntax

void system_disable_interrupts();

Return value

No return value.

Conditions and limits

Keep protected updates short and restore interrupts appropriately afterward. Interrupt masking is separate from the conditions needed by a frame-wait routine.

On GB, waiting returns immediately with the LCD off, but the wrapper still increments its counter and calls its callback. Initialization alone does not configure the LCD or interrupt sources.

vram.h — Queued VRAM updates and transfer

Initialize the deferred VRAM command queue to empty and clear its overflow latch. This does not erase the screen, upload tile graphics or allocate hardware VRAM.

GB counts command slots: the default capacity is 32. Every queue helper uses one slot, even for a large or zero-length transfer. Set VRAM_QUEUE_MAX consistently in every compilation unit to a value from 1 to 255. An empty queue has used=0 and free=capacity.

Wait with __wait_vblank, then call vram_flush_now. Use this for a modest batch of queued screen changes. The single wait does not impose a transfer budget or guarantee that the entire batch finishes within one VBlank.

Build and consume the queue in coordinated phases. Do not append while an interrupt executes it, change its bookkeeping directly, or overwrite retained source data unintentionally. These APIs provide neither locking nor double buffering. Capacity describes the command buffer, not free bytes in hardware VRAM.

vram_clear_queue

Discard pending VRAM commands and clear the overflow flag without performing their writes.

Syntax

c
void vram_clear_queue();

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

GB counts command slots: the default capacity is 32. Every queue helper uses one slot, even for a large or zero-length transfer. Set VRAM_QUEUE_MAX consistently in every compilation unit to a value from 1 to 255. An empty queue has used=0 and free=capacity.

Build and consume the queue in coordinated phases. Do not append while an interrupt executes it, change its bookkeeping directly, or overwrite retained source data unintentionally. These APIs provide neither locking nor double buffering. Capacity describes the command buffer, not free bytes in hardware VRAM.

Usage example

c
vram_clear_queue();
if (vram_get_queue_used()!=0 || vram_get_overflowed()!=0) failures++;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This complete program demonstrates deferred writes, queue accounting and overflow recovery. Seven drawing calls use 7 of 32 command slots on GB, or 52 of 128 command bytes on FC: CAPACITY/USED/FREE reads 032/007/025 or 128/052/076. AFTER FLUSH and FAILED CHECKS must be 000; OVERFLOW SEEN must be 001. An intentional full-queue rejection tests the latch. Reading or flushing does not clear it; clearing the queue does. On FC, an uncommitted direct flush must leave the pending queue intact.

Image coordinates are pixels from the upper-left corner. Expect solid 8 × 8 squares at (16,16) and (32,16), a solid 32 × 24 rectangle at (16,32), and a 40 × 8 horizontal bar at (80,64). The final VBlank write adds an 8 × 8 square at (144,80). The discarded write at (144,24) must leave that cell blank. DMG uses black shapes on white, CGB uses red, blue and green shapes on white, and FC uses red, blue and green shapes on black. These emulator images do not constitute real-hardware verification.

Three original 8 × 8 patterns distinguish the copy operations: tile 1 is solid; tile 2 fills its left four columns; tile 3 is a left-aligned triangle widening from one pixel at the top to eight at the bottom. At (80,32), the 3 × 2 tile block must read [1,2,3] / [3,0,2], where 0 is blank. Its first source byte changes after queuing, so a solid tile there proves that the source pointer is retained. At (16,64), the copy shows [1,2,3]; at (48,64), the tiles alias shows [2,3]. Their dimensions are 24 × 16, 24 × 8 and 16 × 8 pixels respectively.

In CGB mode, the two upper squares, the three-pattern copy and the final VBlank square are red. The 32 × 24 rectangle and two-pattern copy are blue. The packed 3 × 2 block and 40 × 8 bar are green. Text remains black on white. Color checks cover each drawn pixel as well as geometry.

Wait with __wait_vblank, then call vram_flush_now. Use this for a modest batch of queued screen changes. The single wait does not impose a transfer budget or guarantee that the entire batch finishes within one VBlank.

Syntax

void vram_flush();

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

GB counts command slots: the default capacity is 32. Every queue helper uses one slot, even for a large or zero-length transfer. Set VRAM_QUEUE_MAX consistently in every compilation unit to a value from 1 to 255. An empty queue has used=0 and free=capacity.

Build and consume the queue in coordinated phases. Do not append while an interrupt executes it, change its bookkeeping directly, or overwrite retained source data unintentionally. These APIs provide neither locking nor double buffering. Capacity describes the command buffer, not free bytes in hardware VRAM.

vram_flush_now

Execute every queued command in insertion order, then set the used count to 0. No VBlank wait is performed here. The called safe VRAM intrinsics handle writable periods when the LCD is on, but a large queue can span several scanlines or frames. The overflow latch is preserved.

With the LCD on, safe write paths can enable interrupts; they do not preserve an interrupt-disabled calling state.

In CGB mode, the two upper squares, the three-pattern copy and the final VBlank square are red. The 32 × 24 rectangle and two-pattern copy are blue. The packed 3 × 2 block and 40 × 8 bar are green. Text remains black on white. Color checks cover each drawn pixel as well as geometry.

kitaqgb/lib/vram.h:61

Declaration notes (original source)
Execute pending commands in insertion order without waiting for VBlank here.
The caller must arrange suitable VRAM access timing and a sufficient transfer budget.
Only the used count is cleared; overflow stays latched until an explicit reset.

kitaqgb/lib/vram.c:125

c
void vram_flush_now()
{
    u8 i = 0;
    while (i < kq_vram_queue_used) {
        VramCommand* cmd = &kq_vram_queue[(__safe_index u8)i];
        if (cmd->kind == VRAM_CMD_BG_TILE) {
            __settile_xy(cmd->x, cmd->y, cmd->value);
        } else if (cmd->kind == VRAM_CMD_BG_RECT) {
            __settile_rect(cmd->x, cmd->y, cmd->w, cmd->h, cmd->value);
        } else if (cmd->kind == VRAM_CMD_BG_BLOCK) {
            __settilemap_rect(cmd->dst, cmd->x, cmd->y, cmd->w, cmd->h, cmd->src);
        } else if (cmd->kind == VRAM_CMD_MEMCPY) {
            __vram_copy(cmd->dst, cmd->src, cmd->len);
        } else if (cmd->kind == VRAM_CMD_MEMSET) {
            __vram_fill(cmd->dst, cmd->value, cmd->len);
        }
        i++;
    }
    kq_vram_queue_used = 0;
}
vram_get_overflowed

Read the queue-overflow flag without clearing it; it can retain an earlier failure.

Syntax

c
u8 vram_get_overflowed();

Return value

0 if no overflow is currently latched; 1 after a rejected append until explicit reset. Flushing does not clear this latch.

Conditions and limits

GB counts command slots: the default capacity is 32. Every queue helper uses one slot, even for a large or zero-length transfer. Set VRAM_QUEUE_MAX consistently in every compilation unit to a value from 1 to 255. An empty queue has used=0 and free=capacity.

Build and consume the queue in coordinated phases. Do not append while an interrupt executes it, change its bookkeeping directly, or overwrite retained source data unintentionally. These APIs provide neither locking nor double buffering. Capacity describes the command buffer, not free bytes in hardware VRAM.

Usage example

c
overflow_seen=vram_get_overflowed();
if (overflow_seen!=1) failures++;
// Reading the latch again does not clear it.
if (vram_get_overflowed()!=1) failures++;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This complete program demonstrates deferred writes, queue accounting and overflow recovery. Seven drawing calls use 7 of 32 command slots on GB, or 52 of 128 command bytes on FC: CAPACITY/USED/FREE reads 032/007/025 or 128/052/076. AFTER FLUSH and FAILED CHECKS must be 000; OVERFLOW SEEN must be 001. An intentional full-queue rejection tests the latch. Reading or flushing does not clear it; clearing the queue does. On FC, an uncommitted direct flush must leave the pending queue intact.

Image coordinates are pixels from the upper-left corner. Expect solid 8 × 8 squares at (16,16) and (32,16), a solid 32 × 24 rectangle at (16,32), and a 40 × 8 horizontal bar at (80,64). The final VBlank write adds an 8 × 8 square at (144,80). The discarded write at (144,24) must leave that cell blank. DMG uses black shapes on white, CGB uses red, blue and green shapes on white, and FC uses red, blue and green shapes on black. These emulator images do not constitute real-hardware verification.

Three original 8 × 8 patterns distinguish the copy operations: tile 1 is solid; tile 2 fills its left four columns; tile 3 is a left-aligned triangle widening from one pixel at the top to eight at the bottom. At (80,32), the 3 × 2 tile block must read [1,2,3] / [3,0,2], where 0 is blank. Its first source byte changes after queuing, so a solid tile there proves that the source pointer is retained. At (16,64), the copy shows [1,2,3]; at (48,64), the tiles alias shows [2,3]. Their dimensions are 24 × 16, 24 × 8 and 16 × 8 pixels respectively.

In CGB mode, the two upper squares, the three-pattern copy and the final VBlank square are red. The 32 × 24 rectangle and two-pattern copy are blue. The packed 3 × 2 block and 40 × 8 bar are green. Text remains black on white. Color checks cover each drawn pixel as well as geometry.

vram_queue_bg_block

Queue a w × h rectangle of tile numbers from src into the map at base. Source rows are tightly packed with w bytes each; destination rows are 32 bytes apart. The command retains the source pointer, so edits to the source before execution affect the displayed block.

Syntax

c
u8 vram_queue_bg_block(u16 base, u8 x, u8 y, u8 w, u8 h, const u8* src);

Parameters

base

Tile and rectangle commands select the background map from LCDC bit 3 when executed. On CGB, use VRAM bank 0 for tile numbers. A block uses its explicit base, normally 0x9800 or 0x9C00. Rows have a stride of 32 bytes; coordinates are not clipped.

x, y

Top-left coordinates in 8×8 tiles, not pixels. No clipping is performed. Keep the affected rectangle inside the intended map: x + w <= 32, and y + h <= 32 on GB or <= 30 in an FC nametable's tile area. For a single tile, use width and height 1.

w, h

Unsigned byte width and height in tiles. The source block contains w * h bytes in row order. Zero dimensions perform no visible writes, but queue-storage use follows the platform's record rules.

src

Near pointer to readable bytes, retained until execution. Keep the required bytes alive and their memory/ROM bank mapped for the entire flush; no bank number or payload copy is stored. A nonempty transfer requires a valid source. Do not use an expired local array.

Return value

1 when this command was queued, or 0 if no slot was available. A failure sets the overflow latch and leaves existing commands intact. An earlier overflow does not by itself make a later successful append return 0.

Conditions and limits

GB counts command slots: the default capacity is 32. Every queue helper uses one slot, even for a large or zero-length transfer. Set VRAM_QUEUE_MAX consistently in every compilation unit to a value from 1 to 255. An empty queue has used=0 and free=capacity.

Build and consume the queue in coordinated phases. Do not append while an interrupt executes it, change its bookkeeping directly, or overwrite retained source data unintentionally. These APIs provide neither locking nor double buffering. Capacity describes the command buffer, not free bytes in hardware VRAM.

kitaqgb/lib/vram.h:50

Declaration notes (original source)
Queue a tile-map rectangle while retaining src rather than copying its bytes.

kitaqgb/lib/vram.c:79

c
u8 vram_queue_bg_block(u16 base, u8 x, u8 y, u8 w, u8 h, const u8* src)
{
    VramCommand* cmd = vram_push(VRAM_CMD_BG_BLOCK);
    if (cmd == 0) return 0;
    cmd->dst = base;
    cmd->x = x;
    cmd->y = y;
    cmd->w = w;
    cmd->h = h;
    cmd->src = src;
    return 1;
}

Three original 8 × 8 patterns distinguish the copy operations: tile 1 is solid; tile 2 fills its left four columns; tile 3 is a left-aligned triangle widening from one pixel at the top to eight at the bottom. At (80,32), the 3 × 2 tile block must read [1,2,3] / [3,0,2], where 0 is blank. Its first source byte changes after queuing, so a solid tile there proves that the source pointer is retained. At (16,64), the copy shows [1,2,3]; at (48,64), the tiles alias shows [2,3]. Their dimensions are 24 × 16, 24 × 8 and 16 × 8 pixels respectively.

In CGB mode, the two upper squares, the three-pattern copy and the final VBlank square are red. The 32 × 24 rectangle and two-pattern copy are blue. The packed 3 × 2 block and 40 × 8 bar are green. Text remains black on white. Color checks cover each drawn pixel as well as geometry.

vram_queue_bg_tile

Queue one background tile-number write at (x, y). The visible tile changes when the queue executes. The command writes a map entry; it does not upload the tile's pixel data or change its palette attributes.

Syntax

c
u8 vram_queue_bg_tile(u8 x, u8 y, u8 tile);

Parameters

x, y

Top-left coordinates in 8×8 tiles, not pixels. No clipping is performed. Keep the affected rectangle inside the intended map: x + w <= 32, and y + h <= 32 on GB or <= 30 in an FC nametable's tile area. For a single tile, use width and height 1.

tile

Tile-map byte, 0–255. Load the corresponding graphic separately and select the intended pattern table/addressing mode. A tile number is neither a pointer nor a color value.

Return value

1 when this command was queued, or 0 if no slot was available. A failure sets the overflow latch and leaves existing commands intact. An earlier overflow does not by itself make a later successful append return 0.

Conditions and limits

GB counts command slots: the default capacity is 32. Every queue helper uses one slot, even for a large or zero-length transfer. Set VRAM_QUEUE_MAX consistently in every compilation unit to a value from 1 to 255. An empty queue has used=0 and free=capacity.

Tile and rectangle commands select the background map from LCDC bit 3 when executed. On CGB, use VRAM bank 0 for tile numbers. A block uses its explicit base, normally 0x9800 or 0x9C00. Rows have a stride of 32 bytes; coordinates are not clipped.

Build and consume the queue in coordinated phases. Do not append while an interrupt executes it, change its bookkeeping directly, or overwrite retained source data unintentionally. These APIs provide neither locking nor double buffering. Capacity describes the command buffer, not free bytes in hardware VRAM.

Usage example

c
check_result=vram_queue_bg_tile(2,2,1); // A solid 8x8 tile at pixel (16,16).
if (check_result!=1) failures++;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

AFTER FLUSH and FAILED CHECKS must be 000; OVERFLOW SEEN must be 001. An intentional full-queue rejection tests the latch. Reading or flushing does not clear it; clearing the queue does. On FC, an uncommitted direct flush must leave the pending queue intact.

At (80,32), the 3 × 2 tile block must read [1,2,3] / [3,0,2], where 0 is blank. Its first source byte changes after queuing, so a solid tile there proves that the source pointer is retained. vram_queue_memcpy

Queue a copy of len consecutive bytes from src to dst. Source and destination advance by one byte, without a tile-row stride. This can transfer map bytes or writable tile-pattern bytes; the function does not convert formats or infer how many bytes a tile occupies.

Syntax

c
u8 vram_queue_memcpy(u16 dst, const void* src, u16 len);

Parameters

dst

Destination byte address in VRAM (0x8000–0x9FFF), in the bank selected when executed. The transfer is contiguous, without tilemap row wrapping. Keep the entire destination range valid. With the LCD on, safe write paths can enable interrupts; they do not preserve an interrupt-disabled calling state.

src

Near pointer to readable bytes, retained until execution. Keep the required bytes alive and their memory/ROM bank mapped for the entire flush; no bank number or payload copy is stored. A nonempty transfer requires a valid source. Do not use an expired local array.

len

Number of consecutive bytes, 0–65535. It is not a tile count. Keep the complete address range inside valid source and writable destination storage; the API does not check bounds or prevent 16-bit address wrap.

wire3d.h — Wireframes for DMG

Monochrome 3D line drawing. Supply model vertices, edges and faces and object position, rotation and scale. Use initialization, frame start, drawing and upload in that order. Physics is separate. Angles have sixteen steps per turn; model scale 256 is unity.

Vec3 holds x/y/z, Edge vertex indices a/b, and Face triangle indices a/b/c. Model vertices, edges and faces point to these arrays; each count gives its length. edge_faces contains adjacent face indices f0/f1, with FACE_NONE for a missing face. MODEL_HIDDEN_LINES in flags requests face-based edge selection. Projected signed area determines face orientation, so vertex order matters.

Object stores a model reference, position x/y/z, angles rx/ry/rz, scale_q8 and visible. Objects may share a model, but drawing neither copies tables nor automatically switches their ROM banks. Keep referenced data readable throughout drawing. CGB Object also has a color index.

The 96-row Model also contains edge_masks and edge_mask_count. Supply a RAM table of 16-bit edge masks selected by object yaw, or set both fields to zero when unused.

Wire3D_BeginFrame

Begin drawing a frame and disable occlusion testing.

Syntax

c
void Wire3D_BeginFrame();

Return value

No return value; the state affected and display timing are described above.

Conditions and limits

WIRE3D_DMG_HEIGHT = 96. Clear staged pixels and occlusion mask and disable occlusion filtering. This leaves the displayed VRAM frame and pending BG tile queue unchanged.

This sample uses the 128x96 profile. Its viewport starts at screen (0,0). Reserve WRAM D000..DFFF and keep its bank mapping stable on CGB too. Shared state is not reentrant.

Usage example

c
#pragma bank 0
// Draw a frame with a gap, a projected diagonal, and a copied corner tile.
// The selected 96-line profile determines the stage layout and camera center.
#define WIRE3D_DMG_HEIGHT 96
#include "wire3d.h"
__location(0xC110) u16 result[8];
__location(0xFF47) u8 sample_bgp;
__location(0xFF40) u8 sample_lcdc;
__location(0xFF44) u8 sample_ly;
__location(0xFF4F) u8 sample_vbk;
__location(0xFF68) u8 sample_bgpi;
__location(0xFF69) u8 sample_bgpd;
u8 projected_x;
u8 projected_y;
void main() {
    u8 i;
    for(i=0;i<8;i++) result[i]=0;
    Wire3D_Init();
    // A CGB-compatible ROM also needs CGB palette and tile-map attributes.
    if(__cgb_is_cgb()) {
        while(sample_ly>=144) {} while(sample_ly<144) {}
        sample_lcdc=0; sample_vbk=1;
        __vram_memset_unsafe(0x9800,0,1024); sample_vbk=0;
        sample_bgpi=0x80; sample_bgpd=255; sample_bgpd=127;
        for(i=0;i<6;i++) sample_bgpd=0;
        sample_lcdc=0x81;
    }
    Wire3D_SetPalette(0xFC); // White background; every nonzero shade is black.
    result[0]=sample_bgp;
    Wire3D_SetCamera(8,0,0,0,0,0);
    result[1]=Wire3D_ProjectPoint(0,0,96,&projected_x,&projected_y);
    result[2]=projected_x; result[3]=projected_y;
    projected_x=91; projected_y=92;
    result[4]=Wire3D_ProjectPoint(0,0,7,&projected_x,&projected_y);

Wire3D_DrawLine2D

Draw an inclusive, four-connected screen-space line into the stage.

Syntax

c
void Wire3D_DrawLine2D(w3ddmg_u8 ax, w3ddmg_u8 ay, w3ddmg_u8 bx, w3ddmg_u8 by);

Parameters

ax

Vertex A X coordinate in viewport pixels.

ay

Vertex A Y coordinate in viewport pixels.

bx

Vertex B X coordinate in viewport pixels.

by

Vertex B Y coordinate in viewport pixels.

Return value

No return value; the state affected and display timing are described above.

Conditions and limits

WIRE3D_DMG_HEIGHT = 96. Draw a connected line into the 128x96 stage, including endpoints. During DrawScene, use the coarse five-sample occlusion rejection; otherwise draw directly. Supply viewport coordinates. VRAM is updated only by EndFrame.

This sample uses the 128x96 profile. Its viewport starts at screen (0,0). Reserve WRAM D000..DFFF and keep its bank mapping stable on CGB too. Shared state is not reentrant.

Usage example

c
#pragma bank 0
// Draw a frame with a gap, a projected diagonal, and a copied corner tile.
// The selected 96-line profile determines the stage layout and camera center.
#define WIRE3D_DMG_HEIGHT 96
#include "wire3d.h"
__location(0xC110) u16 result[8];
__location(0xFF47) u8 sample_bgp;
__location(0xFF40) u8 sample_lcdc;
__location(0xFF44) u8 sample_ly;
__location(0xFF4F) u8 sample_vbk;
__location(0xFF68) u8 sample_bgpi;
__location(0xFF69) u8 sample_bgpd;
u8 projected_x;
u8 projected_y;
void main() {
    u8 i;
    for(i=0;i<8;i++) result[i]=0;
    Wire3D_Init();
    // A CGB-compatible ROM also needs CGB palette and tile-map attributes.
    if(__cgb_is_cgb()) {
        while(sample_ly>=144) {} while(sample_ly<144) {}
        sample_lcdc=0; sample_vbk=1;
        __vram_memset_unsafe(0x9800,0,1024); sample_vbk=0;
        sample_bgpi=0x80; sample_bgpd=255; sample_bgpd=127;
        for(i=0;i<6;i++) sample_bgpd=0;
        sample_lcdc=0x81;
    }
    Wire3D_SetPalette(0xFC); // White background; every nonzero shade is black.
    result[0]=sample_bgp;
    Wire3D_SetCamera(8,0,0,0,0,0);
    result[1]=Wire3D_ProjectPoint(0,0,96,&projected_x,&projected_y);
    result[2]=projected_x; result[3]=projected_y;
    projected_x=91; projected_y=92;
    result[4]=Wire3D_ProjectPoint(0,0,7,&projected_x,&projected_y);
    result[5]=projected_x; result[6]=projected_y;
    Wire3D_SetCamera(0,0,0,0,0,0);
    Wire3D_BeginFrame();
    Wire3D_DrawLine2D(8,8,56,8);
    Wire3D_DrawLine2D(56,8,56,40);
    Wire3D_DrawLine2D(56,40,8,40);
    Wire3D_DrawLine2D(8,40,8,8);
    Wire3D_EraseSpan2D(8,40,24); // Inclusive endpoints are ordered internally.
    Wire3D_DrawLine3D(-24,-24,96,24,24,96);
    // Copy the viewport's top-left frame corner to a separate map cell.
    Wire3D_PutBgTile(18,1,157);
    Wire3D_EndFrame();
    result[7]=0xA55A;
    while(1) {}
}

c
void Wire3DDMG_DrawLine2D(w3ddmg_u8 ax, w3ddmg_u8 ay, w3ddmg_u8 bx, w3ddmg_u8 by)
{




    if (w3ddmg_occlusion_active)
    {
        w3ddmg_line_stage_masked_c(ax, ay, bx, by);
        return;
    }

    w3ddmg_line_x0 = ax;
    w3ddmg_line_y0 = ay;
    w3ddmg_line_x1 = bx;
    w3ddmg_line_y1 = by;
    if (ax < 128 && bx < 128 && ay < WIRE3D_DMG_SCREEN_H && by < WIRE3D_DMG_SCREEN_H)
        w3ddmg_line_inside_asm();
    else
        w3ddmg_line_stage_asm();
}

Wire3D_DrawModel

Draw a vertex-and-edge model at the requested position and rotation at unity scale.

Syntax

c
void Wire3D_DrawModel(const Wire3DDMG_Model* model, w3ddmg_i16 x, w3ddmg_i16 y, w3ddmg_i16 z, w3ddmg_i8 rx, w3ddmg_i8 ry, w3ddmg_i8 rz);

Parameters

model

Model holding vertex, edge and face arrays and counts; its tables must remain readable during the call.

x

World-space X component of the point or object origin.

y

World-space Y component of the point or object origin.

z

World-space Z component of the point or object origin.

rx

Rotation about X; sixteen steps make a full turn.

ry

Rotation about Y; sixteen steps make a full turn.

rz

Rotation about Z; sixteen steps make a full turn.

Return value

No return value; the state affected and display timing are described above.

Conditions and limits

WIRE3D_DMG_HEIGHT = 96. Draw an unscaled model by delegating to DrawModelScaled with scale 256.

This sample uses the 128x96 profile. Its viewport starts at screen (0,0). Reserve WRAM D000..DFFF and keep its bank mapping stable on CGB too. Shared state is not reentrant.

Usage example

c
#pragma bank 0
// Compare direct model scaling with an object-array scene.
// The selected 96-line profile determines the stage layout and camera center.
#define WIRE3D_DMG_HEIGHT 96
#include "wire3d.h"
__location(0xC110) u16 result[8];
__location(0xFF47) u8 sample_bgp;
__location(0xFF40) u8 sample_lcdc;
__location(0xFF44) u8 sample_ly;
__location(0xFF4F) u8 sample_vbk;
__location(0xFF68) u8 sample_bgpi;
__location(0xFF69) u8 sample_bgpd;
__prg_rom Wire3D_Vec3 vertices[8]={{-16,-16,-16},{16,-16,-16},{16,16,-16},{-16,16,-16},{-16,-16,16},{16,-16,16},{16,16,16},{-16,16,16}};
__prg_rom Wire3D_Edge edges[12]={{0,1},{1,2},{2,3},{3,0},{4,5},{5,6},{6,7},{7,4},{0,4},{1,5},{2,6},{3,7}};
Wire3D_Model cube;
Wire3D_Object objects[2];
u16 masks[2];
void main() {

    u8 i;
    for(i=0;i<8;i++) result[i]=0;
    Wire3D_Init();
    // A CGB-compatible ROM also needs CGB palette and tile-map attributes.
    if(__cgb_is_cgb()) {
        while(sample_ly>=144) {} while(sample_ly<144) {}
        sample_lcdc=0; sample_vbk=1;
        __vram_memset_unsafe(0x9800,0,1024); sample_vbk=0;
        sample_bgpi=0x80; sample_bgpd=255; sample_bgpd=127;
        for(i=0;i<6;i++) sample_bgpd=0;
        sample_lcdc=0x81;
    }
    Wire3D_SetPalette(0xFC); // White background; every nonzero shade is black.
    result[0]=sample_bgp;

    cube.vertices=vertices;cube.edges=edges;cube.faces=0;cube.edge_faces=0;
    cube.vertex_count=8;cube.edge_count=12;cube.face_count=0;cube.flags=0;
    cube.edge_masks=0; cube.edge_mask_count=0;
    Wire3D_BeginFrame();
    // Upper pair: direct model calls at unity and half scale.
    Wire3D_DrawModel(&cube,-32,32,96,0,0,0);
    Wire3D_DrawModelScaled(&cube,32,32,96,0,0,0,128);
    // Lower pair: the caller owns both object records and the model tables.
    for(i=0;i<2;i++) {
        objects[i].model=&cube;objects[i].x=-32+(s16)i*64;
        objects[i].y=-32;objects[i].z=96;
        objects[i].rx=0;objects[i].ry=0;objects[i].rz=0;
        objects[i].scale_q8=256-(s16)i*128;objects[i].visible=1;
    }
    Wire3D_DrawScene(objects,2);
    // Numeric checks cover the operation supplied by this viewport profile.
    masks[0]=3;masks[1]=12;cube.edge_masks=masks; cube.edge_mask_count=2;
    result[1]=Wire3D_SelectEdgeMask(&cube,0,0,0);
    result[2]=Wire3D_SelectEdgeMask(&cube,0,8,0);
    Wire3D_EndFrame(); result[7]=0xA55A;
    while(1) {}
}

Wire3D_DrawModelScaled

Scale a model, rotate it in Y/X/Z order, translate and project its vertices, then draw edges.

Syntax

c
void Wire3D_DrawModelScaled(const Wire3DDMG_Model* model, w3ddmg_i16 x, w3ddmg_i16 y, w3ddmg_i16 z, w3ddmg_i8 rx, w3ddmg_i8 ry, w3ddmg_i8 rz, w3ddmg_i16 scale_q8);

Parameters

model

Model holding vertex, edge and face arrays and counts; its tables must remain readable during the call.

x

World-space X component of the point or object origin.

y

World-space Y component of the point or object origin.

z

World-space Z component of the point or object origin.

rx

Rotation about X; sixteen steps make a full turn.

ry

Rotation about Y; sixteen steps make a full turn.

rz

Rotation about Z; sixteen steps make a full turn.

scale_q8

Scale with 256 as unity; nonpositive values also mean unity.

Return value

No return value; the state affected and display timing are described above.

Conditions and limits

WIRE3D_DMG_HEIGHT = 96. Scale, rotate in Y/X/Z order, translate and project at most 24 vertices; then draw up to 16 edges filtered by yaw masks and optional front-facing faces. Nonpositive scale becomes unity (256). Null model/vertex/edge pointers are ignored; referenced tables must remain readable. Keep scale products and translations in signed 16-bit range. Depth-crossing edges are dropped, not clipped.

This sample uses the 128x96 profile. Its viewport starts at screen (0,0). Reserve WRAM D000..DFFF and keep its bank mapping stable on CGB too. Shared state is not reentrant.

kitaqgb/lib/wire3d_dmg.c:2965

c
void Wire3DDMG_DrawModelScaled(const Wire3DDMG_Model* model, w3ddmg_i16 x, w3ddmg_i16 y, w3ddmg_i16 z, w3ddmg_i8 rx, w3ddmg_i8 ry, w3ddmg_i8 rz, w3ddmg_i16 scale_q8)








{
    w3ddmg_u8 i;
    w3ddmg_u8 count;
    w3ddmg_u8 edge_count;
    w3ddmg_u8 face_count;

    if (model == 0) return;
    if (model->vertices == 0) return;
    if (model->edges == 0) return;
    if (scale_q8 <= 0) scale_q8 = 256;

    count = model->vertex_count;
    if (count > WIRE3D_DMG_MODEL_VERTEX_LIMIT) count = WIRE3D_DMG_MODEL_VERTEX_LIMIT;

    i = 0;
    while (i < count)
    {
        const Wire3DDMG_Vec3* v;
        w3ddmg_i16 vx;
        w3ddmg_i16 vy;
        w3ddmg_i16 vz;
        w3ddmg_u8 sx;
        w3ddmg_u8 sy;

        v = &model->vertices[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)i];
        vx = (w3ddmg_i16)((v->x * scale_q8) >> 8);
        vy = (w3ddmg_i16)((v->y * scale_q8) >> 8);
        vz = (w3ddmg_i16)((v->z * scale_q8) >> 8);


        w3ddmg_rotate_y(&vx, &vz, (w3ddmg_i8)ry);

    face_count = model->face_count;
    if (face_count > WIRE3D_DMG_MODEL_FACE_LIMIT) face_count = WIRE3D_DMG_MODEL_FACE_LIMIT;

Wire3D_DrawScene

Draw up to eight objects near to far, using nearer faces to hide later edges.

Syntax

c
void Wire3D_DrawScene(Wire3DDMG_Object* objects, w3ddmg_u8 count);

Parameters

objects

Object array containing positions, rotations, scales and visibility flags.

count

Number of supplied array entries; see the operation-specific processing limit.

Return value

No return value; the state affected and display timing are described above.

Conditions and limits

WIRE3D_DMG_HEIGHT = 96. Process at most the first eight objects, sorted near to far by transformed origin depth. Draw visible valid models, then mark their front-face bounding rectangles to reject fully sampled later lines. This approximates inter-object occlusion, not a depth buffer. It clears its mask but retains existing staged pixels. Null arrays are ignored; objects and their data must remain readable.

This sample uses the 128x96 profile. Its viewport starts at screen (0,0). Reserve WRAM D000..DFFF and keep its bank mapping stable on CGB too. Shared state is not reentrant.

Usage example

c
#pragma bank 0
// Compare direct model scaling with an object-array scene.
// The selected 96-line profile determines the stage layout and camera center.
#define WIRE3D_DMG_HEIGHT 96
#include "wire3d.h"
__location(0xC110) u16 result[8];
__location(0xFF47) u8 sample_bgp;
__location(0xFF40) u8 sample_lcdc;
__location(0xFF44) u8 sample_ly;
__location(0xFF4F) u8 sample_vbk;
__location(0xFF68) u8 sample_bgpi;
__location(0xFF69) u8 sample_bgpd;
__prg_rom Wire3D_Vec3 vertices[8]={{-16,-16,-16},{16,-16,-16},{16,16,-16},{-16,16,-16},{-16,-16,16},{16,-16,16},{16,16,16},{-16,16,16}};
__prg_rom Wire3D_Edge edges[12]={{0,1},{1,2},{2,3},{3,0},{4,5},{5,6},{6,7},{7,4},{0,4},{1,5},{2,6},{3,7}};
Wire3D_Model cube;
Wire3D_Object objects[2];
u16 masks[2];
void main() {

    u8 i;
    for(i=0;i<8;i++) result[i]=0;
    Wire3D_Init();
    // A CGB-compatible ROM also needs CGB palette and tile-map attributes.
    if(__cgb_is_cgb()) {
        while(sample_ly>=144) {} while(sample_ly<144) {}
        sample_lcdc=0; sample_vbk=1;
        __vram_memset_unsafe(0x9800,0,1024); sample_vbk=0;
        sample_bgpi=0x80; sample_bgpd=255; sample_bgpd=127;
        for(i=0;i<6;i++) sample_bgpd=0;
        sample_lcdc=0x81;
    }
    Wire3D_SetPalette(0xFC); // White background; every nonzero shade is black.
    result[0]=sample_bgp;

    cube.vertices=vertices;cube.edges=edges;cube.faces=0;cube.edge_faces=0;
    cube.vertex_count=8;cube.edge_count=12;cube.face_count=0;cube.flags=0;
    cube.edge_masks=0; cube.edge_mask_count=0;
    Wire3D_BeginFrame();
    // Upper pair: direct model calls at unity and half scale.
    Wire3D_DrawModel(&cube,-32,32,96,0,0,0);
    Wire3D_DrawModelScaled(&cube,32,32,96,0,0,0,128);
    // Lower pair: the caller owns both object records and the model tables.
    for(i=0;i<2;i++) {
        objects[i].model=&cube;objects[i].x=-32+(s16)i*64;
        objects[i].y=-32;objects[i].z=96;
        objects[i].rx=0;objects[i].ry=0;objects[i].rz=0;
        objects[i].scale_q8=256-(s16)i*128;objects[i].visible=1;
    }
    Wire3D_DrawScene(objects,2);
    // Numeric checks cover the operation supplied by this viewport profile.
    masks[0]=3;masks[1]=12;cube.edge_masks=masks; cube.edge_mask_count=2;
    result[1]=Wire3D_SelectEdgeMask(&cube,0,0,0);
    result[2]=Wire3D_SelectEdgeMask(&cube,0,8,0);
    Wire3D_EndFrame(); result[7]=0xA55A;
    while(1) {}
}

Expected result

Unity and half-scale models appear above an object-array scene at the same scales, demonstrating projection and scaling.

void Wire3DDMG_DrawScene(Wire3DDMG_Object* objects, w3ddmg_u8 count)

    {

        j = (w3ddmg_u8)(i + 1);

            oi = w3ddmg_scene_order[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)i];
            oj = w3ddmg_scene_order[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)j];

            // The array itself stays in caller order; only the scratch index list is sorted.

            if (w3ddmg_scene_depth[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)oj] < w3ddmg_scene_depth[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)oi])
            {

                w3ddmg_scene_order[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)j] = oi;
            }

        }
        i = (w3ddmg_u8)(i + 1);
    }

    w3ddmg_clear_occlusion_mask();

    w3ddmg_occlusion_active = 1;




    i = 0;
    while (i < scene_count)
    {

        obj = &objects[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)w3ddmg_scene_order[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)i]];
        if ((obj->visible != 0) && (obj->model != 0))

Wire3D_EndFrame

Submit pending background writes and staged drawing to VRAM.

Syntax

c
void Wire3D_EndFrame();

Return value

No return value; the state affected and display timing are described above.

Conditions and limits

WIRE3D_DMG_HEIGHT = 96. Wait for the next VBlank, flush pending BG map writes, then copy the stage to VRAM while polling access windows. Copying consumes the staged pixels. The transfer may extend beyond VBlank; this is not an atomic frame swap.

This sample uses the 128x96 profile. Its viewport starts at screen (0,0). Reserve WRAM D000..DFFF and keep its bank mapping stable on CGB too. Shared state is not reentrant.

Usage example

c
#pragma bank 0
// Draw a frame with a gap, a projected diagonal, and a copied corner tile.
// The selected 96-line profile determines the stage layout and camera center.
#define WIRE3D_DMG_HEIGHT 96
#include "wire3d.h"
__location(0xC110) u16 result[8];
__location(0xFF47) u8 sample_bgp;
__location(0xFF40) u8 sample_lcdc;
__location(0xFF44) u8 sample_ly;
__location(0xFF4F) u8 sample_vbk;
__location(0xFF68) u8 sample_bgpi;
__location(0xFF69) u8 sample_bgpd;
u8 projected_x;
u8 projected_y;
void main() {
    u8 i;
    for(i=0;i<8;i++) result[i]=0;
    Wire3D_Init();
    // A CGB-compatible ROM also needs CGB palette and tile-map attributes.
    if(__cgb_is_cgb()) {
        while(sample_ly>=144) {} while(sample_ly<144) {}
        sample_lcdc=0; sample_vbk=1;
        __vram_memset_unsafe(0x9800,0,1024); sample_vbk=0;
        sample_bgpi=0x80; sample_bgpd=255; sample_bgpd=127;
        for(i=0;i<6;i++) sample_bgpd=0;
        sample_lcdc=0x81;
    }
    Wire3D_SetPalette(0xFC); // White background; every nonzero shade is black.
    result[0]=sample_bgp;
    Wire3D_SetCamera(8,0,0,0,0,0);
    result[1]=Wire3D_ProjectPoint(0,0,96,&projected_x,&projected_y);
    result[2]=projected_x; result[3]=projected_y;
    projected_x=91; projected_y=92;
    result[4]=Wire3D_ProjectPoint(0,0,7,&projected_x,&projected_y);
    result[5]=projected_x; result[6]=projected_y;
    Wire3D_SetCamera(0,0,0,0,0,0);
    Wire3D_BeginFrame();
    Wire3D_DrawLine2D(8,8,56,8);
    Wire3D_DrawLine2D(56,8,56,40);
    Wire3D_DrawLine2D(56,40,8,40);
    Wire3D_DrawLine2D(8,40,8,8);
    Wire3D_EraseSpan2D(8,40,24); // Inclusive endpoints are ordered internally.
    Wire3D_DrawLine3D(-24,-24,96,24,24,96);
    // Copy the viewport's top-left frame corner to a separate map cell.
    Wire3D_PutBgTile(18,1,157);
    Wire3D_EndFrame();
    result[7]=0xA55A;
    while(1) {}
}

Expected result

This sample demonstrates basic lines, points, erasure and projection in one frame. The middle of the upper-left frame’s top edge is erased and a diagonal is projected near the center. Rejected projection preserves outputs 91 and 92.

Project front-facing model triangles and erase staged pixels inside them.

Syntax

c
void Wire3D_EraseModelFaces(const Wire3DDMG_Model* model, w3ddmg_i16 x, w3ddmg_i16 y, w3ddmg_i16 z, w3ddmg_i8 rx, w3ddmg_i8 ry, w3ddmg_i8 rz, w3ddmg_i16 scale_q8);

Parameters

model

Model holding vertex, edge and face arrays and counts; its tables must remain readable during the call.

x

World-space X component of the point or object origin.

y

World-space Y component of the point or object origin.

z

World-space Z component of the point or object origin.

rx

Rotation about X; sixteen steps make a full turn.

ry

Rotation about Y; sixteen steps make a full turn.

rz

Rotation about Z; sixteen steps make a full turn.

scale_q8

Scale with 256 as unity; nonpositive values also mean unity.

Return value

No return value; the state affected and display timing are described above.

Conditions and limits

WIRE3D_DMG_HEIGHT = 96. Project up to 24 vertices and erase front-facing triangle interiors from the stage for a model with hidden-line flags and face data. Nonpositive scale means 256 (unity). Up to 16 faces are considered; depth-crossing faces are skipped. This also replaces shared projection caches, but does not update VRAM.

This sample uses the 128x96 profile. Its viewport starts at screen (0,0). Reserve WRAM D000..DFFF and keep its bank mapping stable on CGB too. Shared state is not reentrant.

Usage example

#pragma bank 0
// Erase a screen triangle and a projected model face from separate filled panels.
// The selected 96-line profile determines the stage layout and camera center.
#define WIRE3D_DMG_HEIGHT 96
#include "wire3d.h"
__location(0xC110) u16 result[8];
__location(0xFF47) u8 sample_bgp;
__location(0xFF40) u8 sample_lcdc;
__location(0xFF44) u8 sample_ly;
__location(0xFF4F) u8 sample_vbk;
__location(0xFF68) u8 sample_bgpi;
__location(0xFF69) u8 sample_bgpd;
__prg_rom Wire3D_Vec3 vertices[4]={{-24,-24,0},{24,-24,0},{24,24,0},{-24,24,0}};
__prg_rom Wire3D_Edge edges[4]={{0,1},{1,2},{2,3},{3,0}};
__prg_rom Wire3D_Face faces[2]={{0,2,1},{0,3,2}};
Wire3D_Model plane;

void main() {

    u8 i;
    for(i=0;i<8;i++) result[i]=0;
    Wire3D_Init();
    // A CGB-compatible ROM also needs CGB palette and tile-map attributes.
    if(__cgb_is_cgb()) {
        while(sample_ly>=144) {} while(sample_ly<144) {}
        sample_lcdc=0; sample_vbk=1;
        __vram_memset_unsafe(0x9800,0,1024); sample_vbk=0;
        sample_bgpi=0x80; sample_bgpd=255; sample_bgpd=127;
        for(i=0;i<6;i++) sample_bgpd=0;
        sample_lcdc=0x81;
    }
    Wire3D_SetPalette(0xFC); // White background; every nonzero shade is black.
    result[0]=sample_bgp;
        plane.vertices=vertices;plane.edges=edges;plane.faces=faces;plane.edge_faces=0;
    plane.vertex_count=4;plane.edge_count=4;plane.face_count=2;plane.flags=1;plane.edge_masks=0;plane.edge_mask_count=0;
    Wire3D_BeginFrame();
    // Separate panels show a direct screen triangle and a projected square face.
    for(i=8;i<=32;i++) Wire3D_DrawLine2D(8,i,32,i);
    for(i=24;i<=72;i++) Wire3D_DrawLine2D(40,i,88,i);

    Wire3D_EraseModelFaces(&plane,0,0,64,0,0,0,256);

    Wire3D_EndFrame(); result[7]=0xA55A; while(1) {}

            w3ddmg_screen_y[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)i] = sy;
            w3ddmg_screen_visible[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)i] = 1;
        }
        else
        {
            w3ddmg_screen_visible[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)i] = 0;
        }
        i = (w3ddmg_u8)(i + 1);
    }

    face_count = model->face_count;
    if (face_count > WIRE3D_DMG_MODEL_FACE_LIMIT) face_count = WIRE3D_DMG_MODEL_FACE_LIMIT;
    w3ddmg_build_face_visibility(model, count, face_count);

    i = 0;
    while (i < face_count)
    {
        const Wire3DDMG_Face* f;
        f = &model->faces[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)i];
        if (w3ddmg_face_visible[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)i] &&
            w3ddmg_screen_visible[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)f->a] &&
            w3ddmg_screen_visible[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)f->b] &&
            w3ddmg_screen_visible[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)f->c])

                w3ddmg_screen_x[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)f->c],
                w3ddmg_screen_y[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)f->c]);
        }
        i = (w3ddmg_u8)(i + 1);
    }
}

void Wire3DDMG_EraseSpan2D(w3ddmg_u8 y, w3ddmg_u8 x0, w3ddmg_u8 x1)

__location(0xFF4F) u8 sample_vbk;
__location(0xFF68) u8 sample_bgpi;
__location(0xFF69) u8 sample_bgpd;
__prg_rom Wire3D_Vec3 vertices[4]={{-24,-24,0},{24,-24,0},{24,24,0},{-24,24,0}};
__prg_rom Wire3D_Edge edges[4]={{0,1},{1,2},{2,3},{3,0}};
__prg_rom Wire3D_Face faces[2]={{0,2,1},{0,3,2}};

    for(i=0;i<8;i++) result[i]=0;
    Wire3D_Init();

        __vram_memset_unsafe(0x9800,0,1024); sample_vbk=0;

        for(i=0;i<6;i++) sample_bgpd=0;
        sample_lcdc=0x81;
    }
    Wire3D_SetPalette(0xFC); // White background; every nonzero shade is black.
    result[0]=sample_bgp;
        plane.vertices=vertices;plane.edges=edges;plane.faces=faces;plane.edge_faces=0;
    plane.vertex_count=4;plane.edge_count=4;plane.face_count=2;plane.flags=1;plane.edge_masks=0;plane.edge_mask_count=0;
    Wire3D_BeginFrame();

c
void Wire3DDMG_Init()
{
    w3ddmg_u8 row;
    w3ddmg_u8 col;
    w3ddmg_u8 tid;
    w3ddmg_u16 off;

    w3ddmg_wait_vblank_start();
    w3ddmg_reg_lcdc = 0;

    w3ddmg_clear_vram_asm();

    w3ddmg_load_hud_tiles();

    w3ddmg_fill_bg_map_asm();

    row = 0;
    tid = 0x90;
    while (row < WIRE3D_DMG_TILE_H)
    {

        off = (w3ddmg_u16)((w3ddmg_u16)row << 5);



        col = 0;
        while (col < WIRE3D_DMG_TILE_W)
        {
            w3ddmg_bg_map_9800[(w3ddmg_u16)(off + (w3ddmg_u16)col)] = tid;
            tid = (w3ddmg_u8)(tid + WIRE3D_DMG_TILE_H);
            col = (w3ddmg_u8)(col + 1);
        }
        row = (w3ddmg_u8)(row + 1);
        tid = (w3ddmg_u8)(0x90 + row);
    }


    w3ddmg_reg_scx = 0;



    w3ddmg_reg_scy = 0;
    w3ddmg_reg_bgp = 0xB4;
    w3ddmg_reg_lcdc = 0x81;
    w3ddmg_bgq_count = 0;





    Wire3DDMG_SetCamera(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0);
    w3ddmg_clear_stage_asm();




}

c
void Wire3DDMG_PutBgTile(w3ddmg_u8 x, w3ddmg_u8 y, w3ddmg_u8 tile)
{
    if (x >= 32) return;
    if (y >= 32) return;
    if (w3ddmg_bgq_count >= WIRE3D_DMG_BG_QUEUE_LIMIT) return;
    w3ddmg_bgq_x[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)w3ddmg_bgq_count] = x;
    w3ddmg_bgq_y[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)w3ddmg_bgq_count] = y;
    w3ddmg_bgq_tile[(__safe_index w3ddmg_u8)w3ddmg_bgq_count] = tile;
    w3ddmg_bgq_count = (w3ddmg_u8)(w3ddmg_bgq_count + 1);
}
Wire3D_SelectEdgeMask

Select a precomputed edge-visibility mask for the object yaw.

Syntax

c
w3ddmg_u16 Wire3D_SelectEdgeMask(const Wire3DDMG_Model* model, w3ddmg_i8 rx, w3ddmg_i8 ry, w3ddmg_i8 rz);

Parameters

model

Model holding vertex, edge and face arrays and counts; its tables must remain readable during the call.

rx

Rotation about X; sixteen steps make a full turn.

ry

Rotation about Y; sixteen steps make a full turn.

rz

Rotation about Z; sixteen steps make a full turn.

Return value

A 16-bit edge visibility mask, or 0xFFFF when no table is supplied.

Conditions and limits

WIRE3D_DMG_HEIGHT = 96. Select a precomputed mask from the low four bits of object yaw; pitch, roll and camera orientation are ignored. Use 16, 8, 4 or 2 bins; other positive counts select entry zero (counts >=16 use the first 16). Missing data returns 0xFFFF. Keep the mask table readable through the current data-pointer mapping.

This sample uses the 128x96 profile. Its viewport starts at screen (0,0). Reserve WRAM D000..DFFF and keep its bank mapping stable on CGB too. Shared state is not reentrant.

Usage example

#include "wire3d.h"

__location(0xFF40) u8 sample_lcdc;
__location(0xFF44) u8 sample_ly;
__location(0xFF4F) u8 sample_vbk;
__location(0xFF68) u8 sample_bgpi;
__location(0xFF69) u8 sample_bgpd;
__prg_rom Wire3D_Vec3 vertices[8]={{-16,-16,-16},{16,-16,-16},{16,16,-16},{-16,16,-16},{-16,-16,16},{16,-16,16},{16,16,16},{-16,16,16}};
__prg_rom Wire3D_Edge edges[12]={{0,1},{1,2},{2,3},{3,0},{4,5},{5,6},{6,7},{7,4},{0,4},{1,5},{2,6},{3,7}};
Wire3D_Model cube;
Wire3D_Object objects[2];
u16 masks[2];
void main() {

    u8 i;
    for(i=0;i<8;i++) result[i]=0;
    Wire3D_Init();
    // A CGB-compatible ROM also needs CGB palette and tile-map attributes.
    if(__cgb_is_cgb()) {
        while(sample_ly>=144) {} while(sample_ly<144) {}
        sample_lcdc=0; sample_vbk=1;
        __vram_memset_unsafe(0x9800,0,1024); sample_vbk=0;
        sample_bgpi=0x80; sample_bgpd=255; sample_bgpd=127;
        for(i=0;i<6;i++) sample_bgpd=0;
        sample_lcdc=0x81;
    }
    Wire3D_SetPalette(0xFC); // White background; every nonzero shade is black.
    result[0]=sample_bgp;

    cube.vertices=vertices;cube.edges=edges;cube.faces=0;cube.edge_faces=0;
    cube.vertex_count=8;cube.edge_count=12;cube.face_count=0;cube.flags=0;
    cube.edge_masks=0; cube.edge_mask_count=0;
    Wire3D_BeginFrame();
    // Upper pair: direct model calls at unity and half scale.
    Wire3D_DrawModel(&cube,-32,32,96,0,0,0);
    Wire3D_DrawModelScaled(&cube,32,32,96,0,0,0,128);
    // Lower pair: the caller owns both object records and the model tables.
    for(i=0;i<2;i++) {
        objects[i].model=&cube;objects[i].x=-32+(s16)i*64;
        objects[i].y=-32;objects[i].z=96;
        objects[i].rx=0;objects[i].ry=0;objects[i].rz=0;
        objects[i].scale_q8=256-(s16)i*128;objects[i].visible=1;
    }
    Wire3D_DrawScene(objects,2);
    // Numeric checks cover the operation supplied by this viewport profile.
    masks[0]=3;masks[1]=12;cube.edge_masks=masks; cube.edge_mask_count=2;
    result[1]=Wire3D_SelectEdgeMask(&cube,0,0,0);
    result[2]=Wire3D_SelectEdgeMask(&cube,0,8,0);
    Wire3D_EndFrame(); result[7]=0xA55A;
    while(1) {}
}
